nodes.name: mmu.h
nodes.summary: MMU subsystem public header. Declares mmu_init, mmu_map, mmu_duplicate_pagetable, mmu_free_usermemory, data_abort_handler, TLB invalidation, mmu_map_kernel prototypes.

nodes.name: pci.h
nodes.summary: Header defining PCI device descriptor struct and declaring the pci_init, pci_scan_bus, and driver registration function prototypes.

nodes.name: pipe.c
nodes.summary: UNIX pipe stub. pipe_buffer_t with 4096-byte ring buffer, spinlock, waiter task pointers. All operations stub returning ENOSYS.

nodes.name: pipe
nodes.summary: Creates a pipe by allocating a pipe buffer and registering read/write file descriptors in the current task's file table.

nodes.name: pipe_read
nodes.summary: Reads data from the pipe's circular buffer into the caller's buffer, blocking if no data is available.

nodes.name: pipe_write
nodes.summary: Writes data into the pipe's circular buffer, blocking if the buffer is full.

nodes.name: pipe_poll
nodes.summary: Returns poll event flags indicating whether the pipe has data ready to read or space to write.

nodes.name: pipe_close
nodes.summary: Closes a pipe file descriptor and frees the backing buffer when both ends are closed.

nodes.name: pipe.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the pipe creation and pipe file operation function prototypes.

nodes.name: select.c
nodes.summary: Kernel implementations of POSIX select() and poll() that iterate open file descriptors and invoke per-file poll callbacks to test readiness.

nodes.name: signal.c
nodes.summary: POSIX-style signal subsystem: supports signal(), sigaction(), kill() with per-task signal bitmask, deliver_signals() called at schedule time, and handle_exception() for AArch64 fault-to-signal translation.

nodes.name: sigaction
nodes.summary: Installs or queries a signal action for the current task, copying old handler to oldact and setting new handler with mask and flags.

nodes.name: kill
nodes.summary: Delivers a signal to a target task by PID, setting the signal bit in the task's pending mask and waking it if blocked.

nodes.name: deliver_signals
nodes.summary: Checks the current task's pending signal bitmask and calls the registered handler or default action for each set signal.

nodes.name: sigreturn
nodes.summary: Restores the saved register context after a user signal handler returns.

nodes.name: handle_exception
nodes.summary: Translates an AArch64 exception (ESR/FAR) into a SIGSEGV or SIGBUS and calls deliver_signals, or halts the system for unrecoverable faults.

nodes.name: register_default_handlers
nodes.summary: Installs default signal handlers for SIGTERM, SIGKILL, and other signals at task creation.

nodes.name: spinlock.c
nodes.summary: AArch64 spinlock implementation using LDXR/STXR exclusive monitor instructions, with IRQ-save/restore variants for use in interrupt-context-safe critical sections.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AArch64 exclusive monitor (LDXR/STXR) with DMB barriers rather than a simple swap, ensuring correct acquire/release semantics on multi-core systems.

nodes.name: spinlock_init
nodes.summary: Initialises a spinlock to the unlocked state.

nodes.name: spin_lock_irqsave
nodes.summary: Saves and disables IRQs via DAIF then acquires the spinlock with exclusive load/store retry, ensuring IRQ-safe critical sections.

nodes.name: spin_unlock_irqrestore
nodes.summary: Releases a spinlock and restores the saved interrupt flags.

nodes.name: spin_lock
nodes.summary: Acquires the spinlock without saving IRQ state, spinning on LDAXR/STXR until the lock word transitions from 0 to 1.

nodes.name: spin_unlock
nodes.summary: Releases a spinlock acquired with spin_lock.

nodes.name: spinlock.h
nodes.summary: Header defining the spinlock_t type and declaring all spinlock primitive prototypes.

nodes.name: task.c
nodes.summary: POSIX-style process management implementing fork() (clone current task with duplicated page tables), execve() (load ELF binary into user address space), and wait/waitpid for child termination.

nodes.name: fork
nodes.summary: Creates a child task by allocating a new TCB, duplicating the parent's page tables and kernel stack, and enqueuing the child on the current CPU's run queue.

nodes.name: execve
nodes.summary: Loads an ELF binary from VFS into the current task's user address space, sets up program segments via mmu_map, and prepares argv/envp on the user stack before returning to EL0.

nodes.name: usb_storage.c
nodes.summary: USB mass-storage class driver stub: registers a block-device interface over xHCI bulk transfers, translating read/write requests into SCSI CBW/CSW sequences.

nodes.name: vfs.c
nodes.summary: Virtual filesystem layer: provides a uniform read/write/seek/poll/close interface over registered filesystem drivers, implements filesystem mounting, and registers the Filecore (ADFS/FAT32) filesystem driver.

nodes.name: fc_vfs_read
nodes.summary: Filecore-backed VFS read callback: calls filecore_read_file to transfer file data from disc into the caller's buffer, managing intermediate kernel allocations.

nodes.name: fc_vfs_seek
nodes.summary: VFS seek adapter for FileCore files, adjusting the file position with SEEK_SET/CUR/END semantics.

nodes.name: vfs_close
nodes.summary: Dispatches close to the file's ops->close handler.

nodes.name: vfs_read
nodes.summary: Dispatches a read request to the file's ops->read handler.

nodes.name: vfs_write
nodes.summary: Dispatches a write request to the file's ops->write handler.

nodes.name: vfs_seek
nodes.summary: Dispatches a seek request to the file's ops->seek handler.

nodes.name: vfs_poll
nodes.summary: Dispatches a poll query to the file's ops->poll handler.

nodes.name: vfs_register_filesystem
nodes.summary: Registers a filesystem driver by name in the global filesystem table.

nodes.name: vfs_mount
nodes.summary: Mounts a named filesystem at a mount-point by finding the registered driver and calling its mount callback, logging success or failure.

nodes.name: filecore_vfs_readdir
nodes.summary: VFS readdir adapter that walks FileCore directory entries, bridging the FileCore API to the VFS dirent interface.

nodes.name: filecore_vfs_mount
nodes.summary: Filecore VFS mount callback: calls filecore_init to discover and parse the disc record, then filecore_list_root to populate the root directory.

nodes.name: vfs_register_filecore
nodes.summary: Registers the Filecore filesystem driver with the VFS layer and immediately mounts it at the root, making ADFS/FAT32 volumes accessible.

nodes.name: vl805_init.c
nodes.summary: Initialises the VL805 USB 3.0 controller firmware via VideoCore mailbox: sends a notify-xHCI property message to the GPU, which loads VL805 firmware and enables the USB hub.

nodes.name: mbox_read
nodes.summary: Reads a response from the VideoCore mailbox by polling the status register until data is available on the requested channel.

nodes.name: mbox_property
nodes.summary: Sends a single VideoCore mailbox property buffer and blocks until the GPU acknowledges, returning the response payload.

nodes.name: vl805_init
nodes.summary: Sends the NOTIFY_XHCI_RESET mailbox property message to the VideoCore, triggering VL805 USB controller firmware load; logs mailbox base and response status.

nodes.name: vl805_mailbox_test.c
nodes.summary: Test harness for VideoCore mailbox interactions: queries firmware revision, sends the NOTIFY_XHCI_RESET message, and probes USB power/enable tags to validate mailbox communication with the GPU.

nodes.name: mbox_test_tag
nodes.summary: Generic helper that builds a single-tag mailbox request, calls mbox_call, and prints request and response buffers for diagnostic purposes.

nodes.name: mbox_get_fw_rev
nodes.summary: Queries the VideoCore firmware revision via a mailbox property call and logs the result.

nodes.name: mbox_test_notify_xhci
nodes.summary: Constructs and sends the NOTIFY_XHCI_RESET mailbox property message, logging the GPU's response and confirming the VL805 notification succeeded.

nodes.name: mbox_test_usb_tags
nodes.summary: Sends USB power state query tags via the mailbox and logs the power status results.

nodes.name: vl805_mailbox_test
nodes.summary: Top-level test entry point: prints mailbox base address, queries GPU firmware revision, sends NOTIFY_XHCI_RESET, and tests USB-related mailbox tags.

nodes.name: dhcp_test_module.c
nodes.summary: DHCP client test module that exercises the DHCP state machine by injecting synthetic OFFER and ACK packets, verifying correct state transitions and IP assignment.

nodes.name: dhcp_test_module_init
nodes.summary: Module init function that runs a full DHCP exchange sequence, injecting crafted OFFER and ACK buffers and asserting bound/unbound state at each step.

nodes.name: blockdev.h
nodes.summary: Earlier block device header defining a simple blockdev_t struct with per-device read/write function pointers, plus register/unregister/find API declarations; superseded by blockdriver.h with richer media classification.

nodes.name: dl.c
nodes.summary: Implements a minimal dynamic-linker shim for the Phoenix kernel, providing symbol resolution against a built-in table and a dlclose stub.
nodes.languageNotes: Symbol resolution is done via a linear strcmp scan of a compiled-in symbol table rather than ELF relocations at runtime.

nodes.name: dlopen
nodes.summary: Opens an ELF64 shared object via VFS, validates its magic and type, parses PT_DYNAMIC, and registers it in the loaded-library table.

nodes.name: dlsym
nodes.summary: Walks the symbol table of a loaded library to find a named symbol and return its value as a function pointer.

nodes.name: elf64.h
nodes.summary: Defines ELF-64 data structures (Elf64_Ehdr, Elf64_Phdr, Elf64_Shdr, Elf64_Sym, Elf64_Rela, etc.) and associated constants used by the kernel's module loader.

nodes.name: errno.c
nodes.summary: Provides the kernel's POSIX-style errno string table and any errno utility functions for translating error codes to messages.

nodes.name: strerror
nodes.summary: Looks up an error number in the static message table and returns the corresponding POSIX error string, or 'Unknown error' for out-of-range values.

nodes.name: errno.h
nodes.summary: Declares POSIX errno constants and the kernel errno variable for use across kernel subsystems.

nodes.name: error.h
nodes.summary: Defines Phoenix OS error types, error block structures, and macros for error propagation compatible with the RISC OS error-handling convention.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors the RISC OS error block structure (error number + message string) for OS SWI error returns.

nodes.name: irq.h
nodes.summary: IRQ subsystem public header. Defines IRQ vector constants, irq_handler_t, irq_init/set_handler/unmask/eoi prototypes, IPI constants, xhci_irq_pending() inline helper.

nodes.name: kernel_malloc.c
nodes.summary: Implements the kernel heap allocator (kmalloc/kfree) wrapping a simple buddy or slab allocator, with a heap_stats diagnostic function.

nodes.name: kmalloc
nodes.summary: Bump-pointer allocator: advances heap_used by the 16-byte-aligned request size and returns the pre-advance pointer, or NULL on exhaustion.

nodes.name: mmio.c
nodes.summary: Memory-mapped I/O access primitives (readb/readl/readq, writeb/writel/writeq) plus virtual-to-physical and GPU bus address translation helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses volatile pointer casts rather than inline assembly for MMIO to let GCC emit correct load/store barrier semantics on AArch64.

nodes.name: gpu_bus_addr
nodes.summary: Converts a virtual address to a GPU/VC bus address by adding the VideoCore DMA offset used by the Raspberry Pi mailbox interface.

nodes.name: genet.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the BCM2711 GENETv5 Ethernet hardware driver, declaring the polling-mode TX/RX API, diagnostic counter accessors, and the exported MAC address variable.

nodes.name: genet_module.h
nodes.summary: Header defining the PhoenixGENET DCI4 module public API, all DCI4 constants and SWI offsets, and the key data structures (DIB, filter, stats buffer) needed for RISC OS DCI4 compliance.
nodes.languageNotes: Documents the full DCI4 stack: Internet module → DCIShim → PhoenixGENET → BCM2711 hardware.

nodes.name: ethernet.h
nodes.summary: Ethernet header constants (ETH_HDR_LEN, ETH_MTU, EtherType values) and the eth_hdr_t struct, plus big-endian byte-swap helper declarations.

nodes.name: resolver_module.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the PhoenixResolver SWI chunk constants, the BSD-compatible hostent_t struct, and the public API for resolver_module_init, resolver_module_final, resolver_module_swi, and resolver_gethostbyname.

nodes.name: tcp.c
nodes.summary: Implements PhoenixTCP: a minimal RFC 793 client-side TCP state machine with four static connection slots, SYN/ACK/FIN handling, per-connection 4 KB receive ring buffers, and TCP checksum computation.
nodes.languageNotes: No heap allocation; all TCBs are static. No retransmit timer (suitable for LAN); SYN retransmit driven by tcp_tick() calls from the WIMP loop.

nodes.name: tcp_connect
nodes.summary: Initiates an active TCP open by allocating a TCB slot, assigning an ephemeral local port and ISN, and transmitting the initial SYN segment.

nodes.name: tcp_rx
nodes.summary: Processes incoming TCP segments: matches by local port, handles RST unconditionally, and drives the FSM through SYN_SENT, ESTABLISHED, FIN_WAIT, TIME_WAIT, and CLOSED states.

nodes.name: tcp_write
nodes.summary: Sends data on an established TCP connection; caps at MSS 1460 per call and advances snd_nxt.

nodes.name: tcp_read
nodes.summary: Non-blocking read from the connection receive ring buffer; returns bytes copied or 0 if none available.

nodes.name: uart.h
nodes.summary: Minimal UART driver header declaring the five public I/O functions used throughout the kernel for serial diagnostics and boot output.

nodes.name: blockdriver.c
nodes.summary: Block device driver framework implementation providing registration, lookup, LBA read/write/trim/poll/close dispatch through an ops table, and a diagnostic blockdev_print_all function that lists all registered storage devices with type, size, and FileCore scoring.

nodes.name: blockdev_register
nodes.summary: Allocates and registers a new block device descriptor under a spinlock, assigning the next available unit number and adding it to the global device table.

nodes.name: blockdev_get
nodes.summary: Looks up a registered block device by name and optional unit number under a spinlock, returning a pointer to its descriptor or NULL.

nodes.name: blockdev_print_all
nodes.summary: Iterates all registered block devices and prints their name, unit, media class, block size, total size in MB, and computed FileCore disc-scoring value to the debug console.

nodes.name: blockdriver.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the Phoenix block device framework, defining blockdev_t, blockdev_ops_t, the media_class_t enum (UNKNOWN/SD/USB_FLASH/SSD/NVME), and declarations for register/get/print_all and the global device list.

nodes.name: Bits64.c
nodes.summary: Phoenix stub replacing the RISC OS disc reader 64-bit arithmetic helpers with integer-only implementations; provides Zero64, Inc64, Dec64, Cmp64, Add64, Add64_32, Sub64, Sub64_32, and integer-formatted display helpers (Print64, Size32, Size64, Percent64) that avoid floating-point instructions.
nodes.languageNotes: Floating-point is banned by -mgeneral-regs-only in the kernel build; Size64 simply delegates to Size32 since the disc reader only deals with 32-bit-capped sizes in practice.

nodes.name: Bits64.h
nodes.summary: Header providing inline macros and helpers for 64-bit arithmetic on 32-bit word pairs, used throughout the disc reader subsystem for 64-bit address and size manipulation.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements 64-bit operations (INC64, DEC64, ZERO64, ADDR64SEC, etc.) using struct pairs, working around bare-metal AArch64 C toolchain limitations.

nodes.name: dr_types.h
nodes.summary: Defines core types, character classification helpers, and the safe_exit utility for the disc reader subsystem.

nodes.name: dr_realloc
nodes.summary: Bare-metal realloc shim that kmalloc-allocates a new buffer, copies at most 2048 bytes from the old buffer, and kfree-s it; used exclusively by LoadDirectory when growing big-directory buffers.

nodes.name: BootRecord.c
nodes.summary: Reads and writes the ADFS/FileCore disc boot block, parses the on-disc disc record structure, validates checksums, and reads defect lists.

nodes.name: ReadBootBlock
nodes.summary: Reads the disc boot block from the storage device, parses the disc record and defect lists, and initialises global disc geometry state.

nodes.name: GetDiscRecord
nodes.summary: Extracts and decodes the disc record fields from a raw boot block buffer into a structured disc record.

nodes.name: DisplayRecord
nodes.summary: Formats and prints all fields of a disc record to the debug output for diagnostic purposes.

nodes.name: CalcMapLocation
nodes.summary: Calculates the LBA address of the disc map from disc record parameters.

nodes.name: DiscReader.c
nodes.summary: Minimal glue file for the disc reader subsystem containing the ExtractObject helper that copies an object from a sector buffer.

nodes.name: Map.c
nodes.summary: Implements the ADFS new-map parser: reads, decodes, and writes the bit-map zones that track disc allocation, providing ID resolution, free space tracking, and map address arithmetic.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the FileCore new-map format with per-zone cross-zone IDs, bit-level address arithmetic, and zone checksum validation.

nodes.name: ReadMap
nodes.summary: Reads all map zones from disc, allocates zone arrays, and invokes the map record and contents parsers.

nodes.name: ReadMapContents
nodes.summary: Iterates all bit entries in the map zones to classify fragments as free or assigned to object IDs.

nodes.name: AddID
nodes.summary: Registers a disc fragment ID in the in-memory object list, creating a new entry or extending an existing fragmented object's chain.

nodes.name: MakeID
nodes.summary: Allocates a new disc object ID from the free map, setting the appropriate map bits across zones.

nodes.name: MapAddr
nodes.summary: Converts a zone/bit-offset pair to an LBA disc address.

nodes.name: MapZoneCheck
nodes.summary: Verifies the checksum and consistency of a single map zone.

nodes.name: BigFile.c
nodes.summary: Implements platform-portable big-file I/O (open, close, read, write) using 64-bit addressing, bridging RISC OS OSLib SWIs and POSIX/Win32 file APIs for accessing raw disc images larger than 2 GB.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses conditional compilation for __riscos, _WIN32, and POSIX targets; 64-bit seek via _fseeki64 on Windows and off_t on POSIX.

nodes.name: BigFile.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the BigFile API (open, close, read, write) for 64-bit addressed large disc image files.

nodes.name: BootRecord.c
nodes.summary: Reads, parses, and displays the FileCore boot block and disc record (LBA0), including defect lists, CRC computation, and map location calculation for E and E+ format RISC OS discs.

nodes.name: DirUtils.c
nodes.summary: Comprehensive directory manipulation library supporting both old (Hugo/Nick) and new (BigDir) FileCore directory formats, including load, create, add/remove/find entries, sort, checksum, and RISC OS filename collation.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains a full 256-entry static collation table implementing RISC OS filename ordering rules that differ from standard ASCII/locale ordering.

nodes.name: Directories.c
nodes.summary: Recursively reads and validates the directory tree of a FileCore disc, checking each entry against the allocation map and optionally backing up files or extracting objects.

nodes.name: DiscOps.c
nodes.summary: Provides low-level disc I/O operations (byte and sector read/write, SWI dispatch, extract-to-sparse-file) that abstract over live RISC OS drives and raw disc image files.

nodes.name: DiscReader.c
nodes.summary: Main entry point for the DiscReader utility: parses command-line arguments, orchestrates boot block / map / directory reading, and displays statistics and size-distribution tables.

nodes.name: DiscReader.h
nodes.summary: Central header defining all FileCore disc constants, the global s_info program-state structure, struct types for disc record / map objects / free space / directory info, and function prototypes for the entire DiscReader subsystem.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines the large s_info aggregate that acts as a global program-state singleton, including nested structs for options, file handle, disc parameters, statistics counters, and space accounting.

nodes.name: Map.c
nodes.summary: Reads and interprets the FileCore allocation map, building in-memory linked-list structures for used and free space extents, and providing utilities for bit manipulation, address translation, and map writing.

nodes.name: Objects.c
nodes.summary: Handles FileCore object (file and directory) loading, saving, extraction, and copying using SIN-based addressing and map chunk traversal; also tracks per-object statistics.

nodes.name: SparceFile.c
nodes.summary: Implements a sparse disc-image container format that stores only written blocks with their 64-bit disc addresses, using a binary-search cache for fast random access during extraction and replay.
nodes.languageNotes: The format stores (addr64, size, data) records sequentially; a sorted in-memory cache enables O(log n) lookup. Note: the filename intentionally preserves the historical 'Sparce' spelling.

nodes.name: SparceFile.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the SparceFile API for creating, reading, writing, and appending blocks in a sparse disc-image container format identified by the magic bytes 'SPARCE\x00\x01'.

nodes.name: BigFile_Open
nodes.summary: Opens a disc image file for random access using an OSLib file handle.

nodes.name: BigFile_Read
nodes.summary: Reads a block from a 64-bit address in a big disc image file, dispatching to osgbpb on RISC OS or fseek/fread on host platforms.

nodes.name: BigFile_Write
nodes.summary: Writes a block to a 64-bit address in a big disc image file, dispatching to osgbpb on RISC OS or fseek/fwrite on host platforms.

nodes.name: ReadBootBlock
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the LBA0 sector containing the FileCore boot block, extracts the disc record, validates defect lists, and handles 512MB+ disc size checks.

nodes.name: ReadDefectLists
nodes.summary: Parses primary and secondary defect lists from the boot block, printing entries and reporting termination markers.

nodes.name: BootBlockChecksum
nodes.summary: Calculates the FileCore boot block CRC by accumulating a rotating byte sum over the first 511 bytes.

nodes.name: GetDiscRecord
nodes.summary: Deserialises a binary FileCore disc record from a byte buffer into the s_disc_record structure, including 64-bit disc size handling.

nodes.name: DisplayRecord
nodes.summary: Prints all fields of a disc record in human-readable form, including geometry, density type, and optional disc name for map records.

nodes.name: CalcMapLocation
nodes.summary: Calculates the sector address of the first map copy from the disc record geometry.

nodes.name: LoadDirectory
nodes.summary: Allocates memory and loads a FileCore directory object (old or new format), reallocating for large E+ directories.

nodes.name: IsDirectory
nodes.summary: Probes a disc SIN to determine if it refers to a valid FileCore directory, checking magic names and loading large E+ directories as needed.

nodes.name: CreateDir
nodes.summary: Initialises an empty FileCore directory buffer in either old (Hugo/Nick) or new (BigDir) format with correct header fields and initial checksum.

nodes.name: AddEntry
nodes.summary: Inserts a sorted directory entry (old or new format) into a FileCore directory buffer, extending E+ directories if needed.

nodes.name: RemoveEntry
nodes.summary: Removes a directory entry and compacts the directory buffer, shrinking large E+ directories when significant free space is reclaimed.

nodes.name: AdjustNameHeap
nodes.summary: Adjusts name-heap pointers in a BigDir directory after inserting or removing a name, maintaining consistent offsets.

nodes.name: SortDirectory
nodes.summary: Sorts directory entries in FileCore collation order using qsort, rebuilding the E+ name heap in the new entry order.

nodes.name: DirCheckByte
nodes.summary: Computes the FileCore directory integrity check byte by XOR-accumulating a 13-bit-rotated word sum over the directory data.

nodes.name: FindEntry
nodes.summary: Searches a directory for an entry by filename using RISC OS collation, returning its SIN and entry/offset indices.

nodes.name: WriteDirectory
nodes.summary: Updates the directory checksum and writes the directory object back to disc via SaveObject.

nodes.name: GetI
nodes.summary: Reads a 1–4 byte little-endian integer from an unaligned byte offset in a data buffer.

nodes.name: GetS
nodes.summary: Extracts a control-terminated or fixed-length ASCII string from a binary data buffer into a null-terminated C string.

nodes.name: filename_cmp
nodes.summary: Compares two RISC OS filenames using a 256-entry collation table that implements the Filer's observed ordering rules.

nodes.name: ReadDirectory
nodes.summary: Recursively reads all entries in a FileCore directory, validating SINs against the map, optionally extracting or backing up files.

nodes.name: ReadEntry
nodes.summary: Processes a single directory entry, verifying it exists in the allocation map, dispatching to shared/non-shared object readers, and optionally backing up the file.

nodes.name: ReadSharedObject
nodes.summary: Validates and accounts for a shared-sector FileCore object, computing its allocated size and detecting excess fragments.

nodes.name: ReadNonSharedObject
nodes.summary: Validates and accounts for a non-shared FileCore object, summing chunk allocations and tracking fragmentation and rounding statistics.

nodes.name: ReadSubDir
nodes.summary: Constructs the child directory path and recurses into ReadDirectory for a sub-directory entry.

nodes.name: Initialise
nodes.summary: Initialises disc access by opening a disc image file or dynamically resolving the DiscOp SWI name for a live RISC OS filing system, and creates the extract sparse file if needed.

nodes.name: DiscOp
nodes.summary: Invokes a FileCore DiscOp SWI and handles errors, distinguishing fatal conditions (drive empty, bad drive) from recoverable disc errors.

nodes.name: ReadBytes
nodes.summary: Reads bytes from a disc (file or live drive) applying partition offset, dispatching to SparceFile, BigFile, or DiscOp as appropriate.

nodes.name: WriteBytes
nodes.summary: Writes bytes to a disc (file or live drive) applying partition offset, dispatching to SparceFile, BigFile, or DiscOp.

nodes.name: ReadSectors
nodes.summary: Reads sectors from a disc image or live drive, falling back to single-sector reads when a multi-sector DiscOp fails.

nodes.name: WriteSectors
nodes.summary: Writes sectors to a disc image or live drive using the appropriate SparceFile, BigFile, or SectorDiscOp path.

nodes.name: Extract
nodes.summary: Appends a disc block at its 64-bit address to the sparse extraction file, converting between byte and sector addressing.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses command-line options (file, verbose, backup, extract, show flags), orchestrates the full disc-read pipeline (init, boot block, map, objects), and emits final statistics.

nodes.name: Finalise
nodes.summary: Frees all dynamically allocated resources — maps, object structures, free list — and closes the disc image file.

nodes.name: ShowTables
nodes.summary: Displays object and free-space size distribution tables in exponentially increasing size bins.

nodes.name: ShowStats
nodes.summary: Displays a summary table of disc statistics including used/free space, file/directory counts, fragmentation, and map wastage.

nodes.name: ReadMap
nodes.summary: Reads both copies of the FileCore allocation map, computes geometry parameters, builds the object and free-space index, and optionally extracts map sectors.

nodes.name: ReadMapContents
nodes.summary: Decodes the bit-packed allocation map zone by zone, classifying each entry as a file ID, free block, defect, or system file.

nodes.name: WriteMap
nodes.summary: Recalculates all zone check bytes for the modified map and writes it to both map copies on disc.

nodes.name: AddID
nodes.summary: Inserts a map allocation chunk into the object index linked list, maintaining zone-ordered fragment order and accumulating used-space statistics.

nodes.name: MakeID
nodes.summary: Allocates a new file ID from free space in the map, splitting or consuming free blocks and updating free-chain pointers and zone headers.

nodes.name: MapAddr
nodes.summary: Converts a zone number and bit offset to a sector address by applying the LFAU/sector size relationship.

nodes.name: SetBit
nodes.summary: Sets or clears a single bit in a byte array by index.

nodes.name: ReadObjects
nodes.summary: Locates the root directory in the object map and recursively reads the entire directory tree, tracking statistics.

nodes.name: SinAddr
nodes.summary: Converts a FileCore SIN (Sector Index Number) to its sector address by resolving the object's map chunk and applying the sharing offset.

nodes.name: LoadObject
nodes.summary: Loads a FileCore object from disc into a buffer, either as a single shared fragment or by concatenating multiple non-shared map chunks.

nodes.name: SaveObject
nodes.summary: Writes a FileCore object from a buffer back to disc, handling shared and multi-chunk non-shared objects.

nodes.name: ExtractObject
nodes.summary: Copies a FileCore object to the sparse extraction file, preserving its disc address for later replay.

nodes.name: CopyObject
nodes.summary: Copies a FileCore object to a host filesystem file, using a zone-sized buffer and chunked I/O for fragmented or large files.

nodes.name: SparceFile_Find
nodes.summary: Locates the file offset of a disc address block within a sparse file, rebuilding and binary-searching a sorted cache of block headers on first access.

nodes.name: SparceFile_AppendBlock
nodes.summary: Appends a new block to a sparse file, updating the sorted cache and marking superseded blocks as free.

nodes.name: SparceFile_Write
nodes.summary: Writes data to an existing block in a sparse file at the given address, or appends a new block if no matching block is found.

nodes.name: SparceFile_Read
nodes.summary: Reads data from a sparse file at the given 64-bit address, zeroing the buffer before reading to handle partial-block misses.

nodes.name: SparceFile_ReadNext
nodes.summary: Reads the next sequential block header and data from a sparse file, allocating a buffer for the caller.

nodes.name: GetUsedInfo
nodes.summary: Returns the head of the chunk linked list for a given file ID from the object index, or NULL if not present.

nodes.name: AddFree
nodes.summary: Adds a free space extent to the doubly-linked free list and accumulates free-space statistics.

nodes.name: MapZoneCheck

nodes.name: internet6

nodes.languageNotes: Uses inline ARM/AArch64 assembly (__asm blocks) to invoke internet stack callbacks with the correct private-word register (r12/x12) convention required by RISC OS DCI.

nodes.name: internet6_enumerate_drivers

nodes.name: internet6_filter
nodes.summary: Handles DCI6 filter claim and release requests from the internet stack, storing or clearing the stack RX/status/can-TX handler pointers and enabling promiscuous mode on claim.

nodes.name: internet6_transmit
nodes.summary: DCI6 transmit SWI handler: loads an mbuf chain into the next available TX DMA descriptor, advances the TX producer index, and signals back-pressure to the stack when the ring is nearly full.

nodes.name: dci_tx_handler
nodes.summary: Direct-call TX veneer (invoked via CMHG dci_tx_veneer): transmits an mbuf chain from the internet stack's direct-call path, returning a pause flag rather than an OS error pointer.

nodes.name: genet_rxintr6
nodes.summary: RX interrupt bottom-half: drains all pending frames from the GENET RX DMA ring, allocates mbuf chains from the RISC OS mbuf manager, copies data from uncached DMA memory, and dispatches each frame to the registered internet-stack RX handler.

nodes.name: genet_setup_txbuf6
nodes.summary: Loads an mbuf chain into DMA segments and calls genet_setup_txdesc for each segment, setting SOP/EOP/CRC/QTAG flags; returns the number of descriptors consumed or -1 if the ring is full.

nodes.name: mbuf6

nodes.name: mbuf_register6
nodes.summary: Initialises and registers a DCI6 mbuf session with the RISC OS Mbuf Manager, populating the dci4_mbctl6 control block with the requested buffer size parameters.

nodes.name: EtherGENETHdr
nodes.summary: CMHG module header for the EtherGENET RISC OS module: declares module title/help strings, initialisation/finalisation entry points, service call handlers for DCI and mbuf events, SWI chunk 0x59F00 (EtherGE.*), generic veneers for interrupt and TX callbacks, and five *Configure commands (EGEInfo, EGETest, EGELink, EGEAdvertise, EGEFlowControl).
nodes.languageNotes: CMHG (C Module Header Generator) source — compiled by the RISC OS cmhg tool to produce module header glue and C stubs; not C source itself.

nodes.name: bcmgenetreg
nodes.summary: Hardware register map for the Broadcom GENETv5 Gigabit Ethernet controller: defines all MMIO register offsets and bitfield masks for the system control, UMAC, MDIO, RBUF/TBUF, and TX/RX DMA descriptor rings; sets DMA descriptor count to 64 for RISC OS (256 on NetBSD).

nodes.name: bcmgenetvar
nodes.summary: Defines the genet_softc driver state structure (PHY mode, bus space handles, MII data, TX/RX DMA ring state), the genet_ring and genet_bufmap DMA buffer tracking types, and the genet_attach/genet_intr function prototypes; ported from NetBSD.
nodes.languageNotes: Conditionally includes bcmgenetreg.h from a RISC OS-local path rather than the NetBSD kernel tree path.

nodes.name: bus
nodes.summary: RISC OS bus-space and DMA abstraction layer: defines bus_space_tag/handle/addr/size types mapped to uintptr_t, MMIO read/write helpers (bus_read_4 etc.), and the DMA map/segment/sync types and operations used by the BSD-ported genet driver.
nodes.languageNotes: Elesar-authored RISC OS porting shim replacing the NetBSD machine/bus.h machine abstraction; DMA segments carry a ds_logical field for the uncached virtual address alongside ds_addr.

nodes.name: debug
nodes.summary: Conditional debug logging header: declares debugf, memdump, mbufdump, debuglog, mbufchain, dbpmem, and prmbdata as real functions under INDEBUG, as no-op static stubs under Norcroft C90 (which lacks variadic macros), or as empty macros otherwise.
nodes.languageNotes: Provides Norcroft-safe C90 static stubs (rather than variadic macros) to avoid compile errors with the RISC OS native C compiler.

nodes.name: egemodule
nodes.summary: Central module-wide type definitions and global declarations for the EtherGENET driver: defines etherge_if_t (per-interface state including DCI6 stack handler slots), etherge_nic_t (controller state with flags, MTU, and fault codes), error/message token enumerations, and all global externs (nic[], nicunit[], nicifp, mbufsession, module_pw).

nodes.name: entrypoints
nodes.summary: Defines the if_entrypoint structure used to advertise direct-call entry points from the EtherGENET driver to the RISC OS internet stack, including the TX packet veneer pointer and AArch32/AArch64-safe private-word field.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses uintptr_t for the r12 private-word field to be safe across AArch32 (32-bit) and AArch64 (64-bit) builds, avoiding the silent truncation that would occur with plain int.

nodes.name: filtering
nodes.summary: C header defining the packet-filtering subsystem for the EtherGENET driver, including the filter_t struct, address-level classification macros, and declarations for filter management and dispatch functions.
nodes.languageNotes: RISC OS extension-less C header; uses _kernel_oserror and RISC OS DCI Dib/RxHdr types. The IS_A_KEEPER macro encodes a 4x4 address/error filtering matrix in a single 16-bit bitmask lookup.

nodes.name: ro_mbuf0

nodes.languageNotes: Same role as ro_mbuf; the '0' suffix is a RISC OS source tree convention for alternate header variants used by different object files in the same driver.

nodes.name: VL805 xHCI Driver Development
nodes.summary: Development arc (Sessions 1–5, boots 1–143+) for the VL805 USB 3.0 host controller connected via BCM2711 PCIe. Key challenges: HSE root cause, CNR deadlock, ERST/ERSTBA caching, MSI collision, firmware-dependent init sequences, and event ring activation.

nodes.name: VL805 ERSTBA Cache Problem
nodes.summary: The VL805 MCU reads ERSTBA from MMIO exactly once during HCRST firmware re-init and caches it permanently. After HCRST the hardware clears the register to 0, making the cache always 0. Solution: relocate ERST to physical address 0 and set RC_BAR2 to cover PCIe address 0.

nodes.name: xHCI Event Ring Working (Boot 143)
nodes.summary: Historic milestone at boot 143: the VL805 event ring started working after 143+ debug sessions. Three undocumented VL805-specific requirements discovered via Circle project disassembly: CMD_INTE before CMD_RS, ERSTSZ=1 before ERSTBA, and ERDP with EHB=1 on init.

nodes.name: DWC2 OTG USB Driver
nodes.summary: Synopsys DWC2 core (revision 2.80a) at 0xFE980000 driving the USB-C OTG port on Raspberry Pi 4. First successful device detection (boot 118) via the OTG port, entirely independent of the VL805 xHCI controller.

nodes.name: BCM2711 GENETv5 Ethernet Driver
nodes.summary: Bare-metal driver for the BCM2711 integrated GENETv5 NIC at MMIO 0xFD580000 with BCM54213PE PHY in RGMII-ID mode. Development arc boots 302–342 culminating in reliable DHCP, ARP, and ICMP ping with sub-4ms RTT. Key rule: ID_MODE_DISABLE=1 to avoid double TX clock delay.

nodes.name: USB Device Enumeration Stack
nodes.summary: xHCI USB enumeration pipeline: Enable Slot, Address Device, GET_DESCRIPTOR. Multi-slot support added in boot 147 with per-slot DMA layout. First device detected at boot 38; full enumeration working after boot 143 event ring fix.

nodes.name: PCIe RC + VL805 Initialization
nodes.summary: BCM2711 PCIe RC initialization sequence for the VL805 USB controller. Critical fixes: RGR1 ordering before MISC_CTRL, mailbox GET_POWER_STATE guard, Memory Space enable before xhci_init, MSI setup, and conditional HCRST based on firmware version detection.

nodes.name: RISC OS Module Loading System
nodes.summary: Phoenix's native RISC OS module infrastructure supporting both AArch64 (bit 30 in init_entry) and ARM32 (stub) modules. Modules loaded from NVMe disc via FileCore/DiscReader or linked directly into kernel. CMunge -64bit pipeline for building new AArch64 modules.

nodes.name: RISC OS SWI Dispatch Infrastructure
nodes.summary: SVC exception handler routes SWI calls to registered module handlers. SWI dispatch via SVC #0 with SWI number in x10 (riscos64-clib convention). Implemented OS SWIs: OS_WriteC/N/S, OS_ReadC, OS_Heap, OS_Module, OS_ChangeEnvironment, OS_ReadMonotonicTime, OS_Mouse, OS_SpriteOp stub.

nodes.name: FileCore/ADFS Disc Access
nodes.summary: Phoenix FileCore implementation for reading RISC OS new-map ADFS discs from NVMe. IDA→LBA resolution via zone maps. DiscReader integration (boot 401+) solved RTL9210 USB-SATA bridge zero-return bug for interleaved reads. Supports filecore_find_path, filecore_read_file, filecore_exec_obey.

nodes.name: Phoenix Network Stack
nodes.summary: Bare-metal TCP/IP stack with DHCP, ARP, ICMP, UDP, TCP, and DNS. PhoenixResolver implements Inet6Sources Resolver SWI chunk 0x46000 for hostname lookup. PhoenixGENET registered as DCI4 module EtherGENET. All blocking poll loops must drive GENET RX ring directly.

nodes.name: SDIO CYW43455 WiFi/BT Driver
nodes.summary: SDIO Phase 1 driver for CYW43455 WiFi+BT chip via BCM2711 SlowArasan at 0xFE300000 (EMMC0). GPIO 34-39 ALT3, bus power 3.3V, CMD0→CMD5→CMD3→CMD7→CCCR probe. Phase 2 (firmware download, brcmfmac SDIO protocol) ongoing as of boot 492.

nodes.name: xHCI DMA Buffer Layout
nodes.summary: 264KB DMA region at 0x080b3000–0x080f5000 (Normal-NC, MMU identity map) containing DCBAA, cmd_ring, evt_ring, MSI landing pad, ERST, scratchpad array/pages, input/output contexts, EP0 ring and data buffer. DMA_OFFSET=0 (identity mapping after boot 22 RC_BAR2 fix).

nodes.name: VL805/BCM2711 Hardware Rules Compendium
nodes.summary: 120+ numbered hardware rules accumulated across 400+ boot iterations. Covers VL805-specific HCRST sequences, ERST/ERSTBA ordering, PORTSC write safety, CNR firmware dependency, RGMII clock delay, AArch64 ABI vararg limits, and SDIO controller address mapping.

nodes.name: CursorModule — RISC OS Pointer/Input Manager
nodes.summary: Kernel-linked AArch64 RISC OS module managing mouse pointer sprite and keyboard input. Built via CMunge -64bit pipeline and linked directly into kernel ELF. Required LDR+BLR fix for external calls (BL offsets are invalid after heap copy), and linker.ld fix to place cursor_module_start inside section braces.

nodes.name: ARM32 RISC OS Module Support
nodes.summary: ARM32 RISC OS modules loaded from disc (ABIMod, Colours, IconBorderFob, LanMan98) are registered as stubs with Init() deferred. Full AArch32 EL0 execution requires mode-switching infrastructure not yet implemented as of boot 438.

nodes.name: USB Mass Storage (NVMe via RTL9210)
nodes.summary: NVMe SSD connected via RTL9210B USB-NVMe bridge accessed through xHCI bulk transfers. RTL9210 has a zero-return bug for interleaved zone/data reads (resolved by DiscReader integration). Endpoint recovery (ep_recover) required for BOT reset during cold-start.

nodes.name: Phoenix OS Boot Milestones
nodes.summary: Key development milestones: boot 35 (xHCI controller running), boot 118 (first DWC2 device), boot 143 (event ring working), boot 314 (first Ethernet frames), boot 381 (DNS resolving), boot 411 (DiscReader integration), boot 438 (all disc modules Init() OK, cursor visible). SDIO WiFi probe boot 466.

nodes.name: Circle Project Reference
nodes.summary: R. Stange's Circle bare-metal C++ framework for Raspberry Pi was instrumental in solving the VL805 event ring at boot 143. Circle's xhcieventmanager.cpp and xhcidevice.cpp disassembly revealed three undocumented VL805-specific register write requirements absent from the xHCI spec.

nodes.name: riscos64-clib AArch64 C Library
nodes.summary: RISC OS 64-bit C library used by AArch64 modules. Key integration challenges: _clib_initialisemodule SWI sequence, OS_Module Claim/Free for heap setup, _FORTIFY_SOURCE __vfprintf_chk recursion bug (fixed in boot 432), and GOT-based relocation for disc-loaded modules. Charles Ferguson provides ongoing support.

nodes.name: WIMP Desktop / Task Manager
nodes.summary: Cooperative task scheduler (WIMP) running as the main execution loop. Polls GENET RX ring every 4ms, drives keyboard and mouse input. Boot 413 tri-factor milestone: disc modules loaded, WIMP desktop running, TCP/DNS/DHCP working, keyboard live.

nodes.name: usb_mass_storage.c
nodes.summary: USB Mass Storage class driver implementing Bulk-Only Transport (BOT) over SCSI. Handles device enumeration, READ/WRITE(16) commands, BOT error recovery, read-ahead caching, and blockdev registration with media-class scoring for NVMe/SSD/Flash.

nodes.name: bot_scsi_cmd
nodes.summary: Core BOT SCSI command executor: sends CBW, optional data phase, reads CSW. On data-phase stall issues CLEAR_HALT per BOT §6.6.2 and still drains the CSW to keep the pipe clean. On CSW failure clears both endpoints and calls xhci_ep_recover_guarded.

nodes.name: bot_read_capacity
nodes.summary: Issues SCSI READ CAPACITY (10) command via bot_scsi_cmd and parses the 8-byte response to extract the last LBA and block size for a given LUN.

nodes.name: bot_read_capacity16
nodes.summary: Issues SCSI READ CAPACITY (16) for drives >2 TB: builds a 16-byte CDB, parses the 32-byte response, extracts 64-bit last LBA and 32-bit block size. Handles RTL9210 bridge quirks.

nodes.name: usb_bot_rw
nodes.summary: Issues READ(16) or WRITE(16) SCSI commands over BOT using 64-bit LBA. Switched from READ(10) to avoid RTL9210 bridge firmware bug that silently returns zeros for certain LBA ranges.

nodes.name: bot_recover
nodes.summary: Full BOT error recovery: BOT Mass Storage Reset, CLEAR_HALT on bulk IN+OUT, xhci_ep_recover_guarded (CLEAR_HALT preceded), then TUR retry up to 5 times.

nodes.name: usb_bdev_read
nodes.summary: blockdev read callback implementing an 8-sector (4 KB) read-ahead cache. On cache miss fetches READAHEAD_N sectors; detects RTL9210 zero-return bug and retries after 2 ms.

nodes.name: usb_bdev_write
nodes.summary: blockdev write callback: invalidates read-ahead cache then issues a WRITE(16) via usb_bot_rw.

nodes.name: usb_storage_probe
nodes.summary: MSC probe: declines UAS, allocates usb_storage_t, finds bulk endpoints, performs BOT reset + CLEAR_HALT + TUR retry loop + INQUIRY + READ CAPACITY (RC10 then RC16 polling), registers blockdev with media-class classification.

nodes.name: usb_mass_storage_init
nodes.summary: Registers the USB MSC class driver with the USB core.

nodes.name: timer.c
nodes.summary: ARM Generic Timer driver for Phoenix OS. Manages per-CPU timer lists with spinlock protection, reads CNTPCT_EL0/CNTFRQ_EL0 system registers for time-keeping, and implements a 4 ms (250 Hz) PPI-30 interrupt via timer_enable_interrupt(). The ISR (timer_irq_handler) re-arms the countdown and sets deferred HID request flags (hid_mouse_request, hid_kbd_request) consumed by wimp_task(). timer_tick() walks expired callbacks and calls schedule().

nodes.name: timer_init
nodes.summary: Global timer initialization. Zeroes all per-CPU timer lists and initializes all MAX_CPUS spinlocks. Logs the ARM generic timer frequency read from CNTFRQ_EL0.

nodes.name: timer_init_cpu
nodes.summary: Per-CPU timer initialization. Resets the timer list for the current CPU, initializes its spinlock, and sets CNTP_CTL_EL0 = 0x2 (IMASK=1, ENABLE=0) to keep the timer masked until irq_init() completes.

nodes.name: timer_enable_interrupt
nodes.summary: Arms the ARM generic timer at 4 ms (250 Hz). Registers timer_irq_handler on GIC PPI 30 (nCNTPNSIRQ) via irq_set_handler/irq_unmask, loads CNTP_TVAL_EL0 with the computed tick count, and sets CNTP_CTL_EL0 = 1 (ENABLE=1, IMASK=0). Must be called after irq_init() and after DAIF.I is cleared.

nodes.name: timer_tick
nodes.summary: Software timer tick dispatcher. Walks the per-CPU expired timer list under spinlock, fires each callback, then calls schedule() and re-arms the hardware countdown register.

nodes.name: timer_irq_handler
nodes.summary: GIC PPI-30 interrupt service routine for the ARM generic timer. Re-arms CNTP_TVAL_EL0 immediately, then sets hid_mouse_request=1 every tick and hid_kbd_request=1 every 4th tick for deferred HID polling in wimp_task().

nodes.name: dashboard.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that builds and deploys the Phoenix OS knowledge dashboard to GitHub Pages. Triggers on push to main and on workflow_dispatch. Uses actions/checkout and actions/deploy-pages to publish static dashboard content from the repository.

nodes.name: README_BOOT.md
nodes.summary: Boot guide for Phoenix OS at boot438. Describes SD card file requirements (kernel8.img, config.txt, Pi 4 firmware blobs), hardware setup (serial console GPIO 14/15 at 115200 8N1, NVMe via USB-C DeskPi Pro). Documents expected 10-step boot sequence including GPU framebuffer, device tree, MMU, scheduler, heap, GIC, PCIe/USB, VFS/modules/network. Lists module status table (AArch64 modules all init OK, ARM32 modules deferred). Tracks boot arc history from boot431 to boot438 with fix summaries. Includes troubleshooting guide.

nodes.name: ARCHITECTURE.md
nodes.summary: Architecture overview for Phoenix OS. Describes target hardware (Raspberry Pi 4B BCM2711 Cortex-A72, secondary Pi 5 BCM2712). Documents the design philosophy: bare-metal AArch64 kernel inspired by RISC OS, single-address-space, cooperative-first, all drivers/kernel/apps run at EL1, monolithic image. Defines the memory map: 0x00000000-0xFFFF reserved/MMIO trap, 0x00010000-0x1FFFF xHCI DMA buffer (Normal-NC), 0x00080000 kernel load address, 0x00100000+ kernel heap. References the xHCI DMA sub-layout (DCBAA, command ring, event ring, ERST, MSI pad).

nodes.name: USB_XHCI_VL805.md
nodes.summary: Detailed development history and breadcrumb document for the VL805 xHCI USB driver. Documents hardware topology (BCM2711 PCIe RC → VL805, BDF 01:00.0, PCI ID 1106:3483), VL805 MCU 8051 firmware boot behaviour, initialisation sequence (PCIe bring-up, ring setup, controller start, port power, port scan/enumeration), the force-ring pattern (atomic W1C→RS→CRCR→doorbell within 4ms MCU window), PP power-cycle port recovery, companion port DR=1 hazard, and the event ring write-back problem (diagnosed at boot61, root causes listed). Key learnings indexed by boot number (boots 1-61). Documented at boot61 milestone when USB-MSC class driver first binds.

nodes.name: milestone-usb-mass-storage-bot.md
nodes.summary: Milestone document for USB Bulk-Only Transport (BOT) mass storage driver, achieved at boot163. Documents the hardware (Pi 4B DeskPi Pro, VL805 xHCI, VL812 hub, ASMedia ASM1153E SATA bridge, 500GB SSD registering as usb0). Details code changes: xhci_configure_endpoints() for ConfigureEndpoint command, xhci_bulk_transfer() full implementation with DMA bounce buffer and doorbell, SET_CONFIGURATION control transfer (boot162 fix), usb_mass_storage.c rewrite with bot_scsi_cmd()/bot_read_capacity(), blockdev_ops_t registration. Documents DMA memory layout for per-slot bulk rings. Bug timeline from boot159-163. Next steps: FileCore sector reads, partition table parsing, Makefile -MMD dependency tracking.

nodes.name: usb_gadget_start
nodes.summary: Enables the DWC2 D+ pull-up to signal device presence to the host.

nodes.name: aif.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the Phoenix RISC OS AIF loader. Documents the AIF header layout (offsets 0x00–0x100+) as defined by riscos64-clib's aif.lnk linker script, the application memory slot layout (base 0x8000, top 0x30000000), and declares the single public function aif_run. Include guard: AIF_H.

nodes.name: aif_run
nodes.summary: Declaration: int aif_run(const char *path, const char *cmdtail). Loads and executes an AIF absolute file from the RISC OS filing system. path is a RISC OS pathname (e.g. '$.!Boot.Resources.!OBSD.BASIC'); cmdtail is the command tail passed to the application (may be empty string). Returns 0 on normal application exit, -1 on load error. May not return if the application calls OS_Exit directly.

nodes.name: LICENSE
nodes.summary: MIT licence text granting broad permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute the Phoenix OS source code.

nodes.name: NOTES.md
nodes.summary: Working notes on integrating the RISC OS SystemVars module into Phoenix OS, documenting the reversed 'kernel collusion' mechanism, the default variable namespace established by SystemVarsDefaults, the Phoenix wiring plan, and open questions requiring further reverse-engineering.

nodes.name: swi_call.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 assembly veneer implementing _kernel_call, the calling convention used by OS_ClaimOSSWI-registered handlers; marshals up to 10 32-bit registers (R0-R9) from an inregs array, calls the handler with the private word in x12, captures outregs, and returns an error pointer.
nodes.languageNotes: Also contains test_osswi_handler, a self-test stub that computes R0+R1 and clears V to verify the register/private-word passing convention end-to-end. The calling convention (V flag for error signalling, x12 for private word) mirrors the 32-bit RISC OS module ABI.

nodes.name: _kernel_call
nodes.summary: Loads R0-R9 from an optional inregs uint32_t array into w0-w9, passes the private word in x12, calls an OS_ClaimOSSWI handler via blr, then stores the resulting registers to an optional outregs array; returns the error pointer (x0 if V was set, else 0).

nodes.name: test_osswi_handler
nodes.summary: Self-test handler stub: sets R0 = R0+R1 and R2 = private word, then clears all condition flags to signal no error; used by osswi_selftest to validate _kernel_call.

nodes.name: Objects.c
nodes.summary: Implements FileCore object I/O — loading and saving disc objects via their Sector Index Numbers (SINs) — handling fragmented objects through the map and supporting copy, extract, and statistics operations.
nodes.languageNotes: SIN-to-disc-address translation goes through SinAddr/MapAddr, mirroring the FileCore map indirection layer; CopyObject uses RISC OS OSFile/OSGBPB SWI wrappers for host-side extraction.

nodes.name: ReadObjects
nodes.summary: Recursively enumerates all FileCore objects starting from a given SIN, reading directories and accumulating object statistics across the disc image.

nodes.name: SinAddr
nodes.summary: Translates a FileCore Sector Index Number (SIN) to a physical disc address by walking the allocation map, handling both direct and indirect map entries.

nodes.name: LoadObject
nodes.summary: Loads a FileCore object identified by its SIN into a caller-supplied buffer, handling fragmented objects by reading each contiguous run of sectors via SinAddr.

nodes.name: SaveObject
nodes.summary: Writes a FileCore object from a caller-supplied buffer back to disc at the physical sectors identified by its SIN, handling fragmented extents.

nodes.name: AddObjectStat
nodes.summary: Accumulates global file and directory count/size statistics as objects are enumerated during a disc-image scan.

nodes.name: dr_api.h
nodes.summary: Public C header exposing the discreader module API — function declarations and shared types that consumers (e.g., the filing-system layer) use to initialise, query, and write FileCore disc images.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only interface with no implementations; guards the public surface of the discreader module from internal implementation details.

nodes.name: vfs.h
nodes.summary: VFS (Virtual Filesystem) header defining the shared filesystem abstraction types, vfs_open/close/read/seek/write function prototypes, and the vfs_handle structure used across the kernel filing layer.

nodes.name: sched.c
nodes.summary: Implements a 4-CPU symmetric round-robin scheduler with per-CPU run queues, idle tasks, spinlock-protected enqueue/dequeue, assembly-level context switching, and cross-CPU task wakeup via inter-processor interrupts.
nodes.languageNotes: context_switch relies on inline assembly or an assembly stub to save/restore AArch64 callee-saved registers; the scheduler uses __builtin_ctzll for efficient least-loaded CPU selection.

nodes.name: sched_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the global scheduler data structures and spinlock before any CPU-specific setup is performed.

nodes.name: sched_init_cpu
nodes.summary: Sets up the per-CPU run queue and creates the CPU's idle task, enrolling it in the scheduler so the CPU always has something to run.

nodes.name: context_switch
nodes.summary: Performs the low-level AArch64 context switch between two tasks, saving the outgoing task's register state and restoring the incoming task's state.

nodes.name: schedule
nodes.summary: Core scheduler dispatch function: acquires the per-CPU run queue lock, selects the next runnable task via pick_next_task, and calls context_switch to transfer execution.

nodes.name: task_block
nodes.summary: Marks the current task as blocked with the given state and immediately yields the CPU by calling schedule.

nodes.name: task_wakeup
nodes.summary: Transitions a blocked task back to the runnable state and sends an inter-processor interrupt to wake the target CPU if the task belongs to a different core.

nodes.name: enqueue_task
nodes.summary: Appends a task to a scheduler run queue under spinlock protection, ensuring safe concurrent access from multiple CPUs.

nodes.name: yield
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper that voluntarily surrenders the CPU by calling schedule, allowing other runnable tasks to execute.

nodes.name: .gitignore
nodes.summary: Git ignore rules excluding build artifacts, object files, kernel ELF binaries, and editor temporaries from version control.

nodes.name: WORKFLOW.md
nodes.summary: Developer session guide covering project vision and aims, current status at boot577, hardware setup, FileCore parameters, SBPr directory format, multi-disc priority rules, milestone history, next steps, and important gotchas for ongoing development.

nodes.name: PI5_FACTS.md
nodes.summary: Hardware fact table for the BCM2712-based Raspberry Pi 5, recording confirmed address maps, SoC peripheral window, RP1 southbridge PCIe endpoint identity, DMA coherency behaviour, and gaps identified from real Pi OS boot-log observations to guide the Pi 5 port.

nodes.name: PI5_PORT_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Detailed nine-phase implementation plan for porting Phoenix OS to the Raspberry Pi 5 (BCM2712), covering a code audit, DT-first peripheral detection, GIC bring-up, mailbox, SD/FileCore, PCIe RC and RP1 southbridge, USB via RP1 xHCI, Ethernet GEM driver, NVMe, SMP polish, and a risk register.

nodes.name: mmc.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the MMC/SD driver, declaring the mmc_init, mmc_read_blocks, mmc_write_blocks, and mmc_get_info entry points together with any shared type definitions.

nodes.name: dt_diag.c
nodes.summary: Device tree diagnostics module that prints a structured dump of the parsed FDT — board compatibility strings, memory ranges, CPU list, and GIC addresses — via the kernel debug channel.

nodes.name: dt_dump_diag
nodes.summary: Walks the raw FDT and the parsed dt_state struct to print board compatibility, memory, CPU, and GIC details to the kernel debug output.

nodes.name: fdt_walk.c
nodes.summary: Low-level Flattened Device Tree parser implementing big-endian token walking, node traversal, property lookup, cell-width-aware register reads, and compatible-string matching over a raw FDT blob in memory.
nodes.languageNotes: All FDT integers are big-endian; be32() performs a manual byte-reversal since the kernel has no libc. Node handles are opaque uint32_t offsets into the struct block, not pointers.

nodes.name: fdt_find_node
nodes.summary: Walks the FDT struct block following a slash-delimited path string to locate and return the handle of the named node.

nodes.name: fdt_get_property
nodes.summary: Scans a node's property tokens to find one matching the given name, returning a pointer and length to the raw property value.

nodes.name: fdt_is_compatible
nodes.summary: Searches the null-separated compatible string list in a node's compatible property for an exact match against the given string.

nodes.name: fdt_next_compatible
nodes.summary: Iterates the entire FDT struct block searching for the next node that has a matching compatible string, enabling device enumeration.

nodes.name: fdt_read_reg
nodes.summary: Reads a node's reg property respecting parent #address-cells and #size-cells widths, returning base address and size as 64-bit values.

nodes.name: skip_node
nodes.summary: Advances the struct-block offset past an entire FDT node and all its nested children and properties, used internally by sibling traversal.

nodes.name: fdt_root
nodes.summary: Returns a node handle for the FDT root node by locating the first FDT_BEGIN_NODE token in the struct block.

nodes.name: fdt_check
nodes.summary: Validates the FDT magic number (0xD00DFEED) and returns true if the blob is a well-formed FDT.

nodes.name: fdt_first_child
nodes.summary: Finds and returns the handle of the first child node of a given parent by scanning past the parent's properties to the first nested FDT_BEGIN_NODE.

nodes.name: fdt_next_sibling
nodes.summary: Returns the next sibling node of a given node by skipping the current node's subtree and finding the following FDT_BEGIN_NODE token.

nodes.name: fdt_walk.h
nodes.summary: Public API header for the FDT walker, declaring all fdt_* function prototypes, the fdt_node handle type, the fdt_prop struct, and FDT token constants used across the kernel device tree layer.

nodes.name: malloc.c
nodes.summary: Kernel heap allocator providing kmalloc, kfree, and kcalloc over a 128 MB static heap, using a first-fit free-list with bidirectional physical block links, block-split/coalesce, and header/tail-canary corruption detection.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses magic words (HDR_MAGIC=0xFEEDC0DE, TAIL_MAGIC=0xDEADC0DE) at each block's header and tail to detect corruption and double-free at kfree time without requiring a separate debug build; 16-byte alignment enforced throughout.

nodes.name: kmalloc
nodes.summary: Allocates at least `size` bytes from the kernel heap using first-fit search, optionally splits the found block to reduce waste, plants a tail canary, and returns a 16-byte-aligned pointer.

nodes.name: kfree
nodes.summary: Returns a block to the kernel heap free-list, validating the header magic and tail canary for corruption/double-free detection, then coalesces adjacent free blocks.

nodes.name: kcalloc
nodes.summary: Allocates and zeroes nmemb * size bytes, with overflow-safe total size computation, delegating to kmalloc.

nodes.name: malloc_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the heap by placing a single free block header covering the entire 128 MB heap region and setting the free-list head.

nodes.name: coalesce_forward
nodes.summary: Merges a just-freed block with its physically adjacent successor block if that successor is also free, reducing heap fragmentation.

nodes.name: heap_stats
nodes.summary: Prints heap utilisation diagnostics: bytes allocated, total heap size, free bytes, and number of free blocks.

nodes.name: DiscReader.h
nodes.summary: Master header for the RISC OS-style DiscReader subsystem, defining all ADFS on-disc data structures (DiscRecord, directory layouts, map zone constants) and declaring the public API for every DiscReader submodule including DiscOps, Directories, DirUtils, Map, and Objects.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines both old-style Hugo/Nick (E-format) and new BigDir (E+ format) directory layouts. The DR_DIRBUF macro rounds directory allocations up to the native sector size, which was the key fix for 4K NVMe sector support.

nodes.name: Directories.c
nodes.summary: Implements recursive ADFS directory sector parsing, reading both old Hugo/Nick (E-format) and new BigDir (E+ format) directory structures, verifying each entry against the object map and recursing into subdirectories.

nodes.name: DiscOps.c
nodes.summary: Phoenix bare-metal I/O layer for DiscReader, replacing RISC OS SWI disc access with calls to the Phoenix block device interface and providing 4K-native NVMe sector translation via a temporary buffer to avoid buffer overruns on sub-sector reads.
nodes.languageNotes: The ReadSectors function detects when the requested byte count is not a whole multiple of the native sector size (e.g. 512-byte boot block on a 4K-native NVMe) and reads into a temporary heap buffer before copying out exactly the requested bytes. This was the critical fix enabling all 14 disc modules to load from the Crucial P3 500GB.

nodes.name: DirUtils.c
nodes.summary: ADFS directory utility functions including entry lookup, load/save, name comparison using a 256-entry RISC OS collation table, and byte-field accessors (GetI/SetI/GetS/SetS); write-path functions (CreateDir, RemoveEntry, SortDirectory) are conditionally disabled with #if 0 for the read-only bare-metal Phoenix port.
nodes.languageNotes: The 256-entry fn_collate table implements the RISC OS filer collation order (case-insensitive, locale-aware character ordering) for filename_cmp. Most write-path functions are compiled out with #if 0 since the Phoenix port is currently read-only; AddEntry and AdjustNameHeap are re-enabled for new-file creation (Stage C).

nodes.name: ReadDirectory
nodes.summary: Recursively reads an ADFS directory by loading its sector data, branching on filecore version to handle old-style (Hugo/Nick) and new BigDir (E+) layouts, and iterating over all entries via ReadEntry.

nodes.name: ReadEntry
nodes.summary: Parses a single ADFS directory entry in either old or new format, extracts name/SIN/size/attributes, validates the SIN against the object map, and dispatches to ReadSharedObject, ReadNonSharedObject, or ReadSubDir as appropriate.

nodes.name: ReadNonSharedObject
nodes.summary: Accumulates allocation size for a non-shared ADFS map object by walking its chunk list, detecting excess fragments and fragmentation statistics.

nodes.name: ReadSectors
nodes.summary: Translates a logical ADFS sector read into a Phoenix block-device read, handling 4K-native NVMe sectors by reading into a temporary buffer when the requested byte count is not a whole multiple of the native block size.

nodes.name: ReadBytes
nodes.summary: Byte-addressed disc read that converts byte offsets to sector numbers accounting for the partition LBA base, using a temporary buffer for unaligned spans.

nodes.name: WriteSectors
nodes.summary: Translates a logical ADFS sector write to the Phoenix block device; logs non-SD writes for visibility but allows them, with the NVMe PCIe device naturally protected by its unregistered write stub.

nodes.name: LoadDirectory
nodes.summary: Loads an ADFS directory from disc into a heap buffer, handling both old and new format including multi-extension BigDir reallocation up to DIRECTORY_MAX_SIZE.

nodes.name: IsDirectory
nodes.summary: Loads a disc object and validates its header magic (Hugo/Nick for E-format, SBPr/oven for BigDir) to determine whether the object at a given SIN is a directory, returning the parent SIN and directory name.

nodes.name: AddEntry
nodes.summary: Inserts a new entry into an ADFS directory in collated order, supporting both old E-format (fixed-size entries) and new E+ BigDir (variable-length name heap), with automatic directory extension for BigDir up to 4 MB.

nodes.name: AdjustNameHeap
nodes.summary: Adjusts the BigDir name heap by shifting entries and updating all name pointer fields when entries are inserted or removed.

nodes.name: FindEntry
nodes.summary: Searches an in-memory directory for a named entry using RISC OS collation order, returning the SIN or zero if not found.

nodes.name: GetI
nodes.summary: Reads a 1-4 byte little-endian integer from an unaligned byte offset in a disc buffer.

nodes.name: SetI
nodes.summary: Writes a 1-4 byte little-endian integer to an unaligned byte offset in a disc buffer.

nodes.name: GetS
nodes.summary: Reads a control-character-terminated or fixed-length ASCII string from a disc buffer, converting the RISC OS control-character terminator to a C null terminator.

nodes.name: filename_cmp
nodes.summary: Compares two ADFS filenames using the 256-entry RISC OS filer collation table (case-insensitive, extended-ASCII-aware), returning negative/zero/positive like strcmp.

nodes.name: BTSdioTypeA
nodes.summary: Main body of the BTSdioTypeA RISC OS C module: implements the CYW43455 Bluetooth-over-SDIO (func3, Type-A) driver for Phoenix OS, providing probe, firmware download, polled HCI RX, and the CMHG Init/Final entry points that register/deregister with the kernel SDIODriver SWI provider.
nodes.languageNotes: RISC OS C module using no .c extension (RISC OS directory convention c/FileName). AArch64-clean: all pointer-to-register casts use intptr_t. SWI calls via _kernel_swi/_swix. CMHG-generated module header supplies the Init/Final entry points.

nodes.name: bt_download_firmware
nodes.summary: Reads a binary BCM .hcd firmware patch from disc via OS_GBPB, walks its [opcode:2][plen:1][data] records, H4-wraps each as an HCI command (type 0x01), and sends them to the CYW43455 over SDIO func3 WriteBytes.

nodes.name: bt_irq
nodes.summary: Polled IRQ handler called from the WIMP loop; drains up to 16 Type-A RX frames from func3, parsing HCI event packets (type 0x04) and buffering all received data into the RX ring.

nodes.name: bt_wait_event
nodes.summary: Synchronously polls func3 for a single HCI event response, used during bring-up milestones (HCI Reset, Read Local BD_ADDR) before the polled RX loop is running.

nodes.name: bt_probe
nodes.summary: SDIO driver probe callback: allocates bt_priv state, enables func3, claims the polled IRQ, downloads the .hcd firmware, then executes the Phoenix milestone sequence (HCI Reset + Read Local BD_ADDR) and prints the Bluetooth MAC address.

nodes.name: Init
nodes.summary: CMHG module initialisation entry point: allocates RX and log ring buffers, then calls SDIODriver_RegisterDriver SWI to register the bt_id_table/bt_probe driver with the kernel SDIO provider.

nodes.name: Final
nodes.summary: CMHG module finalisation entry point: deregisters the driver from the kernel SDIO provider via SDIODriver_DeregisterDriver SWI.

nodes.name: SDIODriver
nodes.summary: Client-side ABI header for the Phoenix SDIODriver SWI provider (chunk 0x59000): defines the seven SWI numbers, the sdio_device_id, sdio_func, and sdio_driver structs that must match the kernel provider's layout byte-for-byte on AArch64.
nodes.languageNotes: 64-bit clean: sdio_driver carries function pointers as 8-byte fields on AArch64. This header mirrors drivers/sdio/sdiodriver.h in the Phoenix kernel; both sides must agree on struct layout across the SWI boundary.

nodes.name: BTSdioTypeAHdr
nodes.summary: CMunge (CMHG) module header declaring the BTSdioTypeA 64-bit RISC OS module entry table: specifies the module title, help string, and Init/Final as the only entry points (no start code, as 64-bit modules do not support it).
nodes.languageNotes: Processed by CMunge -64bit; comments go through the C preprocessor so apostrophes are forbidden. No module-is-runnable directive because CMunge -64bit has no 64-bit start code implementation.

nodes.name: .robuild.yaml
nodes.summary: build.riscos.online job descriptor for BTSdioTypeA: configures the aarch64 environment, sets RISC OS library paths, and runs riscos64-amu with BUILD64=1 to produce the rm64 AArch64 module artifact — though in practice AArch64 dispatch on the remote service is non-functional and local Docker builds are required.
nodes.languageNotes: The aarch64 environment on build.riscos.online currently lacks real AArch64 tools (as of Jun 2025); this file serves as reference only — local gerph/riscos-build:latest-64bit Docker builds are the actual build path.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS CModule Makefile for BTSdioTypeA: lists the CMHG header object first (o.BTSdioTypeAHdr) followed by the driver object (o.BTSdioTypeA), sets the include path to h/, and includes the shared CModule rules for AArch64 cross-compilation with BUILD64=1.

nodes.name: README-PHOENIX.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive Phoenix-port documentation for BTSdioTypeA: covers what changed from the Dec-2024 source, build instructions (local Docker only, not remote), deployment steps, hardware status (SDIO-BT transport is a dead end on CM4 — BT is wired to PL011 UART, not SDIO func3), and the planned pivot to BT-over-UART.

nodes.name: sdio.h
nodes.summary: Public interface header for the SlowArasan SDIO host driver. Declares the sdio_card_t state struct and all exported bus-access functions used by the WiFi and Bluetooth layers above.

nodes.name: sdiodriver.c
nodes.summary: Phoenix SDIODriver SWI provider (chunk 0x59000) that bridges the raw SDIO bus to RISC OS-style client modules such as BTSdioTypeA. Implements RegisterDriver, DeregisterDriver, EnableFunction, ReadBytes, WriteBytes, ClaimIRQ, and ReleaseIRQ SWIs using a polled model.

nodes.name: sdiodriver.h
nodes.summary: Shared ABI header for the Phoenix SDIODriver SWI interface. Defines SWI chunk numbers, sdio_device_id/sdio_func/sdio_driver structs, and sdio_irq_handler — compiled into both the kernel provider and client modules like BTSdioTypeA to ensure binary compatibility.
nodes.languageNotes: The PHOENIX_KERNEL guard splits kernel-internal entry points (sdiodriver_register, sdiodriver_probe_all, sdiodriver_poll, sdiodriver_swi) from the module-facing ABI, so the same header builds cleanly in both contexts.

nodes.name: sdiodriver_swi
nodes.summary: SWI dispatch handler for the SDIODriver chunk (0x59000). Routes offsets 0-6 to RegisterDriver, DeregisterDriver, EnableFunction, ReadBytes, WriteBytes, ClaimIRQ, and ReleaseIRQ implementations.

nodes.name: sdiodriver_probe_all
nodes.summary: Deferred probe runner called from kernel.c after WiFi initialisation. Scans SDIO functions for Bluetooth Type-A interface code (0x2) matching the registered driver's id_table, then calls the driver's probe callback.

nodes.name: sdiodriver_poll
nodes.summary: Polled IRQ service called from the WIMP task loop; invokes the registered client's IRQ handler if the function is enabled, driving BT receive speculatively.

nodes.name: sdiodriver_register
nodes.summary: Registers the SDIODriver SWI provider as a native kernel module at SWI chunk 0x59000 via module_register_native, making its SWIs callable by any RISC OS module.

nodes.name: arp.h
nodes.summary: ARP protocol constants (ARP_OP_REQUEST/REPLY, hardware/protocol types), the arp_hdr_t wire-format struct, and forward declarations of the public ARP API.

nodes.name: dhcp.h
nodes.summary: Public API declarations for the PhoenixDHCP module: state constants, the per-interface dhcp_set_target/dhcp_set_send overrides, DISCOVER/REQUEST/ACK lifecycle calls, and full lease query accessors (get_ip, get_gateway, get_dns, etc.).

nodes.name: genet_module.c
nodes.summary: Wraps the BCM GENET hardware driver as a RISC OS DCI4 network module, implementing all nine DCI4 SWI offsets, a filter registration list for future DCIShim integration, TX/RX statistics, and service broadcasts for DCIDRIVER_STARTING and DYING events.
nodes.languageNotes: The DCI4 filter list infrastructure is fully wired but handler dispatch is bypassed for now (no MbufManager); genet_module_rx() falls through to net_rx_frame() directly to keep the native TCP/IP stack functional until DCIShim is ready.

nodes.name: genet_module_init

nodes.name: do_scan
nodes.summary: Runs an HCI inquiry for ~12 seconds, deduplicates found device addresses, requests the remote friendly name for each, and populates the g_scan device list for subsequent pairing or L2CAP commands.

nodes.name: do_pair
nodes.summary: Drives the full SSP pairing state machine (Create Connection + HCI event dispatch for PIN, user-confirmation, passkey, and link-key events), stores the resulting bond key via hw_savekey, and auto-continues into do_hid() on success.

nodes.name: acl_open
nodes.summary: Opens an ACL link to a given Bluetooth address, optionally supplying the stored link key to authenticate; returns the HCI connection handle on success or 0 on failure.

nodes.name: l2cap_open
nodes.summary: Opens an L2CAP channel to the given PSM, handling both outgoing Connection Request and incoming Connection Request (device-initiated), correctly treating result=0x0001 as PENDING (not failure), completing configuration exchange, and returning the remote DCID on success.
nodes.languageNotes: Boot685 fix: the old `if (result) break` bail was replaced with a three-way branch on 0x0000 (success), 0x0001 (pending, keep looping), and >=0x02 (refused, break). Monotonic g_sig_id ensures unique signalling IDs per outstanding L2CAP request.

nodes.name: sdp_search
nodes.summary: Sends an SDP ServiceSearch request and iterates each returned record handle, querying ServiceClassIDList via sdp_class() and printing human-readable service names.

nodes.name: do_l2cap
nodes.summary: Implements the *BTL2CAP command: opens an ACL link then an L2CAP SDP channel to the selected scanned device and triggers full SDP service enumeration.

nodes.name: do_hid
