nodes.name: mmu.c
nodes.summary: AArch64 MMU initialisation for Phoenix OS: builds a flat identity-map page-table hierarchy (L1 1 GB blocks, L2 2 MB splits, L3 4 KB pages) covering Pi 4 and Pi 5 memory layouts including the Pi 5 NVMe PCIe window (l1_table[110] = 0x1B80000000, Device-mapped).
nodes.languageNotes: Inline assembly enables MMU/D-cache/I-cache in a single SCTLR_EL1 RMW after loading TTBR0/TTBR1. TLB invalidation uses TLBI VMALLE1IS (inner-shareable broadcast) for multi-core safety.

nodes.name: mmu_init
nodes.summary: Builds the AArch64 identity page-table hierarchy (L1/L2/L3), marks the .xhci_dma section Normal Non-Cacheable, GPU RAM Non-Cacheable, Pi 4/5 peripheral and PCIe windows Device-nGnRnE (including the Pi 5 NVMe window at l1_table[110] = 0x1B80000000), then programs MAIR/TCR/TTBR and enables MMU+caches in SCTLR_EL1.

nodes.name: mmu_tlb_invalidate_all
nodes.summary: Issues TLBI VMALLE1IS + DSB ISH + ISB to flush all TLB entries broadcast to all inner-shareable PEs.

nodes.name: mmu_tlb_invalidate_addr
nodes.summary: Invalidates the TLB entry for a single virtual address using TLBI VAE1IS.

nodes.name: periph_base.c
nodes.summary: Board-aware peripheral MMIO base detection — probes BCM2711 and BCM2712 System Timer CLO registers for liveness (requiring counter advancement, not just a non-zero read), sets peripheral_base and pi_model globals, and provides accessor functions for GPIO, UART, and Mailbox bases with Pi5 mailbox offset correction.

nodes.name: detect_peripheral_base
nodes.summary: Probes System Timer CLO at Pi4-low (0xFE003004), Pi4-high/CM4 (0x47E003004), and Pi5 (0x107C003004) addresses by requiring the counter to advance between two reads; sets peripheral_base and pi_model accordingly.

nodes.name: wdog_disable
nodes.summary: Disables the BCM2711 PM watchdog by writing zero to PM_WDOG and clearing the WRCFG field of PM_RSTC with the required 0x5A password, followed by a DSB barrier — called on Pi4/CM4 only before UART init to prevent USB enumeration timeouts from triggering a hardware reboot.

nodes.name: get_mailbox_base
nodes.summary: Returns the VideoCore mailbox MMIO base, selecting offset 0x13880 for Pi5 (BCM2712) or 0xB880 for Pi4/CM4 (BCM2711) relative to peripheral_base.

nodes.name: irq.c
nodes.summary: BCM2711/BCM2712 GIC-400 (GICv2) interrupt controller driver that initialises the distributor and CPU interface, manages the IRQ handler table, and dispatches interrupts from the AArch64 EL1 exception vector. Supports board-aware GIC base address selection at runtime (Pi 4 defaults vs Pi 5 hard-coded addresses) and includes SGI/IPI support for future SMP use.

nodes.name: irq_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the complete interrupt subsystem: clears the handler table, selects the correct GIC base address (Pi 5 hard-coded, Pi 4 from DT or default), then calls gicd_init() and gicc_init() to configure hardware.

nodes.name: irq_dispatch
nodes.summary: Called from the AArch64 EL1 IRQ exception vector; reads GICC_IAR to acknowledge the interrupt, looks up and calls the registered C handler, then writes GICC_EOIR to signal end-of-interrupt.

nodes.name: irq_set_handler
nodes.summary: Registers a C handler function and private data pointer for a given GIC IRQ vector number in the software handler table.

nodes.name: send_ipi
nodes.summary: Sends a Software Generated Interrupt (SGI) to a bitmask of target CPUs by writing GICD_SGIR; used for future SMP inter-processor communication.

nodes.name: nvme.c
nodes.summary: NVMe PCIe SSD controller driver for Phoenix OS supporting both BCM2711 (Pi4/CM4) and BCM2712 (Pi5) with board-aware DMA offsets; initialises admin and I/O queues, performs IDENTIFY, and registers the drive as a native-sector block device.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AArch64 inline assembly (dsb sy, mrs cntpct_el0) for memory barriers and cycle-count polling; g_nvme_dma_offset is selected at runtime via get_pi_model() so a single binary runs on Pi4/CM4 (0xC0000000) and Pi5 (0x10_00000000).

nodes.name: nvme_init_controller
nodes.summary: Full 5-stage NVMe controller bring-up: board-aware DMA offset selection, CAP/VS probe, admin queue setup, controller enable, IDENTIFY (controller + namespace), I/O queue creation, LBA-0 read, and blockdev registration.

nodes.name: nvme_submit
nodes.summary: Submits a single NVMe command to a queue's submission ring, rings the SQ doorbell, then poll-waits on the completion queue using phase-bit tracking; returns 0 on success or -1 on error/timeout.

nodes.name: nvme_create_io_queue
nodes.summary: Creates the I/O completion and submission queue pair (QID 1) via admin CREATE_IO_CQ and CREATE_IO_SQ commands and wires up the doorbell pointers.

nodes.name: nvme_read_native
nodes.summary: Reads an arbitrary count of native-sized NVMe blocks from a given LBA into a caller buffer, chunking transfers to fit within the 4 KB PRP page limit.

nodes.name: nvme_write_native
nodes.summary: Writes an arbitrary count of native-sized blocks at a given LBA from a caller buffer, chunking to the 4 KB PRP limit and copying through the NC DMA bounce buffer.

nodes.name: nvme_wait_ready
nodes.summary: Polls CSTS.RDY until it reaches the desired state (0 or 1) or a 5-second timeout expires, returning -1 if the controller signals a fatal status.

nodes.name: nvme_read_blocks
nodes.summary: Public block-read stub returning ENOSYS; the functional path goes through the blockdev interface registered in nvme_init_controller.

nodes.name: nvme_write_blocks
nodes.summary: Public block-write stub returning ENOSYS; the functional path goes through the blockdev interface registered in nvme_init_controller.

nodes.name: usb_init.c
nodes.summary: USB subsystem initializer that sequences class driver registration (hub, HID, mass storage, keyboard, mouse) before triggering the xHCI port scan, then conditionally initializes the DWC2 OTG controller — skipping it on Pi5 where all USB is routed through RP1 xHCI.

nodes.name: usb_xhci.c
nodes.summary: Full xHCI host controller driver targeting the VL805 PCIe chip on Pi 4 and RP1 xHCI1 on Pi 5. Handles DMA ring setup (DCBAA, command ring, event ring, scratchpad), controller startup with HSE-retry logic, device enumeration, endpoint configuration, and polled control/bulk/interrupt transfers. Encodes hard-won knowledge from 94+ boot iterations diagnosing VL805 DMA coherency, ERSTBA, and command-ring sequencing issues.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AArch64 inline assembly extensively (cntpct_el0, dsb sy, isb, AT S1E1R) for cycle-counter timing, memory barriers, and MMU page-table attribute self-checks. Dual-mode (VL805/BCM2711 vs RP1/Pi5) controlled by g_xhci_is_rp1 set at init time.

nodes.name: usb_init
nodes.summary: Sequenced USB subsystem initializer: registers hub, HID, mass-storage, keyboard, and mouse class drivers via weak-linked calls, triggers the deferred xHCI port scan, then conditionally initializes DWC2 OTG (skipped on Pi5 where all USB goes through RP1 xHCI). Prints the block device table on completion.

nodes.name: xhci_init
nodes.summary: Top-level xHCI controller initializer: selects Pi4/Pi5 DMA buffer and offset, zero-inits the DMA region, performs MMU attribute self-check (AT S1E1R), sequences read_caps/do_reset/setup_dcbaa/setup_cmd_ring/setup_event_ring/run_controller, registers HC ops, and verifies MFINDEX post-scan. Encapsulates all VL805/RP1 hardware bring-up.

nodes.name: run_controller
nodes.summary: Programs all xHCI ring pointers into hardware (Linux order: ERSTSZ then ERSTBA then ERDP), starts the controller with RS=1, performs a 3-second HSE-retry loop until TRUE RUNNING, sends a No-op keepalive command to satisfy the VL805 MCU watchdog, powers ports, and runs a 400 ms settle loop with per-iteration ring re-arm on HSE events.

nodes.name: setup_dcbaa
nodes.summary: Allocates and initializes the Device Context Base Address Array and scratchpad pages in DMA memory. Writes DCBAA pointer to OP_DCBAAP. Includes diagnostic canary patterns (BOOT92) for MCU DMA-write verification.

nodes.name: setup_event_ring
nodes.summary: Sets up the xHCI event ring and ERST in DMA memory, computing correct DMA addresses (fixing the boot89 ERSTBA=0 bug). Also writes a fallback ERST to physical address 0 for belt-and-suspenders compatibility with early VL805 firmware behavior.

nodes.name: xhci_scan_ports
nodes.summary: Deferred port scan entry point called from usb_init() after class drivers are registered, ensuring usb_enumerate_device() can bind drivers to newly discovered devices.

nodes.name: xhci_configure_endpoints
nodes.summary: Issues xHCI Configure Endpoint commands for all bulk and interrupt-IN endpoints on a device after config descriptor parsing. Allocates per-slot transfer rings in DMA memory and stores slot_id in ep->slot_id so xhci_bulk_transfer can locate them.

nodes.name: xhci_ep_recover
nodes.summary: Recovers a halted xHCI endpoint: issues Reset Endpoint then Configure Endpoint (masked to Halted DCIs only) to restore the device to operational state without corrupting running endpoints.

nodes.name: xhci_enumerate_hub_port
nodes.summary: Enumerates a device plugged into a USB hub port: performs port reset via Set Port Feature, issues Enable Slot and Address Device commands with hub TT context, retrieves the device descriptor, and calls usb_enumerate_device().

nodes.name: xhci_enumerate_device
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around usb_enumerate_device() that supplies the xHCI control-transfer ops; bridges the xHCI layer to the generic USB enumeration stack.

nodes.name: xhci_control_transfer
nodes.summary: Executes a USB control transfer using xHCI Setup/Data/Status TRBs on EP0 of the given device slot. Handles both IN and OUT data phases, waits for Transfer Event CCEs, and returns bytes transferred or a negative error code.

nodes.name: xhci_bulk_transfer
nodes.summary: Executes a USB bulk transfer using xHCI Normal TRBs on a pre-configured bulk endpoint. Splits large buffers across multiple TRBs, rings the endpoint doorbell, and polls for Transfer Event completion with configurable timeout.

nodes.name: xhci_interrupt_transfer
nodes.summary: Executes a USB interrupt IN transfer for HID polling. Supports timeout=0 (non-blocking event ring check), short timeout (mouse), and longer timeout (keyboard). Handles xHCI Stopped endpoint recovery (CC=13) by re-arming the TRB without resetting the endpoint.

nodes.name: xhci_irq_handler
nodes.summary: GIC interrupt handler for xHCI MSI events (INTID 180). Increments msi_fire_count for diagnostic tracking. On BCM2711/VL805 this path is non-functional (GIC delivery confirmed broken); actual event processing uses pure polling in xhci_wait_event.

nodes.name: xhci_disconnect_hub_child
nodes.summary: Handles disconnect of a device attached to a hub port: stops and disables the xHCI slot, calls hid_device_disconnect to remove HID poll entries, and frees per-slot resources.

nodes.name: xhci_check_hotplug
nodes.summary: Polls the xHCI event ring for Port Status Change Events and responds to device connect/disconnect at root hub ports. Called periodically from the kernel loop to provide hot-plug support.

nodes.name: genet.c
nodes.summary: Bare-metal BCM2711 GENETv5 GigE MAC driver for Phoenix OS (Pi 4/CM4), providing polling-mode TX/RX with direct MMIO, MDIO PHY management, cache-coherency maintenance, and transparent dispatch to the RP1 Cadence GEM driver on Pi 5.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AArch64 inline assembly for cache maintenance (DC CVAC/CIVAC) and system counter reads (CNTPCT_EL0/CNTFRQ_EL0); all DMA buffers are statically allocated with 64-byte alignment to match Cortex-A72 cache line size.

nodes.name: genet_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the BCM2711 GENETv5 MAC: verifies hardware revision, reads board MAC address via VideoCore mailbox, configures RGMII-ID PHY mode, resets UMAC, programs MAC address, sets up DMA rings, masks interrupts, enables TX/RX, and starts PHY autonegotiation.

nodes.name: genet_apply_link
nodes.summary: Reads PHY-negotiated link speed via MDIO and programs UMAC_CMD speed field and RGMII_LINK assertion to match; must be called when physical link comes up to ungate the MAC data path and allow RDMA to advance.

nodes.name: genet_send
nodes.summary: Transmits one Ethernet frame by copying it into a static TX DMA buffer, flushing the D-cache to ensure TDMA reads actual frame data from DRAM, and advancing the TX producer index to kick the DMA engine.

nodes.name: genet_poll_rx
nodes.summary: Polls the RDMA ring for one received Ethernet frame, invalidates D-cache before reading descriptor status, copies the frame payload (skipping the 2-byte IP-alignment prefix), and advances the consumer index; always advances the ring even on error frames to prevent stalls.

nodes.name: genet_reset
nodes.summary: Soft-resets the GENET UMAC and RX/TX paths: flushes the RX buffer, issues a 200 µs UMAC core reset, clears MIB counters, sets max frame length, and programs RBUF_CTRL to the exact working value (ALIGN_2B only) discovered empirically.

nodes.name: genet_init_rings
nodes.summary: Initializes TX and RX DMA descriptor rings: disables RDMA first to avoid races with stale bootloader state, programs ring size, buffer size, start/end addresses, burst size, and populates all RX descriptor slots with static buffer addresses before enabling DMA.

nodes.name: genet_phy_init
nodes.summary: Verifies the BCM54213PE PHY is present via MDIO ID registers, issues a PHY reset, and enables autonegotiation.

nodes.name: genet_setup_rxfilter
nodes.summary: Programs the MAC destination filter with the board unicast MAC and broadcast address, then disables the MDF hardware filter (MDF_CTRL=0) and sets PROMISC mode in UMAC_CMD so all frames reach RDMA.

nodes.name: genet_link_up
nodes.summary: Returns 1 if the PHY reports link status via BMSR (read twice to clear latched-low bit); dispatches to rp1_gem_link_up on Pi 5.

nodes.name: genet_rx_available
nodes.summary: Returns the number of frames currently queued in the RDMA ring by comparing hardware producer index against the software consumer index; dispatches to rp1_gem_rx_available on Pi 5.

nodes.name: genet_delay_us
nodes.summary: Busy-waits for the specified number of microseconds using the AArch64 system counter (CNTPCT_EL0) at the hardware-reported frequency.

nodes.name: exceptions.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 exception vector table and handlers for Phoenix OS, including the #147 nesting-aware SVC stack switch in exc_sync_handler, the IRQ context-save/restore path, and UART crash-dump helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses system registers TPIDRRO_EL0 and FAR_EL1 as scratch stashes to defer stack use until the SVC identity is confirmed; the 176→192 byte frame growth adds caller-SP and x18 slots at [176]/[184] to support the cross-stack return discipline.

nodes.name: exc_sync_handler
nodes.summary: EL1 synchronous exception entry point that performs an EC==0x15 check, switches to the dedicated SVC stack (or continues nested), saves the 192-byte register frame, dispatches to exc_svc_dispatch, restores caller SP before GPRs, then ERETs.

nodes.name: exc_irq_handler
nodes.summary: EL1 IRQ entry point that saves a 176-byte caller-saved register frame, calls irq_dispatch(0) in C, restores all saved registers, and ERETs to the interrupted code.

nodes.name: exc_handler
nodes.summary: Generic unexpected-exception handler that saves x0–x3, reads ESR/ELR/FAR/SP, writes them to a fixed scratchpad at 0x8F200, prints a crash banner over UART, then enters the LED blink-halt loop.

nodes.name: exc_svc.c
nodes.summary: C bridge between the assembly SVC exception handler and the kernel SWI dispatch layer; unpacks the 192-byte register frame into a uint32_t regs[10] array, calls swi_dispatch(), writes results back, and propagates RISC OS V/C flag conventions into SPSR_EL1.
nodes.languageNotes: g_svc_ceiling (uint64_t, initially 0) is the cross-file coordination point between this file and aif.c for the #147 dedicated SVC stack; 0 is treated as 'use __svc_stack_top' so BSS zero-init is correct-by-default.

nodes.name: exc_svc_dispatch
nodes.summary: SVC C bridge called from exc_sync_handler with the register frame pointer and decoded SWI number; handles OS_WriteS and OS_WriteI inline (needing ELR access), routes all other SWIs through swi_dispatch(), and sets the V/C flags in SPSR_EL1 from the return code and g_swi_carry.

nodes.name: vec_call.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 assembly trampoline that calls external vector claimants following the VECTOR_PLAN §3 low-level convention (x0 = register-block pointer, x1 = next-dispatch address, x12 = private word), decoding the return into VEC_CLAIM/VEC_PASS/VEC_EXT_BADCONV/-1, plus two hand-written §3 test claimants used by the vector self-test.
nodes.languageNotes: Clears NZCV before the call so stale V cannot be mistaken for an error return from a CMunge 0.84 veneer; saves only x19-x22 across the blr since §3 permits x1-x15 to be corrupted by the callee.

nodes.name: vec_dispatch_external
nodes.summary: AArch64 assembly trampoline that marshals the VECTOR_PLAN §3 entry conditions, calls an external claimant, then decodes x0/V into VEC_CLAIM (0), VEC_PASS (1), VEC_EXT_BADCONV (-2), or -1 on error (block pointer stored via err_out).

nodes.name: vec_test_external_pass
nodes.summary: Hand-written §3 test claimant that increments R1 in the register block to prove in-place block access and returns pass-on by preserving x0 (the block pointer).

nodes.name: vec_test_external_claim
nodes.summary: Hand-written §3 test claimant that increments R1, writes fingerprint 0x5A to R2, then returns claim by setting x0=0 — serves as a reference for what a correct A64 vector-claim veneer should look like.

nodes.name: fileswitch.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the public FileSwitch API (fs_find, fs_gbpb, fs_bget, fs_bput, fs_args, fs_control, fs_file) with FS handle count constants and RISC OS OS_Find mode flags.

nodes.name: uart.c
nodes.summary: Debug UART driver supporting Pi4 PL011 and Pi5 16550-compatible uart10 at 0x107D001000; provides uart_init(), uart_putc()/puts(), uart_getc(), and tx-busy query used by the kernel debug print path.
nodes.languageNotes: Runtime hardware selection via get_pi_model()/get_uart_base() avoids separate Pi4/Pi5 binaries; the Pi5 uses uart10 (not the Bluetooth uarta) to avoid firmware conflicts.

nodes.name: uart_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the debug UART: detects Pi model, selects the correct base address, configures GPIO mux for Tx/Rx pins, then programs baud-rate divisor and line-control registers for 115200 8N1.

nodes.name: uart_putc
nodes.summary: Transmits a single character over the debug UART, blocking until the TX FIFO has space; expands LF to CRLF for terminal compatibility.

nodes.name: uart_tx_busy
nodes.summary: Returns non-zero if the UART transmitter is still busy (TX FIFO not empty), used by callers that need to drain before taking action.

nodes.name: uart_drain
nodes.summary: Busy-waits until the UART transmit FIFO is fully drained, ensuring all pending debug output is committed before a halt or reboot.

nodes.name: uart_puts
nodes.summary: Transmits a null-terminated string over the debug UART by calling uart_putc() for each byte.

nodes.name: uart_getc
nodes.summary: Non-blocking receive: reads one byte from the UART RX FIFO, returning -1 if no data is available.

nodes.name: uart_set_quiet
nodes.summary: Sets a quiet flag that suppresses UART output, used to silence the debug console during sensitive operations.

nodes.name: HANDOFF.md
nodes.summary: Root-level engineering handoff document summarizing the current state of Phoenix OS for new contributors, including what was completed in the latest arc (native PCIe NVMe SAVE), the next session's starting point, hardware setup, memory map, SWI implementation status, key source files, and a rolling changelog of recent boot sessions.
nodes.languageNotes: 36 sections across 435 lines covering boot sessions boot516 through boot599a. Tracks progress by boot-counter numbers (e.g., boot520, boot577) which serve as build/session identifiers. Complements docs/HANDOFF.md as the root-level copy.

nodes.name: os_swi.c
nodes.summary: Central SWI dispatch hub for Phoenix OS (~6268 lines): implements the full RISC OS OS_ SWI API surface including I/O, clocks, filesystem (FileCore/FAT32), WIMP, dynamic areas, modules, vectors, sound, I2C, networking, and CLI (*-command) dispatch. The monolithic os_swi_handler function (~4741 lines) is the single entry point for all SWI calls routed through the kernel.
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the RISC OS SWI dispatch convention: a single handler function switches on SWI offset and writes results back through a register array (regs[0..9]). The -4 flag in OS_ReadVarVal is the PRM-documented GSTrans flag, not a bug.

nodes.name: mode_variable
nodes.summary: Returns a VDU mode variable value (pixel size, bits-per-pixel, screen dimensions, etc.) for the current screen mode, implementing OS_ReadModeVariable semantics.

nodes.name: input_pump
nodes.summary: Polls all input and peripheral subsystems (HID USB, Bluetooth HID, serial keyboard, PCIe xHCI, HDMI audio DMA, network, mouse cursor) and dispatches pending events. Called periodically as the OS idle/event pump.

nodes.name: osswi_selftest
nodes.summary: Runs a smoke-test suite against os_swi_handler, exercising OS_ReadSysInfo and OS_ReadVarVal calls to verify the SWI dispatch path is working.

nodes.name: var_read_test
nodes.summary: Exercises OS_ReadVarVal (including the GSTrans/-4 flag path) and prints diagnostic output, used to verify system variable reading and GSTrans translation.

nodes.name: gs_parse_number
nodes.summary: Parses a decimal or hexadecimal number from a GSTrans source string, returning the parsed value and number of characters consumed.

nodes.name: gs_translate
nodes.summary: Implements GSTrans (General String Translate): expands pipe sequences (|A, |!), inline decimal/hex escapes (|@N), and system variable references (|<varname>) in the source string, writing the translated result to a destination buffer.

nodes.name: clock_set_cs
nodes.summary: Stores the current ARM system counter (CNTPCT) as the reference epoch for the centisecond-based software clock.

nodes.name: clock_get_cs
nodes.summary: Returns elapsed centiseconds since the reference epoch by reading CNTPCT/CNTFRQ and computing the delta from the stored epoch.

nodes.name: clock_is_set
nodes.summary: Returns non-zero if the real-time clock has been synchronised (e.g. via NTP or RTC read).

nodes.name: os_time_unix
nodes.summary: Returns the current time as a Unix timestamp by combining the software centisecond clock with the hardware RTC register (available on Pi 5) or the stored epoch.

nodes.name: ro_year_is_leap
nodes.summary: Returns non-zero if the given year (as counted from 1900) is a Gregorian leap year.

nodes.name: ro_fields_to_unix
nodes.summary: Converts broken-down calendar fields (year, month, day, hour, minute, second) to a Unix timestamp, handling leap-year day accumulation.

nodes.name: ro_unix_to_fields
nodes.summary: Converts a Unix timestamp to broken-down calendar fields (year, month, day-of-month, hour, minute, second, weekday) using Gregorian calendar arithmetic.

nodes.name: ro_break_time
nodes.summary: Converts a RISC OS 5-byte centisecond timestamp into a broken-down time structure (year, month, day, hour, minute, second) using the RISC OS epoch (1 Jan 1900).

nodes.name: ro_format_time
nodes.summary: Formats a broken-down RISC OS time structure into a string using a format template (e.g. for OS_ConvertDateAndTime), emitting day/month/year/hour/minute/second fields.

nodes.name: sysvar_build
nodes.summary: Builds and registers the Sys$Time and Sys$Date system variables by reading the current clock and formatting the RISC OS timestamp strings.

nodes.name: sysvars_register_time
nodes.summary: Registers the Sys$Time and Sys$Date system variables via OS_SetVarVal SWI calls, initialising the RISC OS time system-variable subsystem.

nodes.name: sysvar_set_string
nodes.summary: Sets a named RISC OS system variable to a string value by invoking OS_SetVarVal (SWI offset 24), with diagnostic logging on failure.

nodes.name: sysvars_set_font_path
nodes.summary: Sets the Font$Path and Font$Prefix system variables to the OS font directory, making the font subsystem discoverable at startup.

nodes.name: os_iicop
nodes.summary: Implements OS_IICOperate: validates and executes one or more I2C bus transfer operations (read/write sequences) by calling the i2c driver, implementing the RISC OS IIC multi-operation protocol.

nodes.name: os_read_unsigned_parse
nodes.summary: Parses an unsigned integer from a string according to OS_ReadUnsigned semantics: supports decimal, hexadecimal (&), binary (%), and base-prefixed (%N) notations with overflow detection.

nodes.name: os_swi_handler
nodes.summary: The central OS SWI dispatch function (~4741 lines): a large switch on SWI offset implementing 30+ OS_ calls including OS_WriteC/WriteS/Write0, OS_ReadC, OS_GetEnv, OS_CLI, OS_Byte, OS_Word, OS_File, OS_Args, OS_BGet/BPut, OS_GBPB, OS_Find, OS_Control, OS_ReadVarVal/SetVarVal, OS_ReadUnsigned, OS_Plot, OS_SpriteOp, OS_DynamicArea, OS_Module, OS_ServiceCall, OS_CallAVector/AddToVector, OS_ReadModeVariable, OS_ReadSysInfo, OS_ConvertDateAndTime, OS_IICOperate, WIMP SWI routing, FileCore SWI routing, Font SWI routing, Sound SWI routing, and Phoenix-specific diagnostics.

nodes.name: os_swi_register
nodes.summary: Registers the OS SWI chunk with the kernel module system via module_register_native, then assigns SWI name strings for OS_SWINumberFromString/OS_SWINumberToString lookups.

nodes.name: filecore.c
nodes.summary: Port of RISC OS FileCore disc filing system kernel, handling new-map disc format parsing, MBR/GPT partitioning, directory enumeration, file read/write, and NVMe 4K-native sector translation for the Phoenix AArch64 OS.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the RISC OS ADFS new-map format: zone-based bit-addressed free-space maps, Hugo-format directories, indirect addressing (IDA) chains, and a multi-zone disc record layout — all adapted for 4K-native NVMe sectors.

nodes.name: filecore_disc_find
nodes.summary: Searches the registered disc table for a disc whose name matches the given string, returning its index or -1.

nodes.name: filecore_bind_disc
nodes.summary: Binds a disc index as the current active disc, tearing down the previous disc context and re-initialising the disc record state.

nodes.name: filecore_bind_disc_name
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that resolves a disc by name and then calls filecore_bind_disc to make it active.

nodes.name: filecore_init
nodes.summary: Initialises FileCore for one block device: reads the MBR/GPT, locates the ADFS disc record in boot block or zone 0, parses zone headers and the disc map, and populates the internal disc descriptor table.

nodes.name: filecore_add_discs
nodes.summary: Iterates all registered block devices, calls filecore_init on each, and binds the first successfully initialised ADFS disc as the boot disc.

nodes.name: filecore_list_root
nodes.summary: Large diagnostic/enumeration routine that walks all map zones, resolves indirection cells, reads Hugo-format directory sectors, and dumps every root directory entry with its SIN, load/exec addresses, and size.

nodes.name: adfs_read_bits
nodes.summary: Reads an arbitrary-width bit field from a byte buffer at a given bit offset, used to extract new-map indirection cell fields.

nodes.name: filecore_populate_root_cache_dr
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the root directory from disc for the currently bound disc, then populates the in-memory root directory cache.

nodes.name: filecore_get_root_entry
nodes.summary: Returns a cached root directory entry by index, refreshing the cache if it is empty.

nodes.name: filecore_root_cache_add
nodes.summary: Appends a new entry to the root directory cache, storing name, SIN, size, directory flag, and load/exec attributes.

nodes.name: filecore_get_child_entry
nodes.summary: Resolves and returns a directory entry by index within a given directory SIN, walking the ADFS chain to read directory sectors and caching entries on first access.

nodes.name: filecore_show_results
nodes.summary: Diagnostic routine that prints all cached root directory entries with their attributes to the UART console.

nodes.name: filecore_find_path
nodes.summary: Resolves a colon-prefixed ADFS path into a directory entry, walking the directory hierarchy component by component and returning the final entry.

nodes.name: filecore_save_open
nodes.summary: Opens an existing file for the save operation by resolving the path, returning its SIN, capacity, parent SIN, and load/exec attributes along with the leaf name.

nodes.name: filecore_resolve_parent
nodes.summary: Resolves the parent directory of a given path, returning the parent SIN and extracting the leaf name for use during file creation.

nodes.name: filecore_exec_obey
nodes.summary: Executes an Obey script loaded into a buffer, splitting it into lines and dispatching each non-comment line through obey_exec_line.

nodes.name: filecore_sd_write_test
nodes.summary: Test routine that writes a known pattern to a specific disc sector and reads it back to verify correct write-through on the SD/NVMe block device.

nodes.name: filecore_sd_save_test
nodes.summary: Test routine that saves a small file to the ADFS disc by locating a free directory slot, allocating map space, and writing content sectors.

nodes.name: filecore_bootdisc_write_test
nodes.summary: Test that writes to sectors on the boot disc and verifies the data survives a rebind cycle, exercising the full disc record re-init path.

nodes.name: filecore_multidisc_test
nodes.summary: Exercises multi-disc support by binding each registered disc in turn, reading its disc record, and verifying the disc name is accessible.

nodes.name: filecore_dr_find_path
nodes.summary: Variant of filecore_find_path that searches across all registered discs rather than only the currently bound disc, returning the SIN and size of the resolved entry.

nodes.name: filecore_dr_resolve_parent
nodes.summary: Multi-disc variant of filecore_resolve_parent that searches all registered discs for an existing file and resolves the target parent directory SIN.

nodes.name: filecore_cat_print
nodes.summary: Implements the *CAT command by reading directory contents for a given path argument and printing each entry's name and attributes to the console.

nodes.name: filecore_resolve_path
nodes.summary: Strips the disc specifier prefix from a full ADFS path, optionally binding the named disc, and returns the remaining path tail.

nodes.name: discinfo_swi
nodes.summary: SWI handler for the DiscInfo software interrupt, dispatching on the reason code to return disc name, disc count, or disc record fields into caller registers.

nodes.name: discinfo_register
nodes.summary: Registers the DiscInfo SWI handler with the kernel SWI dispatch table.

nodes.name: fc_log_discrec
nodes.summary: Dumps all fields of a disc record structure to the UART log, used for diagnostic verification of disc record parsing.

nodes.name: fc_try_boot_discrec
nodes.summary: Attempts to read and validate the ADFS disc record from the boot block at LBA 0 or 1, checking plausibility and checksum before accepting it.

nodes.name: fc_try_zone0_discrec
nodes.summary: Attempts to read and validate the disc record embedded in zone 0 of the new-map, used when no separate boot block exists.

nodes.name: filecore_parse_mbr
nodes.summary: Parses a Master Boot Record sector to enumerate partition entries, identifies ADFS and FAT partition types, and returns the LBA base and sector count of the first ADFS partition found.

nodes.name: fc_read_zone_discrec
nodes.summary: Reads the disc record from a specific new-map zone header and validates it, logging the result on success.

nodes.name: fc_scan_gpt
nodes.summary: Parses a GUID Partition Table to locate ADFS partitions, scanning each GPT entry for a matching partition type GUID and attempting to read the ADFS disc record.

nodes.name: fc_bit_addr_to_data_lba
nodes.summary: Converts a new-map bit address (fragment + offset within zone) to an absolute disc LBA by computing the zone base and scaling by sectors-per-logical-fragment.

nodes.name: fc_ida_to_data_lba
nodes.summary: Resolves a new-map IDA (indirect disc address) to an absolute LBA by locating the fragment in the zone free-space map, following indirection chains if present, and applying the sector-per-fragment scale factor.

nodes.name: adfs_dump_hugo_dir
nodes.summary: Diagnostic function that dumps the tail header of a Hugo-format ADFS directory sector including the start and end masters, directory title, and sequence number.

nodes.name: filecore_populate_root_cache
nodes.summary: Parses a Hugo-format directory sector and populates the root directory cache with entries for all valid files and subdirectories found.

nodes.name: filecore_step6_load_module
nodes.summary: Implements the stage-6 boot step that searches well-known module directories on the ADFS disc, resolves each module file's data LBA, reads it into memory, and registers it with the kernel module subsystem.

nodes.name: fc_load_one_entry
nodes.summary: Reads the data for a single directory entry from disc using its IDA, loading the file content into a kernel-allocated buffer.

nodes.name: fc_try_load_modules_from_dir
nodes.summary: Scans a given directory SIN for files with module-compatible load/exec addresses and attempts to load each as a kernel module.

nodes.name: adfs_chain_traverse
nodes.summary: Traverses an ADFS fragment chain from a given SIN and offset, following new-map indirection cells across zones to collect all constituent LBAs of a file or directory.

nodes.name: adfs_hugo_brute_scan
nodes.summary: Brute-force scans a range of disc LBAs looking for sectors with valid Hugo directory tail signatures, used for recovery or diagnostic purposes.

nodes.name: obey_exec_line
nodes.summary: Parses and executes a single line of an Obey script, dispatching built-in keywords (Set, Echo, Run, Error, RMLoad) and variable substitution.

nodes.name: obey_var_set
nodes.summary: Sets an Obey script variable in the kernel environment variable table, creating or updating the name-value pair.

nodes.name: sdio_wifi.c
nodes.summary: CYW43455 WiFi protocol driver: implements WPA2 association (wifi_join), SDPCM/BCDC frame transport, DHCP client (wifi_dhcp_run), CLM regulatory blob upload, and the wifictl SWI/module registration entry point.
nodes.languageNotes: wifi_join spans 468 lines handling the full 802.11 auth/assoc/4-way-handshake state machine; SDPCM credit flow-control is polled rather than interrupt-driven.

nodes.name: sdio.c
nodes.summary: SDIO host controller core: implements CMD52 single-byte register I/O, CMD53 bulk DMA transfer, Arasan clock programming, bus probe/enumeration, and 1-bit/4-bit bus width negotiation.
nodes.languageNotes: sdio_print_info is an enormous 465-line diagnostic dump covering all CCCR/FBR/CIS registers; sdio_cmd53_setup/finish split the DMA handshake into two callable phases.

nodes.name: sdio_fw.c
nodes.summary: CYW43455 firmware blob management: loads the main firmware image and NVRAM into chip RAM via backplane window writes, resets and activates the ARM Cortex-R4 and D11 MAC cores, and patches the MAC address from the VideoCore mailbox.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a dual path for RAM writes: DMA-to-eMMC (Pi4/CM4) or raw CMD53 (Pi5), selected at runtime by get_pi_model().

nodes.name: sdhci_brcmstb.c
nodes.summary: Pi5 RP1 SDHCI host controller glue: maps the RP1 MMIO region (0x1001100000), configures GPIO pin mux and pull resistors for the WiFi SDIO bus, manages WL_ON assertion, and selects antenna via the RP1 GPIO expander.
nodes.languageNotes: Pi5-specific throughout; uses ioremap to the RP1 peripheral base at 0x1001100000 rather than the BCM2711 GPIO base used by earlier Pi models.

nodes.name: wifi_join
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full WPA2 association sequence: loads config, sets country/CLM, programs security IEs, issues SCAN+JOIN iovar, drives the 4-way EAPOL handshake via SDPCM event polling, and returns with the link up.

nodes.name: wifi_dhcp_run
nodes.summary: Runs the DHCP client loop after association: injects DISCOVER/REQUEST, polls wifi_poll_rx for OFFER/ACK frames, and returns once a lease is bound.

nodes.name: bcdc_iovar
nodes.summary: Core BCDC/SDPCM iovar transport: wraps a get or set request in a BCDC header, sends it via CMD53 write, then polls for the firmware response frame handling intervening async events.

nodes.name: sdpcm_handle_event
nodes.summary: Parses an SDPCM async event frame and dispatches it to the wifi_evt ring buffer, handling auth, assoc, EAPOL, and disassoc event types.

nodes.name: sdpcm_rx_frame
nodes.summary: Reads one SDPCM frame from the chip via CMD53, validates the sequence/len headers, updates the host-side credit counter, and returns the payload buffer.

nodes.name: wifi_dump_fw_console
nodes.summary: Reads the firmware's in-chip debug console ring buffer via backplane window access and prints its content to the host UART or kernel console.

nodes.name: wifi_print_fw_console
nodes.summary: Formats and prints one previously captured firmware console log entry using con_printf.

nodes.name: wifi_wait_fwready
nodes.summary: Polls the chip's SDIO readiness flags after firmware download completes, enables the SDPCM bus layer, and configures the flow-control watermarks.

nodes.name: wifi_clm_load
nodes.summary: Reads the CLM regulatory database blob from the board firmware file and uploads it to the chip via the clmload iovar in chunks.

nodes.name: wifi_cfg_load
nodes.summary: Parses the WiFi configuration file (SSID, passphrase, country) from the firmware file system and also accepts kernel command-line overrides via dt_cmdline_key.

nodes.name: wifi_scan_probe
nodes.summary: Issues an active scan iovar and collects BSSID probe results from SDPCM scan events, building a list of visible APs.

nodes.name: wifi_send_ethernet
nodes.summary: Wraps a raw Ethernet frame in an SDPCM+BCDH header and transmits it to the chip via CMD53 write after awaiting a TX credit.

nodes.name: wifi_poll_rx
nodes.summary: Polls the chip for a pending data frame: reads the mailbox, triggers CMD53 read if data is pending, strips SDPCM/BCDC headers, and returns the Ethernet payload.

nodes.name: wifi_net_poll
nodes.summary: Public receive polling entry point called by the network stack: drains one received Ethernet frame and delivers it to net_rx_frame.

nodes.name: wifi_scan_now
nodes.summary: Console command handler that triggers an active scan and prints the results.

nodes.name: wifi_rejoin
nodes.summary: Console command handler that tears down the current association and performs a fresh wifi_join followed by wifi_dhcp_run.

nodes.name: sdio_wifi_init
nodes.summary: Top-level WiFi initialization: waits for SDPCM bus readiness, enables SDIO function 2, calls wifi_join to associate, then starts DHCP.

nodes.name: wifictl_swi
nodes.summary: SWI dispatcher for the wifictl module: decodes the offset field and routes to wifi_scan_now or wifi_rejoin.

nodes.name: wifictl_register
nodes.summary: Registers the wifictl native module with the kernel module registry at startup.

nodes.name: sdio_send_cmd
nodes.summary: Issues a raw SD command to the Arasan host controller: writes argument and command/transfer registers, polls for completion, handles error and timeout recovery, and returns the 128-bit response.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd52_read
nodes.summary: Single-byte SDIO register read (CMD52) for the specified function and address.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd52_write
nodes.summary: Single-byte SDIO register write (CMD52) for the specified function and address.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd53_write
nodes.summary: Multi-byte SDIO block write (CMD53): splits data into 64-byte FIFO blocks, issues sdio_cmd53_setup/finish around each DMA transfer to the Arasan data FIFO.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd53_read
nodes.summary: Multi-byte SDIO block read (CMD53): issues sdio_cmd53_setup, drains the Arasan data FIFO word-by-word, then calls sdio_cmd53_finish.

nodes.name: sdio_set_clock
nodes.summary: Programs the SDIO bus clock: sets the VideoCore eMMC clock via mailbox, computes the Arasan SDCLKSEL divider, waits for clock stable, and enables the SD clock output.

nodes.name: sdio_host_init
nodes.summary: Resets the Arasan SDHCI host controller, enables bus power, sets the initial identification clock, and verifies the host version register.

nodes.name: sdio_probe
nodes.summary: SDIO bus enumeration: sends GO_IDLE, negotiates I/O voltage via CMD5, reads OCR/CID/RCA, switches to 4-bit high-speed mode, and reads function CIS tuples.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd53_setup
nodes.summary: Sets up a CMD53 transfer on the Arasan host: writes block count, transfer mode, argument, and command registers, then waits for the command complete interrupt.

nodes.name: sdio_cmd53_finish
nodes.summary: Completes a CMD53 transfer: polls for the transfer complete interrupt, handles timeout/error by resetting the DAT line.

nodes.name: sdio_print_info
nodes.summary: Diagnostic function that dumps all SDIO CCCR, FBR, CIS, and Arasan host controller registers in a structured format for debugging.

nodes.name: sdio_dump_functions
nodes.summary: Iterates all SDIO functions and prints their FBR class and block size registers.

nodes.name: sdio_init
nodes.summary: Top-level SDIO subsystem initializer: calls sdio_host_init and sdio_probe to bring the bus up, then invokes sdio_firmware_load.

nodes.name: sdio_firmware_load
nodes.summary: Orchestrates CYW43455 firmware download: puts the ARM CR4 in reset, loads the firmware image and NVRAM into chip RAM via backplane window writes, patches the MAC address, then releases the CPU to start execution.

nodes.name: armcr4_disable
nodes.summary: Halts the CYW43455 ARM Cortex-R4 application CPU by asserting the chip reset via the backplane AXI wrapper, required before downloading new firmware.

nodes.name: armcr4_enable_tcm
nodes.summary: Enables and configures all Tightly Coupled Memory (TCM) banks in the ARM CR4 for firmware data and instruction storage.

nodes.name: armcr4_activate
nodes.summary: Releases the ARM CR4 from reset at the supplied reset-vector address and waits for the firmware's SDIO ready handshake.

nodes.name: d11core_reset
nodes.summary: Performs a full reset sequence on the D11 802.11 MAC core via backplane AXI wrapper reset/enable registers.

nodes.name: bp_ram_write
nodes.summary: Writes a buffer to chip RAM through the SDIO backplane window: selects DMA path (Pi4) or CMD53 path (Pi5) based on model, and calls sdio_cmd53_setup/finish.

nodes.name: dma_to_emmc
nodes.summary: Transfers a buffer to the SDHCI FIFO via the BCM2711 DMA engine, used on Pi4/CM4 for high-throughput firmware image loading.

nodes.name: nvram_convert
nodes.summary: Converts the text NVRAM configuration file into the binary packed format expected by the CYW43455 firmware.

nodes.name: nvram_patch_macaddr
nodes.summary: Patches the macaddr key inside the NVRAM buffer with the board's unique MAC address obtained from the VideoCore mailbox.

nodes.name: pi5_pinctrl_wifi
nodes.summary: Configures the RP1 GPIO pins for the SDIO WiFi bus (CLK, CMD, DAT0-DAT3) with the correct function select and pull resistor settings for Pi5.

nodes.name: pi5_sdhci_cfginit
nodes.summary: Maps the RP1 SDHCI configuration block via ioremap and programs the vendor-specific capability and quirk registers.

nodes.name: pi5_antenna_set
nodes.summary: Selects between two WiFi antennas on Pi5 CM5 boards by toggling a GPIO line on the RP1 expander, with device-tree probe to determine if dual-antenna is present.

nodes.name: pi5_wlon_assert
nodes.summary: Drives the WL_ON GPIO line high on Pi5 to power-enable the CYW43455, waits for the chip power-on delay, then selects the antenna.

nodes.name: pi5_sdhci_probe
nodes.summary: Pi5 SDHCI probe entry: maps the RP1 SDHCI MMIO base, calls pi5_sdhci_cfginit, pi5_pinctrl_wifi, and pi5_wlon_assert to fully initialize the WiFi SDIO slot.

nodes.name: usb_dwc2.c
nodes.summary: Synopsys DWC2 USB host controller driver implementing the full host-mode USB stack: core reset, port power and reset, DMA-driven host channel transfers, split-transaction support, device and hub enumeration, and HID keyboard/mouse polling.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses DMA with explicit dcache_clean/dcache_inval calls around transfer buffers to maintain cache coherency on AArch64; split transactions are required for LS/FS devices behind HS hubs.

nodes.name: usb_hid.c
nodes.summary: USB HID class driver for xHCI host mode, handling keyboard and mouse input by registering a USB class driver, probing HID interfaces, polling devices via interrupt transfers, and translating HID reports to RISC OS keyboard and mouse events.

nodes.name: dwc2_core_reset
nodes.summary: Performs a soft reset of the DWC2 USB core, polling for AHB idle and core reset completion with timeout and debug output.

nodes.name: dwc2_core_init_host
nodes.summary: Initializes the DWC2 controller in USB host mode, configuring DMA, FIFO depths, and host channel interrupt masks.

nodes.name: dwc2_hc_xfer_split
nodes.summary: Executes a USB host channel transfer using split transactions for low-speed or full-speed devices behind a high-speed hub, managing start-split and complete-split phases.

nodes.name: dwc2_hc_xfer
nodes.summary: Core USB host channel transfer engine handling channel arming, NYET, NAK, stall, and retry logic; delegates to split-transaction path when needed.

nodes.name: dwc2_ctrl_xfer
nodes.summary: Executes a complete USB control transfer (Setup + optional Data + Status stages) using DWC2 host channels, managing DMA buffers and cache coherency.

nodes.name: dwc2_enumerate_device
nodes.summary: Enumerates a newly connected USB device by reading its device descriptor at address 0 to determine max packet size and device class.

nodes.name: dwc2_enum_child
nodes.summary: Fully enumerates a USB child device: reads descriptor, assigns address, fetches full config descriptor, parses HID interfaces, sets configuration and boot protocol.

nodes.name: dwc2_enum_hub
nodes.summary: Enumerates a USB hub: self-enumerates the hub device, reads hub class descriptor, powers all ports, waits for port connection, and recursively enumerates child devices.

nodes.name: dwc2_proc_mouse
nodes.summary: Processes a raw HID mouse report from a DWC2-polled device by delegating to the HID layer's offset detection and mouse-event injection functions.

nodes.name: dwc2_proc_keyboard
nodes.summary: Processes a raw HID keyboard report from a DWC2-polled device, diffing key arrays to detect key-down and key-up events and forwarding them to the kernel keyboard handler.

nodes.name: dwc2_int_in_once
nodes.summary: Issues a single USB interrupt-in transfer on a HID endpoint using DWC2 host channels, handling split transactions for LS devices and copying received data out.

nodes.name: dwc2_hid_poll
nodes.summary: Polls all registered DWC2-managed HID devices for new interrupt-in data and dispatches reports to the keyboard or mouse processor.

nodes.name: dwc2_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the DWC2 USB host controller: configures GPIO power, resets the core, enables host mode, powers the root port, and waits for a device to connect before triggering enumeration.

nodes.name: dwc2_device_present
nodes.summary: Returns whether a USB device is currently connected on the DWC2 host port by reading the port connection status bit.

nodes.name: dwc2_start
nodes.summary: Top-level DWC2 start sequence: initializes the controller and dispatches to hub enumeration, direct HID child enumeration, or generic device enumeration depending on detected device type.

nodes.name: dwc2_scan_ports
nodes.summary: Entry point that triggers scanning of the DWC2 USB host port by calling dwc2_start.

nodes.name: mouse_info_s
nodes.summary: Per-event capture record for the mouse history ring buffer, storing raw HID bytes, decoded movement deltas, button state, and source endpoint metadata.

nodes.name: hid_key_to_char
nodes.summary: Maps a USB HID key code to its ASCII character, applying the current keyboard layout patches and shift state.

nodes.name: hid_process_keyboard
nodes.summary: Processes a USB HID keyboard boot-protocol report, diffing the current and previous key arrays to generate key-press and key-release events forwarded to the RISC OS kernel.

nodes.name: hid_inject_keyboard_report
nodes.summary: Injects a synthetic USB HID keyboard report as RISC OS keyboard events, allowing software-generated keystrokes to enter the input pipeline.

nodes.name: mi_capture_src
nodes.summary: Captures a decoded mouse movement sample into the circular mouse history buffer, recording source endpoint metadata alongside movement and button data.

nodes.name: usb_hid_mouse_hist
nodes.summary: Retrieves a historical mouse event entry from the circular ring buffer by back-index, returning decoded movement and button state.

nodes.name: hid_mouse_id_offset
nodes.summary: Determines the byte offset within a HID mouse report at which movement data begins, accounting for an optional Report ID prefix byte.

nodes.name: hid_inject_mouse_report_src
nodes.summary: Decodes a raw USB HID mouse report and injects it as a RISC OS mouse event with signed movement deltas, button state, and source-endpoint attribution.

nodes.name: hid_process_mouse
nodes.summary: Processes a USB HID mouse report from a polled device, supporting both boot-protocol and report-protocol formats and dispatching the decoded event.

nodes.name: hid_poll
nodes.summary: Polls a single HID device via USB interrupt transfer, applies rate limiting for slow-polling keyboards, and dispatches decoded HID reports to the keyboard or mouse processor.

nodes.name: hid_probe
nodes.summary: Probes a newly discovered USB HID interface: allocates device state, reads the HID descriptor to determine report structure, and switches the device to boot protocol.

nodes.name: hid_init
nodes.summary: Registers the USB HID class driver with the USB core so that matching interfaces are automatically probed on device connection.

nodes.name: hid_poll_all
nodes.summary: Polls all registered HID devices in a single pass, calling hid_poll for each active slot.

nodes.name: hid_poll_mice
nodes.summary: High-frequency poll loop for all mouse-class HID devices, using rate limiting to service mice with lower latency than the general hid_poll_all path.

nodes.name: hid_device_disconnect
nodes.summary: Handles USB HID device disconnection by clearing device state in the slot table and freeing associated memory for the given xHCI slot ID.

nodes.name: usb_hid_keyboard_count
nodes.summary: Returns the number of currently connected USB HID keyboard devices.

nodes.name: usb_hid_mouse_count
nodes.summary: Returns the number of currently connected USB HID mouse devices.

nodes.name: wimp_mod.c
nodes.summary: Full RISC OS Wimp manager bridging all Wimp SWIs (Wimp_Initialise, Wimp_CreateWindow, Wimp_Poll, Wimp_RedrawWindow, and others) to the Phoenix framebuffer; implements window z-ordering, icon bar, menus, input routing, and a suite of self-tests that exercise the first WimpDemo desktop on Phoenix.
nodes.languageNotes: The central wimp_swi dispatcher is a single 780-line function switching over SWI offsets; self-test functions are compiled in-tree alongside production code, a bare-metal convention for verifying hardware-facing logic without a separate test binary.

nodes.name: font.c
nodes.summary: Font manager SWI handler implementing Font_FindFont, Font_Paint, and related calls with bitmap and outline font rendering routed through the Phoenix framebuffer abstraction.

nodes.name: vdu.c
nodes.summary: VDU subsystem implementing the RISC OS OS_WriteC/VDU command interpreter including graphics window management, cursor handling, bitmap character plotting (VDU 5 mode), screen-bell scheduling, and self-tests for VDU and icon rendering.
nodes.languageNotes: vdu_out is the primary OS_WriteC entry point; it accumulates multi-byte VDU sequences in a parameter buffer and dispatches to vdu_dispatch when all bytes of a command are received, matching the RISC OS VDU protocol exactly.

nodes.name: spriteop.c
nodes.summary: OS_SpriteOp implementation handling sprite output redirection by reading raw sprite headers from memory, detecting pixel format and depth, and switching the active graphics context to render into sprite buffers.

nodes.name: wrl_sub
nodes.summary: Clips a source redraw-region list against a cut rectangle, emitting up to four sub-rectangles of the source that lie outside the cut area.

nodes.name: wimp_fill_os
nodes.summary: Fills a screen rectangle specified in OS units with a given Wimp colour, converting OS coordinates to pixel coordinates before calling the framebuffer fill primitive.

nodes.name: wimp_menu_paint
nodes.summary: Renders the currently open Wimp menu by iterating its entries, drawing background fills, separators, and item text using VDU draw primitives with Wimp colours.

nodes.name: wimp_iconbar_window
nodes.summary: Creates and configures the persistent icon-bar pseudo-window that spans the bottom of the Phoenix desktop.

nodes.name: wimp_paint_window_clipped
nodes.summary: Paints a single window within a clip rectangle: draws the work area, border chrome, title bar (using Font_Paint), icons, and scroll bars, compositing each element into the correct visual layer.

nodes.name: wimp_repaint_area
nodes.summary: Repaints a damaged screen rectangle by iterating all visible windows in z-order, painting each clipped to the damage region and filling any uncovered desktop background.

nodes.name: wimp_pointer_os
nodes.summary: Reads the hardware mouse position and button state and converts pixel coordinates to OS units for Wimp event processing.

nodes.name: wimp_window_at
nodes.summary: Returns the window handle of the topmost window whose bounding box contains the given OS-unit point, used for hit-testing during pointer and click events.

nodes.name: wimp_swi
nodes.summary: Central Wimp SWI dispatcher handling the full RISC OS Wimp SWI set: Wimp_Initialise through Wimp_SpriteInfo and beyond, routing each call to the correct internal handler and managing task registration, polling, window/icon operations, and drag state.

nodes.name: wimp_drag_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test that injects synthetic mouse moves to exercise Wimp drag operations, verifying pointer tracking, drag boundaries, and drag-end event delivery.

nodes.name: wimp_desktop_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test that verifies the desktop background paint path by clearing the framebuffer and triggering a full Wimp redraw.

nodes.name: wimp_menu_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test that creates a Wimp menu, opens it, verifies it renders correctly, and tests close/reopen sequences.

nodes.name: wimp_icons_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test that creates, queries, and deletes icons within a test window, verifying icon data round-trips and redraws.

nodes.name: wimp_overlap_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test that opens two overlapping windows, brings one to front, and verifies that the redraw-region clipping correctly subtracts occluded areas.

nodes.name: wimp_register
nodes.summary: Registers the Wimp module with the Phoenix kernel module system, binding wimp_swi as the SWI handler and publishing the Wimp SWI name table.

nodes.name: font_set_colours
nodes.summary: Sets the foreground and background pixel colours used for subsequent font rendering operations.

nodes.name: font_swi
nodes.summary: Font manager SWI dispatcher handling Font_FindFont, Font_LoseFont, Font_Paint, Font_SetColour, and related calls; routes text rendering to the framebuffer draw_string primitive.

nodes.name: font_register
nodes.summary: Registers the Font module with the Phoenix kernel, binding font_swi as the SWI handler and installing the Font SWI name table.

nodes.name: vdu_set_graphics_window
nodes.summary: Sets the current VDU graphics clip window in OS units, constraining subsequent plot operations to the specified rectangle.

nodes.name: vdu_reset_graphics_window
nodes.summary: Resets the VDU graphics clip window to the full screen extent.

nodes.name: vdu_get_graphics_window
nodes.summary: Reads the current VDU graphics clip window bounds into the provided output pointers.

nodes.name: vdu_param_count
nodes.summary: Returns the number of parameter bytes expected after a given VDU control character, used by vdu_out to know when to dispatch an accumulated multi-byte command.

nodes.name: vdu5_plot_char
nodes.summary: Plots a single bitmap character at the current graphics cursor position (VDU 5 mode), advancing the cursor and blitting each glyph row via the framebuffer horizontal-span primitive.

nodes.name: vdu_bell_arm
nodes.summary: Arms the VDU bell pending flag so the next vdu_bell call will actually sound.

nodes.name: vdu_bell
nodes.summary: Processes a VDU 7 bell event: accumulates note parameters from the VDU buffer, broadcasts a sound service call, and dispatches individual notes to the sound subsystem.

nodes.name: bell_once
nodes.summary: Emits a single VDU sound note with given channel, volume, frequency, and duration by writing the OS_Sound SWI sequence through vdu_out.

nodes.name: vdu_bell_map
nodes.summary: Maps a VDU bell request to a sequence of individual sound notes, arming the bell and dispatching each note in the current bell definition.

nodes.name: vdu_bell_report
nodes.summary: Diagnostic function that prints a detailed report of the current VDU bell and sound subsystem state to the console.

nodes.name: vdu_dispatch
nodes.summary: Dispatches fully-accumulated VDU commands to their handlers — graphics window set/reset, text cursor movement, screen clear, colour set, and plot operations — based on the VDU code and parameter bytes.

nodes.name: vdu_out
nodes.summary: Primary OS_WriteC entry point: accumulates VDU parameter bytes, dispatches complete commands via vdu_dispatch, plots characters in VDU 5 graphics mode, and outputs printable characters to the text console.

nodes.name: vdu_in_graphics_mode
nodes.summary: Returns whether the VDU subsystem is currently in VDU 5 graphics cursor mode rather than text cursor mode.

nodes.name: vdu_draw_string_px
nodes.summary: Renders a null-terminated string at a given pixel position with a specified foreground colour by temporarily overriding the graphics cursor and colour, calling vdu5_plot_char for each glyph.

nodes.name: icon_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test that exercises the Wimp icon creation and redraw path via SWI dispatch, verifying that icon text appears correctly on screen.

nodes.name: vdu_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test that exercises VDU plot commands, graphics window clipping, and mode-switching by calling OS_Plot and emitting VDU sequences through vdu_out.

nodes.name: sprite_bpp
nodes.summary: Decodes the bits-per-pixel value from a RISC OS sprite mode word, returning the pixel depth for both old-style numeric modes and new-style sprite type words.

nodes.name: spriteop_switch_output
nodes.summary: Implements OS_SpriteOp 60/61 (SwitchOutputToSprite): saves and restores the active graphics context, redirects rendering into a sprite buffer by parsing the sprite header for geometry and pixel format, and manages the graphics window accordingly.

nodes.name: kernel.c
nodes.summary: Top-level kernel entry point that orchestrates the entire boot sequence — initialises all hardware subsystems (UART, MMU, IRQ, timers, scheduler, PCI, USB, MMC, filesystems, networking, GPU, modules) in order, launches BBC BASIC via aif_run, and runs the cooperative event loop.

nodes.name: aif.c
nodes.summary: AIF (ARM Image Format) loader that reads, relocates, and launches RISC OS-style AArch64 binaries; manages the SVC privilege ceiling around application execution, handling OS_Exit cleanly via aif_run and aif_jump.

nodes.name: boot.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 boot stub that parks secondary CPUs, performs EL2-to-EL1 transition (enabling physical counter access for Pi 5), rescues the firmware-loaded CMOS file before BSS zero, clears BSS, and branches to kernel_main.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses eret to transition from EL2 to EL1; installs exception vectors before the BSS clear as a safety measure; relies on linker-script symbols (__bss_start, __bss_end, __kernel_stack_top) for stack and BSS setup.

nodes.name: linker.ld
nodes.summary: AArch64 linker script placing the kernel at 0x80000, carving out xHCI/DWC2/NVMe/GEM DMA regions at 0x30000000, a 64 KB-per-CPU kernel stack, the dedicated 64 KB SVC stack (__svc_stack_base/__svc_stack_top for issue #147), and the application heap floor symbol used by aif.c.
nodes.languageNotes: Sets entry point to primary_cpu_entry; uses ASSERT to enforce that __app_heap_floor never encroaches past 192 MB; splits RX and RW segments to eliminate RWX LOAD segment warnings.

nodes.name: kernel_main
nodes.summary: Main kernel boot function called from boot.S; sequentially initialises every subsystem, registers all built-in modules, loads firmware, starts the scheduler, and launches BBC BASIC as the initial process.

nodes.name: init_process
nodes.summary: Kernel init process task — spawns secondary system tasks after the scheduler is running, then blocks permanently.

nodes.name: halt_system
nodes.summary: Logs a halt message and spins in an infinite WFI loop, stopping the system on unrecoverable error.

nodes.name: get_cpu_id
nodes.summary: Reads MPIDR_EL1 and returns the current CPU affinity index (0–3).

nodes.name: aif_exit_now
nodes.summary: OS_Exit handler that restores the SVC ceiling and unwinds from an in-progress AIF application run, called when BASIC or another AIF image issues OS_Exit.

nodes.name: aif_jump
nodes.summary: Lowers the global SVC ceiling to allow application SWI calls, sets up registers and stack, and branches to the AIF image entry point.

nodes.name: aif_run
nodes.summary: Full AIF image loader — locates the file, reads and validates the AIF header, copies code and data to the application slot, zeroes BSS, applies self-relocations, sets up the application environment, then calls aif_jump; restores SVC ceiling on return.

nodes.name: gos_run_supervisor
nodes.summary: Supervisor-mode command dispatcher that implements a simple GOS *-command interpreter loop, dispatching to the module command table.

nodes.name: primary_cpu_entry
nodes.summary: AArch64 kernel entry point — parks non-primary CPUs, drops from EL2 to EL1 (enabling physical timers), rescues the CMOS file from firmware memory, zeroes BSS, and branches to kernel_main.

nodes.name: secondary_cpu_entry
nodes.summary: Secondary CPU parking loop; spins on WFE waiting to be released by the SMP bringup code.

nodes.name: module.c
nodes.summary: Core RISC OS-compatible module system: loads and relocates AIF module images from memory or file, registers modules (SWI tables, service tables, command tables), dispatches SWI calls, broadcasts service calls, and orchestrates boot-time initialization of all built-in modules.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges AArch64 kernel to RISC OS module ABI via module_call_with_r12; handles both old AIF and new SWI-list module binary formats with per-format relocation paths.

nodes.name: module.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the module system data structures (module record, SWI entry table, service table, callback chain) and exported function prototypes for module loading, SWI dispatch, service broadcasting, and boot initialization.

nodes.name: fileswitch.c
nodes.summary: Implements the RISC OS FileSwitch SWI layer — a virtual filesystem multiplexer that routes OS_Find, OS_GBPB, OS_Args, OS_File, and OS_FSControl calls to registered filing systems (FileCore, FAT32, testfs) by parsing path prefixes and managing an open-file handle table.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FSIB_RESOLVE macros for inline FS entry dispatch and maintains a flat handle array; wildcard matching supports RISC OS ? and * syntax.

nodes.name: vectors.c
nodes.summary: Implements the OS software vector system (OS_Claim, OS_Release, OS_AddToVector, OS_CallAVector) with a tombstone model for safe chain-walking during live dispatch, plus default handlers, self-test, and diagnostic dump.
nodes.languageNotes: Tombstone model defers node deallocation until gc_tombstones runs at the end of vec_call, allowing safe removal of handlers while the chain is being walked.

nodes.name: vectors.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the software vector SWI entry points (vec_swi_claim, vec_swi_release, vec_swi_callavector, vec_swi_addtovector) and internal helpers (vec_call, vec_claim_internal, vec_release_internal) for the vector subsystem.

nodes.name: flush_dcache_icache
nodes.summary: Flushes data cache and invalidates instruction cache over a given memory range, required after loading module code into RAM before executing it.

nodes.name: module_call_with_r12
nodes.summary: Calls a module entry point passing the module's workspace pointer in the R12 position, bridging AArch64 calling conventions to the RISC OS module ABI.

nodes.name: callback_invoke
nodes.summary: Invokes a single registered callback entry, calling its function pointer with workspace and an error-output parameter.

nodes.name: callback_add
nodes.summary: Registers a callback routine and workspace pointer on the pending callback list for deferred execution.

nodes.name: callback_remove
nodes.summary: Removes a previously registered callback from the pending callback list by matching entry pointer and workspace.

nodes.name: callback_dispatch
nodes.summary: Drains the pending callback queue, invoking each registered callback in sequence and clearing the list.

nodes.name: callback_dump
nodes.summary: Prints the current pending callback list to the console for diagnostic purposes.

nodes.name: module_call_swi
nodes.summary: Calls a module's SWI handler entry point, passing register state, workspace pointer, and SWI offset within the module's chunk.

nodes.name: module_call_service_fast
nodes.summary: Dispatches a service call to a module using the fast indexed path derived from the module's service table entry.

nodes.name: module_service_table
nodes.summary: Resolves a service reason code's entry offset and workspace address from a module's declared service table.

nodes.name: module_service_index
nodes.summary: Looks up the service table index entry for a specific reason code in a given module's service table.

nodes.name: module_dump_services
nodes.summary: Prints the complete service call routing table across all registered modules, showing reason codes, entry offsets, and workspace pointers.

nodes.name: module_dump_swis
nodes.summary: Dumps the SWI registration table for all loaded modules, listing chunk base addresses, handler entry points, and SWI name strings.

nodes.name: module_register_native
nodes.summary: Registers a native (non-AIF) module structure by allocating a module record and delegating to module_register, then calling the module's init entry point.

nodes.name: module_register
nodes.summary: Wires a loaded module into the kernel's module list, registering its SWI base chunk, service table, and command table after validating header offsets.

nodes.name: module_load_from_memory
nodes.summary: Parses, relocates, and loads an AIF module image from a memory buffer, handling both the legacy AIF format and the newer SWI-list format with full relocation fixup and cache flush before calling the init entry.

nodes.name: module_load_from_file
nodes.summary: Opens a file by path via VFS, reads it into a heap buffer, passes it to module_load_from_memory, then frees the buffer.

nodes.name: swi_dispatch
nodes.summary: Top-level SWI dispatcher: routes an incoming SWI number to the correct module's SWI handler or handles built-in kernel SWIs (OS_Module, OS_ServiceCall, OS_ReadSysInfo, etc.) directly.

nodes.name: module_broadcast_service
nodes.summary: Broadcasts a service call to all registered modules that have declared interest in the given reason code, using the fast indexed dispatch path.

nodes.name: module_dump_list
nodes.summary: Prints the list of all currently loaded modules, showing each module's name for diagnostics.

nodes.name: modcmd_dispatch
nodes.summary: Dispatches a parsed CLI command string to the matching module command handler, supporting RISC OS abbreviation rules and both execute and status modes.

nodes.name: module_init_all
nodes.summary: Boot-time initialization: loads all built-in module blobs embedded in the kernel image, registers native modules (FileSwitch, FileCore, FAT32, etc.), and dispatches the initial callback queue.

nodes.name: module_service_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test that broadcasts two service calls and verifies the expected test modules handled each correctly.

nodes.name: module_set_swi_names
nodes.summary: Registers name strings for a module's SWI chunk, mapping each offset to its canonical name for use by OS_SWINumberToString.

nodes.name: module_swi_number_from_name
nodes.summary: Resolves a SWI name string (e.g. 'OS_WriteC') to its numeric SWI number by scanning registered module SWI name tables.

nodes.name: fs_module_find
nodes.summary: Searches the registered filing system table for a module whose name matches the given prefix, using case-insensitive comparison.

nodes.name: fs_prefix_split
nodes.summary: Splits a RISC OS path at its 'FSname:' prefix, returning the filing system module index and the remainder of the path.

nodes.name: fs_module_open
nodes.summary: Calls a filing system module's open entry point via the FS dispatch table and fills an open-file handle slot with the result.

nodes.name: fs_module_read
nodes.summary: Calls a filing system module's read entry point for sequential or random-access data transfer.

nodes.name: fs_module_close
nodes.summary: Calls a filing system module's close entry point and releases the open-file handle slot.

nodes.name: fs_find
nodes.summary: Central FileSwitch open/find operation: routes all OS_Find reason codes (open for read, update, create, etc.) to the appropriate backend (FileCore or testfs) and allocates a handle, handling both path-based and handle-based variants.

nodes.name: fs_bget
nodes.summary: Reads a single byte from an open file handle using VFS or FS module dispatch, implementing OS_BGet.

nodes.name: fs_bput
nodes.summary: Writes a single byte to an open file handle by routing through fs_gbpb, implementing OS_BPut.

nodes.name: fs_wildmatch
nodes.summary: Matches a filename against a RISC OS wildcard pattern supporting ? (single character) and * (any sequence) metacharacters.

nodes.name: fs_gbpb_dirents
nodes.summary: Reads directory entries for OS_GBPB reason codes 9-12, supporting wildcard filtering, returning name-only or full attribute records.

nodes.name: fs_gbpb
nodes.summary: Implements OS_GBPB sequential and random byte-block transfer for open file handles, dispatching to module read or VFS read as appropriate.

nodes.name: fs_args
nodes.summary: Implements OS_Args operations (read/write sequential pointer, read extent, flush) on open file handles, supporting both VFS and FS-module backends.

nodes.name: fs_dump_filesystems
nodes.summary: Prints the registered filing system table, showing each FS module's name, entry points, and dispatch flags.

nodes.name: fs_control
nodes.summary: Implements OS_FSControl operations including filing system selection, path canonicalization, copy, rename, and wipe across registered filing system modules.

nodes.name: fs_file
nodes.summary: Implements OS_File operations (save, read catalogue info, write catalogue info, delete, create) for both FileCore-backed and testfs-backed paths.

nodes.name: claim_node
nodes.summary: Allocates a vector handler node and prepends it to a vector chain, optionally deduplicating an existing handler for the same routine/pw pair.

nodes.name: vec_claim_internal
nodes.summary: Claims a vector by installing a C function pointer handler using the internal calling convention.

nodes.name: vec_claim_s3
nodes.summary: Claims a vector with the ARM Stage 3 calling convention, used for SVC-mode module handlers that preserve all registers.

nodes.name: vec_release_internal
nodes.summary: Removes a previously claimed vector handler by locating it in the chain and marking it with a tombstone if the chain is live.

nodes.name: vec_call
nodes.summary: Walks the handler chain for a vector, calling each handler in turn until one claims the call, then GC-sweeps tombstoned nodes at the end.

nodes.name: claim_common
nodes.summary: Shared implementation for OS_Claim and OS_AddToVector, validating vector number and parameters before forwarding to claim_node.

nodes.name: vec_swi_claim
nodes.summary: SWI entry point for OS_Claim, installs a new handler at the head of the specified vector chain.

nodes.name: vec_swi_addtovector
nodes.summary: SWI entry point for OS_AddToVector, installs a handler at the head of the specified vector chain.

nodes.name: vec_swi_release
nodes.summary: SWI entry point for OS_Release, removes a handler from the specified vector chain.

nodes.name: vec_swi_callavector
nodes.summary: SWI entry point for OS_CallAVector, dispatches a vector call with the current register state.

nodes.name: vectors_init
nodes.summary: Initializes all software vectors by installing a default pass-through handler on each vector slot.

nodes.name: vec_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test suite exercising claim, release, call, deduplication, and tombstone GC across all vector dispatch paths.

nodes.name: vec_econet_test
nodes.summary: Tests vector dispatch using the EconetV vector as a realistic example of multi-handler chain traversal.

nodes.name: vec_has_handler
nodes.summary: Returns whether a given vector number has any non-default handler installed in its chain.

nodes.name: vec_dump
nodes.summary: Dumps all vector chains to the debug output, listing each handler's routine address, workspace pointer, and calling convention.

nodes.name: pci.c
nodes.summary: Implements PCIe bus enumeration, link bring-up, xHCI USB host controller initialisation, HID keyboard/mouse enumeration, and USB mass storage support for Raspberry Pi 4, CM4, and Pi 5 hardware variants.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines Pi 4 ECAM-based PCIe and Pi 5 RC-series PCIe in a single translation unit; xHCI state is managed via a large struct xhci rather than separate objects.

nodes.name: devicetree.c
nodes.summary: Parses the Raspberry Pi device tree blob at boot to discover memory layout, CPU count and release addresses, GIC interrupt controller registers, and SOC bus-to-physical translations; also registers the HALInfo SWI.

nodes.name: lib.c
nodes.summary: Provides core kernel utility functions: printf-style debug output (vsnprintf/debug_print), string/memory helpers (strlen, memcmp, strcmp), framebuffer ready flags, and the main WIMP task loop that orchestrates network polling, paint tasks, and application tasks.
nodes.languageNotes: wimp_task is an extremely large function (736 lines) acting as the kernel's cooperative multitasking scheduler loop.

nodes.name: dynarea.c
nodes.summary: Implements RISC OS Dynamic Areas for Phoenix: create, read, resize (OS_DynamicArea reason codes), and report; page-aligned heap regions backed by a fixed-size area table.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the RISC OS OS_DynamicArea SWI reason codes in C; called directly from os_swi.c dispatcher.

nodes.name: cursor_module_impl.c
nodes.summary: Kernel-linked CursorModule implementing RISC OS module init/final entry points; initialises keyboard and mouse event queues, sets mouse bounds from the framebuffer, and starts the pointer sprite via cursor_init/cursor_show/cursor_update.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CMunge -64bit module ABI conventions (_clib_initialisemodule stubs, _kernel_oserror return type); weak-linked USB HID count symbols allow it to build before USB is fully initialised.

nodes.name: pci_init
nodes.summary: Top-level PCIe initialisation entry point called from boot; dispatches to pci_init_pi4 or pci_init_pi5 based on detected hardware.

nodes.name: pci_init_pi4
nodes.summary: Performs full PCIe and xHCI USB initialisation for Raspberry Pi 4: brings up the PCIe link, configures outbound windows, enables bus mastering, and enumerates the USB bus for HID and mass-storage devices.

nodes.name: pci_init_pi5
nodes.summary: Orchestrates PCIe and xHCI initialisation for Raspberry Pi 5, bringing up the RC root complex and both xHCI controllers.

nodes.name: pci_read_config
nodes.summary: Reads a 32-bit value from a PCI device's ECAM configuration space at a given offset.

nodes.name: pci_write_config
nodes.summary: Writes a 32-bit value into a PCI device's ECAM configuration space at a given offset.

nodes.name: pcie_bring_up_link
nodes.summary: Negotiates the PCIe physical link on Pi 4: asserts perst, waits for link training, configures speed and width, and confirms link-up status.

nodes.name: xhci_setup_msi
nodes.summary: Configures MSI (Message Signaled Interrupts) for the xHCI USB host controller, allocating GIC interrupt routes and writing MSI capability registers.

nodes.name: xhci_controller_init
nodes.summary: Initialises an xHCI USB host controller: resets the controller, allocates DMA memory for command/event rings and device context arrays, and starts the controller running.

nodes.name: xhci_evt_dispatch
nodes.summary: Processes xHCI event ring entries, dispatching transfer completion, command completion, and port status change events to appropriate handlers.

nodes.name: xhci_enumerate_bus
nodes.summary: Enumerates all USB devices on an xHCI controller: walks every root port, addresses and configures devices, identifies HID and mass-storage devices, and sets up appropriate data structures.

nodes.name: xhci_attach_msc
nodes.summary: Attaches a USB mass storage class device (MSC): queries descriptors, configures bulk endpoints, reads the capacity via SCSI READ CAPACITY, and registers the block device for filesystem use.

nodes.name: xhci_hotplug_walk
nodes.summary: Handles USB hot-plug attach events by walking the USB topology from a root port, addressing the newly connected device, and identifying its class for further initialisation.

nodes.name: pci_pi5_xhci_run
nodes.summary: Pi 5 primary xHCI controller run loop: enumerates the USB bus, attaches HID and MSC devices, then enters a hot-plug service loop polling for device connect/disconnect events.

nodes.name: pci_pi5_kbd_enum
nodes.summary: Enumerates USB HID keyboards on the Pi 5 xHCI controller: addresses devices, reads HID report descriptors, and activates boot-protocol keyboard input.

nodes.name: xhci_swi
nodes.summary: SWI handler for the XHCI module, dispatching reason codes to query controller count, read port state, and access USB device information.

nodes.name: xhci
nodes.summary: Central xHCI controller state structure holding MMIO base, DMA offsets, command/event ring indices, port tables, hot-plug state, HID slot tracking, and SCSI transfer bookkeeping.

nodes.name: device_tree_parse
nodes.summary: Main device tree entry point: validates the FDT magic, then calls parse_memory, parse_cpus, parse_soc_ranges, parse_gic, parse_model, and parse_bootargs to populate global hardware descriptors.

nodes.name: parse_memory
nodes.summary: Walks the device tree memory node to extract RAM base address and size for the detected Pi board variant.

nodes.name: parse_cpus
nodes.summary: Parses the device tree cpus node to count processors and read per-CPU cpu-release-addr values used for AArch64 spin-table SMP bring-up.

nodes.name: parse_gic
