nodes.summary: Extracts GIC distributor and CPU interface register base addresses from the interrupt-controller node in the device tree.

nodes.name: dt_blob_contains
nodes.summary: Returns whether the parsed device tree blob contains a given substring in any string property, used for board variant detection.

nodes.name: dt_cmdline_key
nodes.summary: Searches the kernel command line (from bootargs) for a named key=value pair and copies the value into the caller's buffer.

nodes.name: halinfo_swi
nodes.summary: SWI handler for the HALInfo module, returning hardware info values (memory start, size, GIC addresses, CPU count) by reason code.

nodes.name: halinfo_register
nodes.summary: Registers the HALInfo SWI module with the kernel module table so the SWI dispatcher can route HALInfo calls.

nodes.name: debug_vprint
nodes.summary: Variadic kernel debug print function: formats a message via vsnprintf, optionally prefixes it with a timestamp, and writes it to the UART and framebuffer console.

nodes.name: debug_print
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper around debug_vprint accepting a printf-style format string and variadic arguments.

nodes.name: vsnprintf
nodes.summary: Kernel-space vsnprintf implementation supporting %d, %u, %x, %s, %c format specifiers with field-width and zero-padding; no floating point.

nodes.name: wimp_task
nodes.summary: Main WIMP cooperative task loop: initialises devices (PCI, VFS, network), spawns secondary CPU tasks, polls input events, drives the window manager, and services network and paint tasks in a round-robin fashion.

nodes.name: net_pump
nodes.summary: Runs several iterations of the network service poll to drain pending network events before yielding back to the WIMP task loop.

nodes.name: dynarea_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the Dynamic Area table, pre-creating the standard RISC OS system areas (application space, screen memory, module area, system heap) with their default sizes.

nodes.name: dynarea_read
nodes.summary: Returns a Dynamic Area's base address and current/maximum size by area number; used by the OS_DynamicArea 2 (read) SWI reason code.

nodes.name: dynarea_change
nodes.summary: Grows or shrinks a Dynamic Area by the requested page delta, returning the actual change; implements OS_DynamicArea 5 (change size).

nodes.name: dynarea_report
nodes.summary: Iterates all active Dynamic Areas and prints their number, name, base, current size, and maximum size to the debug console.

nodes.name: cursor_module_impl_init
nodes.summary: RISC OS module initialisation entry point: initialises keyboard and mouse event queues, sets mouse bounds from the live framebuffer dimensions, calls cursor_init/cursor_show/cursor_update to render the pointer sprite, and reports USB HID device counts.

nodes.name: cursor_module_impl_final
nodes.summary: RISC OS module finalisation entry point: hides the cursor sprite and logs finalisation; called by the module framework when the module is killed or re-loaded.

nodes.name: mmc.c
nodes.summary: SDHCI-based MMC/SD host controller driver that initializes eMMC/SD cards through a full OCR/CID/CSD negotiation sequence, implements PIO block read/write, and registers the device as a block device with the OS.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses direct MMIO register reads/writes via MMIO_READ/MMIO_WRITE macros; no DMA path — all transfers are programmed I/O through the 32-bit SDHCI data port.

nodes.name: mmc_init
nodes.summary: Performs the full SDHCI controller and SD/eMMC card initialization sequence: reset, power-up, clock setup, OCR/ACMD41 negotiation, CID/RCA/CSD parsing, bus width selection, and block device registration.

nodes.name: mmc_send_cmd
nodes.summary: Issues a single MMC/SD command through the SDHCI command/argument registers, handles data transfer setup for read/write commands, and returns the 128-bit response.

nodes.name: mmc_read_chunk
nodes.summary: Reads a contiguous chunk of blocks from the SD/eMMC card using PIO via CMD18 multi-block read and drains data from the SDHCI FIFO 32 bits at a time.

nodes.name: mmc_write_chunk
nodes.summary: Writes a contiguous chunk of blocks to the SD/eMMC card using PIO via CMD25 multi-block write, filling the SDHCI FIFO 32 bits at a time.

nodes.name: mmc_read_blocks
nodes.summary: Public block-read entry point that splits a request across multiple chunks and calls mmc_read_chunk for each segment.

nodes.name: mmc_write_blocks
nodes.summary: Public block-write entry point that splits a request across multiple chunks and calls mmc_write_chunk for each segment.

nodes.name: mmc_get_info
nodes.summary: Fills a block-device info structure with the card's total capacity in blocks and block size.

nodes.name: sdhci_wait_cmd_ready
nodes.summary: Polls the SDHCI present-state register until the command-inhibit-CMD bit clears, returning failure on timeout.

nodes.name: sdhci_wait_data_ready
nodes.summary: Polls the SDHCI present-state register until the command-inhibit-DAT bit clears, returning failure on timeout.

nodes.name: sdhci_reset
nodes.summary: Writes a software reset to the SDHCI software-reset register and spins until the reset-complete bit is asserted.

nodes.name: fat32.c
nodes.summary: Phoenix's FAT32 filesystem driver: mounts FAT32 partitions identified via FileCore, scans root-directory entries for 8.3 filenames, reads files by cluster-chain traversal, and persists CMOS settings into a dedicated file on the FAT32 volume.
nodes.languageNotes: Interoperates tightly with the FileCore layer for partition enumeration (filecore_fat_count / filecore_fat_get) and with CMOS RAM for settings persistence.

nodes.name: fat32
nodes.summary: Volume-state structure for a mounted FAT32 partition, holding block-device handle, partition geometry, cluster-to-LBA mapping parameters, FAT location, and mount flag.

nodes.name: fat32_mount_at
nodes.summary: Mounts a FAT32 partition at a given FileCore partition index by reading and parsing the BPB (BIOS Parameter Block) boot sector and populating the fat32 state structure.

nodes.name: fat32_mount_holding
nodes.summary: Iterates all FileCore FAT partitions to find and mount the one whose root directory holds a file matching the given 11-byte 8.3 volume label.

nodes.name: fat32_find_root
nodes.summary: Scans the FAT32 root directory cluster chain for a file matching an 11-byte 8.3 name, returning its first cluster number and byte size.

nodes.name: fat32_read_file
nodes.summary: Reads a FAT32 file into a buffer by following the cluster chain and reading each sector into the output buffer up to a caller-supplied maximum.

nodes.name: fat32_info
nodes.summary: Diagnostic command that prints FAT32 partition geometry and probes for key files (CMOS image, kernel image) in the root directory, reporting their presence and size.

nodes.name: fat32_verify_cmos
nodes.summary: Reads the CMOS image file from the FAT32 partition and checks its size and header against the in-memory CMOS layout, reporting any mismatch.

nodes.name: fat32_cmos_partition
nodes.summary: Locates the FAT32 partition that contains the CMOS file by scanning all FileCore FAT partitions, returning first cluster and file size on success.

nodes.name: cmos_walk
nodes.summary: Walks the cluster chain of the CMOS file sector by sector, either reading existing data or writing new CMOS image data depending on a mode flag.

nodes.name: fat32_save_cmos
nodes.summary: Saves the in-memory CMOS RAM image to the CMOS file on the FAT32 partition: verifies existing file size, compares old and new content, and writes changed sectors cluster-by-cluster.

nodes.name: fat_next
nodes.summary: Reads the FAT table entry for the given cluster to find the next cluster in a chain, supporting both FAT32 (32-bit) and FAT16 (16-bit) entry widths.

nodes.name: dma4.c
nodes.summary: BCM DMA4 engine driver providing cache-coherent cyclic (ring-buffer) DMA channel management for zero-copy streaming from DREQ peripherals, plus a memory-to-memory test path and diagnostic register dump.
nodes.languageNotes: DMA4 control blocks require 64-byte alignment and use 64-bit physical addresses; the cyclic mode builds a two-CB linked list to create an infinite ring without CPU intervention.

nodes.name: dma4_cb
nodes.summary: Hardware-layout DMA4 control block struct with transfer-info flags, source/destination 64-bit physical addresses, transfer length, and next-CB physical pointer matching the BCM DMA4 register file.
nodes.languageNotes: Struct fields map 1:1 to BCM DMA4 CB register offsets; must be placed in physically-addressed, cache-flushed memory before being written to the DMA4 CONBLK_AD register.

nodes.name: dma4_cache_sync
nodes.summary: Performs a cache clean+invalidate over a given virtual address range to guarantee DMA coherency before starting or after completing a hardware transfer.

nodes.name: dma4_info
nodes.summary: Prints DMA4 channel base address, CS, TI, and address register values to the console for diagnostics, labelled with the detected Pi model.

nodes.name: dma4_test
nodes.summary: Executes a memory-to-memory DMA4 test: fills source buffer with known data, programs a control block, starts the transfer, polls for completion, and validates every destination word.

nodes.name: dma4_cyclic_start
nodes.summary: Configures a cyclic DMA4 transfer from a peripheral DREQ source into a ring buffer by building a linked pair of control blocks and activating the DMA4 channel.

nodes.name: dma4_cyclic_pos
nodes.summary: Returns the current write head position within the cyclic DMA ring buffer by reading the channel's destination-address register.

nodes.name: dma4_cyclic_running
nodes.summary: Returns non-zero if the cyclic DMA4 channel's ACTIVE bit is set in the CS register.

nodes.name: dma4_cyclic_stop
nodes.summary: Clears the ACTIVE bit and sets ABORT in the DMA4 channel CS register to halt and drain the in-flight cyclic transfer.

nodes.name: dma4_cyclic_channel
nodes.summary: Returns the DMA4 hardware channel index allocated for cyclic operation.

nodes.name: dma4_cyclic_regs
nodes.summary: Reads the cyclic DMA4 channel's CS, DEBUG, and transfer-length registers into caller-supplied output pointers for diagnostic use.

nodes.name: dma4_cyclic_status
nodes.summary: Prints the live cyclic DMA4 channel state (CS, DEBUG, source/destination addresses, length) to the console.

nodes.name: i2c.c
nodes.summary: I2C bus master driver using the BCM BSC controller: discovers bus instances from the Device Tree, implements GPIO pin mux, provides raw address-probe and write-read transactions, and contains full DS3231M RTC support including boot-time clock adoption from hardware.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses BCM BSC (Broadcom Serial Controller) registers for I2C; GPIO alternate function selection is manual (no pinctrl layer); DS3231M at address 0x68 is the system RTC source at boot.

nodes.name: i2c_report_node
nodes.summary: Parses a Device Tree I2C bus node to extract its register base, resolve its SoC physical address, check mapping safety, and report it with compatibility strings and GPIO info.

nodes.name: i2c_walk
nodes.summary: Recursively walks Device Tree nodes looking for I2C bus compatible nodes and calls i2c_report_node for each match found.

nodes.name: i2c_probe_report
nodes.summary: Walks the Device Tree from its root to enumerate and report all I2C bus instances and their GPIO pins, printing results to both console and debug output.

nodes.name: gpio_set_func
nodes.summary: Sets the alternate function (FSEL) for a single GPIO pin by read-modify-writing the GPIO function select register bank.

nodes.name: bsc_wait_done
nodes.summary: Polls the BSC status register until DONE or ERR is set, applying a microsecond-based timeout to detect hung transfers.

nodes.name: i2c_addr_probe
nodes.summary: Probes a single 7-bit I2C address by initiating a zero-length read and checking whether the device ACKs, used during bus-scan operations.

nodes.name: i2c_write_read
nodes.summary: Performs a combined I2C write-then-read transaction against a given 7-bit address, loading the write buffer, waiting for DONE, then reading the response bytes from the FIFO.

nodes.name: i2c_explain
nodes.summary: Translates an I2C transaction return code to a human-readable error string and prints it with the failing device address.

nodes.name: hexdump
nodes.summary: Formats and prints a byte buffer as a hex dump with register-address annotations, used to display raw I2C register reads.

nodes.name: i2c_scan_header
nodes.summary: Scans the configured I2C bus across the 7-bit address space, probing each address and printing a grid of responding devices in the style of i2cdetect.

nodes.name: i2c_read_command
nodes.summary: CLI command handler that parses a device address, register, and byte count, performs a write-read I2C transaction, and hex-dumps the result.

nodes.name: ds3231_report
nodes.summary: Reads all 19 DS3231M registers via I2C and prints a decoded human-readable report of time, alarm, control, status, and temperature fields.

nodes.name: ds3231_read_time
nodes.summary: Reads the DS3231M time registers and decodes BCD-encoded year, month, day, hour, minute, second, and oscillator-stop flag into output pointers.

nodes.name: ds3231_write_time
nodes.summary: Encodes year/month/day/hour/minute/second/weekday into BCD and writes them to the DS3231M time-keeping registers over I2C.

nodes.name: ds3231_boot_adopt
nodes.summary: Boot-time routine that configures I2C GPIO pins, reads the DS3231M RTC, and sets the OS software clock from the hardware time if the oscillator has not stopped.

nodes.name: ds3231_set_command
nodes.summary: CLI command to set the DS3231M RTC to the current OS time by reading the software clock, converting to calendar fields, and writing to the RTC over I2C.

nodes.name: i2c_bus_transfer
nodes.summary: Generic I2C bus transfer API callable from other OS components: performs either a write or read against a 7-bit address using the configured BSC bus.

nodes.name: i2c_bus_available
nodes.summary: Returns whether the I2C bus has been successfully initialized and the BSC base address is available.

nodes.name: framebuffer.c
nodes.summary: Implements the VideoCore framebuffer for Pi 4/CM4/Pi5: allocates the display buffer via the GPU mailbox, exposes pixel, rect, line, circle, and text drawing primitives in RGB565 format, and provides a scrolling text console with cursor management and formatted printf output consumed by the VDU and WIMP layers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses RGB565 packed pixel format; the console (con_*) and software cursor (cursor_*) subsystems are co-located with the drawing primitives. Cursor blitting is XOR-based, saving background pixels for restoration.

nodes.name: framebuffer.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring all public framebuffer, console, and cursor APIs, the RGB color macro, pixel-format helpers, and display configuration constants shared by gpu.c and higher-level VDU/WIMP consumers.

nodes.name: gpu.c
nodes.summary: Top-level GPU initialization entry point: queries native display resolution via the VideoCore mailbox, allocates the framebuffer, draws the boot splash screen with scaled text, initializes the text console and mouse bounds, and signals boot progress via LED and debug output.

nodes.name: audio_diag.c
nodes.summary: Provides early-boot audio diagnostic utilities: synthesizes PCM tones via the VideoCore mailbox audio interface and emits configurable beep codes used for error signaling when serial output is unavailable.

nodes.name: hdmi_audio.c
nodes.summary: Comprehensive HDMI audio driver for the Pi VideoCore: configures HDMI audio subsystem registers, encodes IEC 60958 subframes, supports both busy-wait and DMA4-cyclic playback paths, and includes diagnostic frequency sweep, calibration, and tune-playback routines.
nodes.languageNotes: At 2253 lines this is the largest file in the GPU layer. Dead-code stubs are gated by conditional compilation (functions delegating to hdmi_nope). The DMA path uses the Pi 4 DMA4 engine for zero-CPU audio streaming via cyclic IEC 60958-encoded buffers.

nodes.name: mailbox_property.c
nodes.summary: Implements the VideoCore IV property mailbox protocol, providing structured getter/setter functions for board revision, MAC address, ARM/VC memory split, clock rates, power state, GPIO/LED control, and RTC register access — the primary firmware IPC interface for GPU and peripheral drivers.
nodes.languageNotes: All calls funnel through mbox_simple_resp which builds the tagged property-buffer in the 16-byte-aligned mailbox buffer and calls the low-level mbox_call; higher-level wrappers are thin convenience functions over this single code path.

nodes.name: fb_init
nodes.summary: Allocates the VideoCore framebuffer at a requested resolution and depth via the GPU mailbox, maps the returned base address, records screen geometry, and paints a four-panel color test pattern on success.

nodes.name: fb_query_native
nodes.summary: Queries the display native resolution from the VideoCore via a mailbox call and returns width/height, enabling the GPU layer to allocate the framebuffer at the monitor's preferred resolution.

nodes.name: fb_hspan
nodes.summary: Draws a horizontal span (scanline segment) with clipping in RGB565 format, serving as the inner-loop primitive for fb_fill_rect and all higher-level filled-shape renderers.

nodes.name: con_vprintf
nodes.summary: Variable-argument printf implementation for the framebuffer text console, handling %s, %c, %d, %u, %x format specifiers by dispatching to con_putc and con_puts.

nodes.name: cursor_blit
nodes.summary: Saves the pixels beneath the cursor area then composites the cursor sprite by XOR-blending each set bit of the cursor bitmap against the background, implementing a hardware-cursor effect in software.

nodes.name: cursor_update
nodes.summary: Moves the software cursor to a new screen position by restoring the saved background and re-blitting the cursor sprite at the new coordinates.

nodes.name: con_putc
nodes.summary: Outputs a single character to the framebuffer text console, handling newline, carriage-return, backspace, and tab control codes with automatic line scrolling when the bottom row is reached.

nodes.name: fb_set_pixel
nodes.summary: Writes a single pixel to the framebuffer in RGB565 format with bounds-checking, serving as the foundational write primitive for line and circle renderers.

nodes.name: fb_clear
nodes.summary: Fills the entire framebuffer with a single color in a tight word-aligned loop, used for screen clears and initial display setup.

nodes.name: fb_get_pixel
nodes.summary: Reads a pixel from the framebuffer at (x, y) and converts from RGB565 to a 24-bit RGB value, used by the cursor blitter to save background pixels before compositing.

nodes.name: fb_draw_circle
nodes.summary: Draws an outline circle using a midpoint (Bresenham) algorithm, placing eight symmetric pixels per step via fb_set_pixel.

nodes.name: gpu_init
nodes.summary: Orchestrates full GPU initialization: signals LED start, queries native resolution, allocates the framebuffer, draws the boot splash and status text at 2x scale, initializes the console and mouse bounds, marks the framebuffer ready, and signals LED success.

nodes.name: audio_beep
nodes.summary: Generates a PCM tone burst via the VideoCore mailbox audio channel, writing DMA control block descriptors and buffer pointers to the mailbox for the requested number of repetitions.

nodes.name: hdmi_audio_setup
nodes.summary: Probes the Pi model to select the HDMI audio register base, programs sample-rate divisors for the requested rate, and calls snd_configure to arm the HDMI audio hardware for output.

nodes.name: hdmi_audio_beep
nodes.summary: Plays a short tone through HDMI using a busy-wait loop that writes IEC 60958-encoded stereo subframes to the MAI TX FIFO at the programmed sample rate.

nodes.name: hdmi_audio_dma_start
nodes.summary: Initializes DMA4-driven HDMI audio by allocating a cyclic PCM buffer, filling it with IEC 60958 subframes, cache-synchronizing it, and launching the DMA4 channel to stream audio continuously to the HDMI MAI FIFO.

nodes.name: snd_configure
nodes.summary: Programs the HDMI controller registers for audio output: resets the MAI interface, writes the audio infoframe checksum, configures IEC channel-status bits, sets DREQ thresholds, and waits for D0 power-ready state.

nodes.name: hdmi_audio_sweep
nodes.summary: Diagnostic frequency sweep that steps through a range of tones, printing each frequency to the console via con_printf and playing it via hdmi_audio_beep, used for HDMI audio bring-up testing.

nodes.name: mbox_simple_resp
nodes.summary: Core mailbox property transaction helper: builds the tagged property buffer in a 16-byte-aligned mailbox buffer, calls mbox_call on channel 8, and returns the response value array — used internally by all mbox_get/mbox_set wrappers.

nodes.name: mbox_get_arm_memory
nodes.summary: Queries the VideoCore firmware for the ARM-accessible memory region base address and size via the property mailbox.

nodes.name: mbox_get_vc_memory
nodes.summary: Queries the VideoCore firmware for the VC (GPU) memory region base and size, used to determine the ARM/GPU address space split.

nodes.name: mbox_notify_xhci_reset
nodes.summary: Sends the NOTIFY_XHCI_RESET mailbox message to the VideoCore firmware, required after xHCI USB controller reset on Pi 4 to allow firmware to complete USB initialization handshake.

nodes.name: mbox_get_rtc_reg
nodes.summary: Reads a BCM2712 RTC register via the property mailbox, returning two 32-bit response words for DS3231M-compatible RTC access on Pi 5.

nodes.name: mbox_get_mac_address
nodes.summary: Retrieves the board MAC address from the VideoCore firmware via the property mailbox and writes the 6 bytes into the caller-supplied buffer.

nodes.name: mbox_set_rtc_reg
nodes.summary: Writes a value to a BCM2712 RTC register via the property mailbox.

nodes.name: bt_uart.c
nodes.summary: Complete Bluetooth HCI-over-UART driver for the CYW43455 combo chip on Pi 4 and Pi 5. Covers hardware power-up and GPIO control, UART pin-mux and PL011 initialisation, firmware download at 115200 baud followed by re-init at 3 Mbaud, device inquiry, SSP pairing with key persistence, ACL/L2CAP/SDP protocol stacks, HID report injection, and registers as the BTUart-phoenix provider module at SWI 0x5A000.
nodes.languageNotes: Dual-path design for Pi 4 (PL011 UART) and Pi 5 (RP1 mini-UART via ioremap); both paths converge at the same HCI command/event primitives.

nodes.name: input_stub.c
nodes.summary: Keyboard and mouse input event bridge layer that maintains ring-buffer backed event queues for HID devices. Exports init, inject, poll, and query functions for both keyboard and mouse, consumed by the WIMP manager and os_swi.c routing layer.

nodes.name: rp1_gem.c
nodes.summary: RP1 GEM (Gigabit Ethernet MAC) driver for Pi 5, implementing PHY reset and autonegotiation over MDIO, TX/RX DMA descriptor ring initialisation, packet transmit, polled receive, and link-state query. Used directly by the TCP/IP stack (ARP, IPv4) on Pi 5.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses RP1 peripheral MMIO accessed through ioremap; DMA descriptor rings are allocated as static arrays, and the receive path is polled rather than interrupt-driven.

nodes.name: bt_power_on
nodes.summary: Powers on the CYW43455 Bluetooth chip on Pi 4 via VideoCore mailbox GPIO lines, asserting and de-asserting the BT_REG_ON pin with a stabilisation delay.

nodes.name: bt_power_on_pi5
nodes.summary: Powers on the Bluetooth sub-system on Pi 5 by writing to RP1-mapped power control registers, with a delay and readback for diagnostics.

nodes.name: bt_pi5_power_probe
nodes.summary: Exported probe that enables Wi-Fi and Bluetooth power on Pi 5 by asserting WLON via pinctrl, then calls bt_power_on_pi5 to complete BT hardware bring-up.

nodes.name: bt_pi5_uart_probe
nodes.summary: Exported probe that ioremaps the RP1 mini-UART and pin-control registers for Pi 5, reads and logs current UART line and interrupt status, then queries the pin-variant table to confirm hardware identity.

nodes.name: btu_putc
nodes.summary: Transmits a single byte to the RP1 mini-UART used on Pi 5, spinning on the TX-full flag before writing.

nodes.name: btu_getc
nodes.summary: Receives a single byte from the RP1 mini-UART with a millisecond timeout, returning -1 on timeout.

nodes.name: bt_pi5_uart_pinmux
nodes.summary: Configures the RP1 pin-control registers to route UART TX/RX/CTS/RTS signals to the Bluetooth chip on Pi 5, logging each pin-mux register value.

nodes.name: bt_pi5_power_cycle
nodes.summary: Power-cycles the BT_REG_ON GPIO on Pi 5 through the RP1 pad registers, with delay gaps for chip reset stabilisation.

nodes.name: bt_pi5_bt_bringup
nodes.summary: Exported Pi 5 Bluetooth bring-up sequence: configures pin-mux, initialises the mini-UART at 115200, downloads CYW43455 firmware, sends the HCI Reset command, then re-probes the BD address.

nodes.name: bt_pl011_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the Pi 4 PL011 UART for Bluetooth HCI by configuring GPIO alternate functions, setting the divisor for the requested baud rate, and enabling the UART with 8N1 frame format.

nodes.name: bt_read_event
nodes.summary: Reads one HCI event packet from the UART into a caller-supplied buffer, respecting a millisecond deadline and returning the actual byte count received.

nodes.name: bt_cmd
nodes.summary: Flushes any pending RX data, transmits an HCI command packet, and then calls bt_read_event to capture the controller's response.

nodes.name: bt_download_firmware
nodes.summary: Downloads CYW43455 Bluetooth firmware by reading the binary image via fw_read_file and streaming it to the controller chunk-by-chunk using HCI vendor commands, then re-initialising after the chip resets.

nodes.name: bt_set_baud
nodes.summary: Sends the Broadcom vendor HCI baud-rate change command, waits for TX drain, then reconfigures the host PL011 or Pi 5 UART divisors to match, allowing step-up from 115200 to 3 Mbaud.

nodes.name: bt_remote_name
nodes.summary: Sends an HCI Remote Name Request for a given BD address and reads the asynchronous event response, printing the returned device name.

nodes.name: bt_inquiry
nodes.summary: Performs a general Bluetooth inquiry via HCI_Inquiry, collects Inquiry Result events for a fixed window, records discovered device addresses and class-of-device fields, and fetches remote names.

nodes.name: bt_write_file
nodes.summary: Persists a raw byte buffer to a Phoenix filesystem path using filecore primitives, creating or updating the file as needed.

nodes.name: bt_load_keys
nodes.summary: Loads persisted Bluetooth link keys from the filesystem into the in-memory pairing table using fw_read_file.

nodes.name: bt_uart_probe
nodes.summary: Exported Pi 4 Bluetooth probe: powers on the chip via mailbox, initialises the PL011, sends HCI Reset, downloads firmware, steps up to 3 Mbaud, re-initialises the UART, and loads stored link keys.

nodes.name: bt_scan
nodes.summary: Exported convenience wrapper that runs a Bluetooth device inquiry and returns the number of devices found.

nodes.name: bt_pair
nodes.summary: Exported Bluetooth SSP pairing sequence for a discovered device: sends HCI Write Simple Pairing commands, handles PIN/passkey exchange events, responds to user-confirmation requests, and saves the resulting link key to flash.

nodes.name: bt_connect
nodes.summary: Exported function that opens a Classic Bluetooth ACL connection to a previously paired device, handling Connection Complete and Authentication events including re-authentication retries.

nodes.name: bt_read_any
nodes.summary: Reads an ACL or HCI event packet of unknown type by first reading the packet-type indicator byte, then dispatching to the appropriate length-prefixed read loop.

nodes.name: bt_acl_send
nodes.summary: Constructs and transmits an ACL data packet with a 4-byte HCI ACL header and a 4-byte L2CAP header onto the UART stream.

nodes.name: bt_acl_open
nodes.summary: Opens an authenticated or unauthenticated ACL connection by sending an HCI Create Connection command and waiting for the Connection Complete event.

nodes.name: bt_l2cap_open
nodes.summary: Exported function that opens an L2CAP channel by performing the full Connection Request/Response and Configuration Request/Response signalling exchange over the ACL link.

nodes.name: bt_sdp_class
nodes.summary: Queries a remote SDP server for service records matching a given service class UUID, parsing and printing each returned attribute list.

nodes.name: bt_sdp_search
nodes.summary: Performs a complete SDP ServiceSearchAttribute transaction by opening an L2CAP SDP channel and iterating bt_sdp_class over a set of well-known service class UUIDs.

nodes.name: bt_l2cap
nodes.summary: Exported function that connects an ACL link to a discovered device and opens L2CAP SDP channel, triggering an SDP browse of available services.

nodes.name: bt_hid
nodes.summary: Exported function that connects a Bluetooth HID device by opening an ACL connection followed by two L2CAP channels (HID control and HID interrupt PSMs), then sends a GET_REPORT request.

nodes.name: bt_hid_poll
nodes.summary: Exported poll function that reads incoming ACL data from the HID interrupt channel and injects keyboard or mouse HID reports into the Phoenix input layer via hid_inject_keyboard_report and hid_inject_mouse_report_src.

nodes.name: bthw_swi
nodes.summary: Exported SWI 0x5A000 handler for the BTUart-phoenix provider module, dispatching sub-function codes for raw ACL write, ACL read, HID keyboard inject, key save, and scan operations.

nodes.name: bthw_register
nodes.summary: Exported entry point that registers the BTUart hardware module with the Phoenix native module system via module_register_native.

nodes.name: keyboard_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the keyboard event ring buffer and internal state, resetting head/tail indices.

nodes.name: keyboard_event
nodes.summary: Enqueues a raw keyboard event structure into the ring buffer, advancing the write pointer with wrap-around.

nodes.name: keyboard_poll
nodes.summary: Dequeues the next keyboard event from the ring buffer into a caller-supplied structure, returning 0 if the queue is empty.

nodes.name: keyboard_inject_char
nodes.summary: Synthesises a key-down event for a given ASCII character and injects it into the keyboard event queue via keyboard_event.

nodes.name: serial_kbd_poll
nodes.summary: Polls the debug UART for incoming PS2-style escape sequences and ASCII characters, converting them to keyboard events and injecting them into the queue.

nodes.name: mouse_inject_move
nodes.summary: Translates a raw delta (dx, dy) and button mask into an absolute mouse position clamped to screen bounds, then enqueues a mouse event via mouse_event.

nodes.name: mouse_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the mouse event ring buffer, zeroes position and button state, and logs the init to debug output.

nodes.name: mouse_set_bounds
nodes.summary: Sets the screen width and height clamping limits used by mouse_inject_move, called when the display resolution changes.

nodes.name: mouse_event
nodes.summary: Enqueues a mouse event structure into the mouse ring buffer with position clamping, and records absolute X/Y/button state for synchronous queries.

nodes.name: mouse_poll
nodes.summary: Dequeues the next mouse event from the ring buffer, returning 0 if the queue is empty.

nodes.name: mouse_get_pos
nodes.summary: Returns the current absolute mouse X and Y position via output pointer arguments.

nodes.name: mouse_get_buttons
nodes.summary: Returns the current mouse button bitmask (select/menu/adjust).

nodes.name: rp1_gem_phy_reset
nodes.summary: Resets the Ethernet PHY on Pi 5 by toggling the RP1 pad GPIO used as PHY reset, with microsecond-level delays to meet the PHY's power-on timing.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_phy_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the Ethernet PHY by reading OUI/device ID, enabling auto-negotiation for 1000BASE-T/100BASE-TX, waiting for link-up and speed negotiation to complete, then reporting the final link speed via con_printf.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_rings_init
nodes.summary: Allocates and initialises TX and RX DMA descriptor rings, programs the GEM MAC with the board MAC address from the VC mailbox, sets DMA burst size and buffer size registers, enables the MAC, and waits for the DMA engine to become active.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_send
nodes.summary: Exported TX path: copies a frame into the next free TX descriptor slot, writes the descriptor word to trigger DMA, and polls the used flag until the MAC confirms transmission.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_poll_rx
nodes.summary: Exported polled RX path: checks the current RX descriptor's ownership bit, copies the received frame out, recycles the descriptor, and returns the frame length.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_rx_available
nodes.summary: Exported predicate that returns non-zero if the next RX descriptor has been filled by the DMA engine.

nodes.name: rp1_gem_probe
nodes.summary: Exported probe that ioremaps the RP1 GEM MMIO region, reads and prints the hardware version register, then sequences rp1_gem_phy_init and rp1_gem_rings_init to fully bring up the Ethernet interface.

nodes.name: arp.c
nodes.summary: Implements the ARP protocol — maintains an IP-to-MAC resolution table, sends ARP requests, and handles incoming ARP packets. Provides both non-blocking cache lookup and a blocking poll-loop variant that waits for a reply within a timeout.

nodes.name: dhcp.c
nodes.summary: Full DHCP client implementing the DISCOVER/OFFER/REQUEST/ACK state machine, lease renewal (T1/T2 timers via dhcp_tick), gratuitous ARP on bind, and accessors for the negotiated IP, gateway, netmask, and DNS. Also registers the Ifconfig SWI provider module.

nodes.name: ipv4.c
nodes.summary: IPv4 packet handler: validates and demultiplexes incoming packets to ICMP, TCP, or UDP; computes IP checksums; provides ipv4_output for transmitting frames; and implements icmp_echo (ping) using blocking ARP resolution.

nodes.name: net.h
nodes.summary: Shared header defining core network structures (ethernet frame, IPv4 header, ARP table entries, UDP/TCP socket-like descriptors) and function prototypes used across the entire TCP/IP stack.
nodes.languageNotes: Central header for the net/ subsystem; nearly every .c file in this directory includes it.

nodes.name: ntp.c
nodes.summary: NTP client that sends a UDP query to a time server on port 123, polls for a reply with a hardware-counter timeout, and converts the NTP timestamp to a RISC OS centisecond value. Also provides net_poll_all which drives receive polling for all attached Ethernet interfaces.

nodes.name: tcpip.c
nodes.summary: TCP/IP stack initialisation hub: calls init functions for ARP, IPv4, IPv6, TCP, and UDP; and implements net_rx_frame which demultiplexes Ethernet frames (by EtherType) to the correct layer-3 handler.

nodes.name: udp.c
nodes.summary: UDP socket layer: parses incoming UDP datagrams and enqueues them in per-port ring buffers (udp_rx_enqueue), provides a blocking udp_recvfrom, and implements udp_send with ARP-backed next-hop resolution via IPv4 output.

nodes.name: resolver_module.c
nodes.summary: RISC OS-style module providing DNS A-record resolution SWIs: builds DNS query packets (build_dns_query), sends them over UDP and parses responses (parse_dns_response), and exposes resolver_module_swi for SWI dispatch.

nodes.name: arp_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the ARP table and internal state at stack startup.

nodes.name: table_update
nodes.summary: Inserts or refreshes an IP→MAC mapping in the ARP table, evicting the oldest entry when the table is full.

nodes.name: arp_resolve
nodes.summary: Non-blocking ARP cache lookup; returns true and fills mac_out if the IP is already cached, false otherwise.

nodes.name: arp_send_request
nodes.summary: Builds and transmits an ARP WHO-HAS broadcast request for the given target IP.

nodes.name: arp_resolve_blocking
nodes.summary: Blocking ARP resolution that first checks the cache, sends a request if not found, then polls net_poll_all in a loop until a reply arrives or timeout_ms expires.

nodes.name: send_reply
nodes.summary: Builds and transmits an ARP IS-AT reply in response to a request targeting our IP address.

nodes.name: arp_input
nodes.summary: Processes an incoming ARP packet: updates the table for any sender mapping and sends a reply if the request targets our IP.

nodes.name: dhcp_set_send
nodes.summary: Registers the send callback function pointer used by the DHCP client to transmit Ethernet frames.

nodes.name: dhcp_set_target
nodes.summary: Sets the network interface (nif) that the DHCP client will bind to.

nodes.name: _dhcp_make
nodes.summary: Constructs a DHCP message (DISCOVER, REQUEST, or RENEW) into a caller-supplied buffer, filling in options and computing the UDP/IP checksum.

nodes.name: _send_grat_arp
nodes.summary: Sends a gratuitous ARP announcement after the DHCP lease is accepted to claim the assigned address on the LAN.

nodes.name: dhcp_init
nodes.summary: Initialises DHCP client state with the hardware MAC address and clears all lease fields.

nodes.name: dhcp_start
nodes.summary: Transmits the initial DHCPDISCOVER and advances the client state machine to SELECTING.

nodes.name: dhcp_tick
nodes.summary: Periodic timer tick that drives lease renewal (T1/T2) and retransmit logic; called from the main polling loop with the current millisecond timestamp.

nodes.name: dhcp_rx
nodes.summary: Parses all incoming DHCP server messages (OFFER, ACK, NAK), validates the transaction ID and options, drives the SELECTING→REQUESTING→BOUND state transitions, and stores the negotiated lease parameters.

nodes.name: dhcp_bound
nodes.summary: Returns true when the DHCP client has successfully negotiated a lease and the interface is bound.

nodes.name: dhcp_get_ip
nodes.summary: Accessor that copies the DHCP-assigned IP address into the caller's buffer.

nodes.name: dhcp_get_gateway
nodes.summary: Accessor that returns the default gateway IP negotiated via DHCP, used by UDP and ICMP for next-hop routing.

nodes.name: dhcp_get_netmask
nodes.summary: Accessor that copies the DHCP-assigned subnet mask into the caller's buffer.

nodes.name: dhcp_get_dns
nodes.summary: Accessor that returns the DNS server IP address provided by the DHCP server.

nodes.name: dhcp_get_lease_secs
nodes.summary: Returns the lease duration in seconds as negotiated with the DHCP server.

nodes.name: dhcp_module_init
nodes.summary: Module entry point: waits for Ethernet link, initialises DHCP, polls until BOUND, then sets the interface configuration and returns; called once at boot.

nodes.name: dhcp_module_final
nodes.summary: Module finalisation stub: logs teardown and clears the bound flag.

nodes.name: ifconfig_swi
nodes.summary: SWI handler for the Ifconfig module (SWI base 0x5F000): services sub-function calls for reading the assigned IP, gateway, netmask, DNS, and lease duration into caller registers.

nodes.name: ifconfig_register
nodes.summary: Registers the Ifconfig SWI module with the Phoenix kernel's native module system.

nodes.name: ip_checksum
nodes.summary: Computes the one's-complement Internet checksum over a byte buffer of given length.

nodes.name: icmp_input
nodes.summary: Handles incoming ICMP packets: validates the checksum and responds to ECHO_REQUEST messages by constructing and sending an ECHO_REPLY in-place.

nodes.name: ipv4_init
nodes.summary: Initialises IPv4 layer state at stack startup.

nodes.name: ipv4_input
nodes.summary: Entry point for received IPv4 packets: strips the IP header and dispatches to the appropriate transport handler (ICMP, TCP, or UDP) based on the protocol field.

nodes.name: icmp_echo
nodes.summary: Sends an ICMP ECHO_REQUEST (ping) to dst_ip with blocking ARP resolution for the next hop, polls for an ECHO_REPLY within timeout_ms, and returns the round-trip time.

nodes.name: ipv4_output
nodes.summary: Constructs and transmits an IPv4 packet: fills the IP header, computes the checksum, selects the correct output interface, and calls the Ethernet send function.

nodes.name: net_poll_all
nodes.summary: Polls all attached network interfaces (genet, rp1_gem, WiFi) for received frames and feeds each one into net_rx_frame; used by blocking operations to keep the stack alive while waiting.

nodes.name: ntp_query
nodes.summary: Sends an NTPv4 request over UDP to server_ip:123 and polls for a reply, extracting the transmit timestamp into out_secs/out_frac; respects a millisecond timeout using the hardware counter.

nodes.name: ntp_to_riscos_cs
nodes.summary: Converts an NTP timestamp (seconds + fraction since 1900) to RISC OS centiseconds since 1900 for the OS clock.

nodes.name: tcpip_init
nodes.summary: Bootstraps the entire TCP/IP stack by calling arp_init, ipv4_init, ipv6_init, tcp_init, and udp_init in order.

nodes.name: net_rx_frame
nodes.summary: Ethernet frame demultiplexer: reads the EtherType field and dispatches to arp_input, ipv4_input, or ipv6_input accordingly.

nodes.name: udp_init
nodes.summary: Initialises UDP receive ring buffers and per-port state at stack startup.

nodes.name: udp_rx_enqueue
nodes.summary: Enqueues a received UDP datagram into the ring buffer for the destination port, copying the payload and recording the source IP/port; drops if buffer is full.

nodes.name: udp_rx
nodes.summary: Parses the UDP header from an incoming frame and calls udp_rx_enqueue to store the payload for the destination port.

nodes.name: udp_recvfrom
nodes.summary: Dequeues one UDP datagram received on local_port into buf, returning the source address; returns 0 if no data is waiting.

nodes.name: udp_send
nodes.summary: Transmits a UDP datagram: resolves the destination (or gateway) MAC via blocking ARP, builds the UDP header, and passes the frame to ipv4_output for transmission.

nodes.name: res_putip
nodes.summary: Formats a 4-byte IP address as a dotted-decimal string and writes it to UART for debug output.

nodes.name: parse_dotted_decimal
nodes.summary: Parses a dotted-decimal IP address string (e.g. '192.168.1.1') into a 4-byte array; returns false if the string is malformed.

nodes.name: build_dns_query
nodes.summary: Encodes a DNS A-record query for the given hostname into a wire-format packet buffer, inserting the transaction ID and label-encoded question section.

nodes.name: parse_dns_response
nodes.summary: Parses a DNS response packet: validates the transaction ID and flags, follows pointer-compressed labels in the answer section, and extracts the first A record's IPv4 address.

nodes.name: resolver_module_init
nodes.summary: Module init: performs a self-test DNS lookup and logs the result to UART.

nodes.name: resolver_module_final
nodes.summary: Module finalisation stub for the DNS resolver module.

nodes.name: resolver_module_swi
nodes.summary: SWI dispatch handler for the Resolver module: routes SWI sub-function calls to resolver_gethostbyname and returns the resolved IP in caller registers.

nodes.name: resources.c
nodes.summary: RISC OS ResourceFS port that loads module-embedded file blobs and mounts them into a virtual in-memory filesystem, making fonts, templates, and messages accessible via standard file paths.

nodes.name: sound.c
nodes.summary: RISC OS-style sound subsystem implementing Sound SWIs (Configure, Volume, beep) with beep generation routed to HDMI/GPU audio via hdmi_audio_beep, registered as a native kernel module.

nodes.name: fs_call.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 assembly veneer that marshals the RISC OS FileSwitch FS-entry calling contract, loading seven registers from an array, clearing NZCV before the BLR, and capturing the V flag on return to signal errors.
nodes.languageNotes: The msr nzcv, xzr before BLR is load-bearing: without it, an inherited V flag from the caller causes the callee to appear to fail even when it succeeds — an intermittent failure that only manifests when the caller's flags happen to be dirty.

nodes.name: sysvars_code.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 assembly veneers for RISC OS code variables, adapting the SystemVars register contract (x2=pw, x1:x2 out) to the C ABI for time/date/year read and providing a read-only write stub that returns an error.
nodes.languageNotes: The SystemVars code-variable contract is unique in this kernel: x2 carries the private word (not x12), and the return is three values (error, pointer, length) that do not fit AAPCS64's scalar return — hence the register shuffle macro.

nodes.name: testfs.c
nodes.summary: Minimal in-memory test filing system (named Test:) that implements the FileSwitch entry-point contract using disc-reader block I/O, plus a comprehensive self-test suite exercising open/close/read/stat/directory-enumeration paths.

nodes.name: testfs_veneer.S
nodes.summary: AArch64 assembly entry-point veneers for the Test: filing system, bridging the RISC OS FileSwitch register contract (x0–x6 in/out, V=error) to the C functions in testfs.c via a stack-spill/reload/V-flag pattern.
nodes.languageNotes: V is built bit-explicitly rather than via cmp+msr to avoid cmp clobbering the flags that msr would then write — a correctness subtlety shared with vec_call.S and documented inline.

nodes.name: graf_prims.c
nodes.summary: Low-level graphics primitives layer providing clipped point/line/hline/rect drawing, OS_Plot dispatch, ColourTrans SWI handling, and GPU-accelerated VideoV rectangle/triangle fills, all registered as native kernel modules.

nodes.name: graf_prims.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring graphics context types, colour-operation enums, OS-unit/pixel coordinate macros, and all public function prototypes for the Phoenix graphics primitives layer.

nodes.name: dr_init.c
nodes.summary: DiscReader module initialisation and block-level disc abstraction: wraps the FileCore ADFS disc structures (boot block, map, directories) and exposes object-level load/save/find/create/resize operations used by testfs and filecore.

nodes.name: resources_register
nodes.summary: Locates each module's embedded resource blob, builds the in-memory ResourceFS node tree with 4-byte-aligned entries, and registers the complete tree via swi_dispatch into the running ResourceFS.

nodes.name: sound_swi
nodes.summary: Dispatches Sound SWI calls by offset, handling Sound_Configure (sample rate/buffer/channels), Sound_Volume, and Sound_QSchedule (beep scheduling) with HDMI audio output.

nodes.name: sound_register
nodes.summary: Registers the sound subsystem as a native kernel module, binding sound_swi as the SWI handler and publishing SWI names.

nodes.name: sound_report
nodes.summary: Prints current sound configuration (sample rate, buffer depth, volume level, channel count, HDMI N/CTS parameters) to the console for diagnostics.

nodes.name: fs_entry_call
nodes.summary: Calls a filing system entry point with the RISC OS FS contract: loads x0–x6 from a register array, sets x12=private_word, clears NZCV, BLRs the routine, captures V, and writes updated registers back.

nodes.name: sysvar_time_read
nodes.summary: Read veneer for the Time code variable, calling sysvar_build(0) and shuffling the result into the SystemVars x1:x2 out contract.

nodes.name: sysvar_date_read
nodes.summary: Read veneer for the Date code variable, calling sysvar_build(1) and shuffling the result into the SystemVars x1:x2 out contract.

nodes.name: sysvar_year_read
nodes.summary: Read veneer for the Year code variable, calling sysvar_build(2) and shuffling the result into the SystemVars x1:x2 out contract.

nodes.name: sysvar_ro_write
nodes.summary: Write veneer shared by all read-only code variables; always returns an error via sysvar_write_readonly to prevent silent no-op writes.

nodes.name: testfs_open
nodes.summary: FileSwitch Open entry: resolves a path via filecore_dr_find_path, allocates a file handle, loads the object header via dr_load_object, and returns the file's permissions and extent.

nodes.name: testfs_get
nodes.summary: FileSwitch GetBytes entry: reads data bytes from the open file handle using the loaded block data.

nodes.name: testfs_close
nodes.summary: FileSwitch Close entry: frees the file handle and its associated buffer.

nodes.name: testfs_file
nodes.summary: FileSwitch File entry: handles file stat (ReadInfo) and load operations, resolving paths via filecore and loading object data via the disc reader.

nodes.name: testfs_func
nodes.summary: FileSwitch Func entry: implements directory enumeration (ReadDirEntries) and CSD/path operations using filecore_get_child_entry to iterate directory contents.

nodes.name: testfs_register
nodes.summary: Registers the Test: filing system with FileSwitch via fs_control, populating an FSInfoBlock with the veneer entry points.

nodes.name: testfs_selftest
nodes.summary: Comprehensive self-test suite for the Test: filing system, exercising open/close/stat/read/getbytes/dirents paths through FileSwitch and verifying results against expected values.

nodes.name: tf_read_via_testfs
nodes.summary: Test helper that opens a file, reads it in chunks via fs_gbpb, then closes it, returning bytes read for assertion.

nodes.name: testfs_open_veneer
nodes.summary: AArch64 FS-entry veneer for testfs_open: spills x0–x6 to a stack array, calls testfs_open, reloads the registers, and sets V from the C return value.

nodes.name: testfs_get_veneer
nodes.summary: AArch64 FS-entry veneer for testfs_get: spills x0–x6 to a stack array, calls testfs_get, reloads the registers, and sets V from the C return value.

nodes.name: testfs_close_veneer
nodes.summary: AArch64 FS-entry veneer for testfs_close: spills x0–x6 to a stack array, calls testfs_close, reloads the registers, and sets V from the C return value.

nodes.name: testfs_file_veneer
nodes.summary: AArch64 FS-entry veneer for testfs_file: spills x0–x6 to a stack array, calls testfs_file, reloads the registers, and sets V from the C return value.

nodes.name: testfs_func_veneer
nodes.summary: AArch64 FS-entry veneer for testfs_func: spills x0–x6 to a stack array, calls testfs_func, reloads the registers, and sets V from the C return value.

nodes.name: phoenix_prim_hline
nodes.summary: Draws a horizontal pixel span from x1 to x2 at screen-Y using fb_hspan, converting OS colour-op to a pixel value.

nodes.name: phoenix_prim_point
nodes.summary: Plots a single pixel at (x,y) in screen coordinates using fb_set_pixel with the resolved colour-op pixel value.

nodes.name: phoenix_gcx_init
nodes.summary: Initialises a graphics context with default clipping bounds, pixel-resolution primitives, and the current framebuffer dimensions.

nodes.name: phoenix_videov_rect
nodes.summary: Fills a pixel-space rectangle using the VideoV hardware vector if available, falling back to CPU span rendering if not.

nodes.name: phoenix_videov_tri
nodes.summary: Fills a pixel-space triangle using the VideoV hardware vector for GPU-accelerated rasterisation.

nodes.name: phoenix_gcol_exchange
nodes.summary: Sets the foreground and background colour-op from GCOL action and colour-number values, updating the graphics context.

nodes.name: plot_line_px
nodes.summary: Bresenham-style line drawing in pixel coordinates, plotting each pixel via phoenix_prim_point.

nodes.name: phoenix_os_plot
nodes.summary: Implements OS_Plot: converts OS-unit coordinates to pixels, dispatches to point/line/triangle/rectangle primitives based on plot code, and updates the graphics cursor.

nodes.name: plot_selftest
nodes.summary: Self-test for the plot primitives: invokes ColourTrans and OS_Plot operations and checks the VideoV availability path.

nodes.name: colourtrans_swi
nodes.summary: Implements the ColourTrans SWI set: converts OS 24-bit colours to pixel values, maps colour numbers, and calls font_set_colours for anti-aliased text rendering.

nodes.name: colourtrans_register
nodes.summary: Registers the ColourTrans module as a native kernel module, binding colourtrans_swi as the SWI handler.

nodes.name: grafctx_swi
nodes.summary: Handles GrafCtx SWIs for graphics context allocation and initialisation.

nodes.name: grafctx_register
nodes.summary: Registers the GrafCtx module as a native kernel module, binding grafctx_swi as the SWI handler.

nodes.name: dr_init
nodes.summary: Initialises the DiscReader layer for a block device at an LBA base: calls FileCore Initialise, reads the boot block and allocation map, and caches disc parameters.

nodes.name: dr_load_object
nodes.summary: Loads a disc object (file data) identified by SIN into a caller-supplied buffer via FileCore LoadObject.

nodes.name: dr_save_object
nodes.summary: Saves a buffer as a disc object identified by SIN via FileCore SaveObject.

nodes.name: dr_dir_checkbyte
nodes.summary: Computes the ADFS directory check byte by rotating and XORing all entry bytes, matching the FileCore on-disc format for directory integrity.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the classic ADFS big-directory check-byte algorithm: rotate-by-13 XOR chain over the directory header and entries.

nodes.name: dr_update_entry_len
nodes.summary: Updates a directory entry's load/exec/length fields in-place: loads the directory sector, locates the named entry, patches the fields, recomputes the check byte, and saves the directory back to disc.

nodes.name: dr_create_file
nodes.summary: Creates a new file in a disc directory: allocates sectors via FileCore map, adds a directory entry, computes the check byte, and saves both the updated directory and the new empty file object.

nodes.name: dr_read_disc_name
nodes.summary: Reads the ADFS disc name from the map sectors, using CalcMapLocation to find the relevant sector and extracting the name string.

nodes.name: dr_find_in_dir
nodes.summary: Searches an ADFS directory (identified by SIN) for a named entry, returning the entry's SIN, size, and directory flag if found.

nodes.name: dr_object_size
nodes.summary: Returns the byte size of a disc object by querying the FileCore allocation map for the sectors used by the SIN.

nodes.name: dr_shutdown
nodes.summary: Tears down the DiscReader layer, freeing all cached disc structures (boot block, map, directory buffers) allocated during dr_init.

nodes.name: DrawFile
nodes.summary: Clean-room Phoenix reimplementation of the RISC OS DrawFile module. Walks Draw file object lists, rendering path objects via Draw_Fill/Draw_Stroke, text objects via Font_Paint, and recursing into groups, while computing accurate bounding boxes from object geometry rather than the file header.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the RISC OS relocatable module pattern: CMHG-generated entry stubs call SWI_Render/SWI_BBox/SWI_DeclareFonts. All Draw file reads are done byte-wise via rd32() to tolerate unaligned buffers.

nodes.name: DrawFile.h
nodes.summary: Draw file format constants and field offsets for the DrawFile Phoenix module. Defines all object type codes, byte offsets into path/text/font-table/group objects, colour constants, and the Draw_Fill/Draw_Stroke winding-rule flags, verified against a real Draw file rather than documentation alone.

nodes.name: DrawFileHdr
nodes.summary: CMHG module header for the DrawFile Phoenix module. Declares the module title, help string, init/finalisation entry points, SWI chunk base &45540, and the SWI decode table mapping DrawFile_Render/BBox/DeclareFonts onto their C handlers.
nodes.languageNotes: CMHG (C Module Header Generator) is a RISC OS tool that generates the assembler module entry stubs from a structured declaration file, bridging the OS module protocol to C entry points.

nodes.name: VersionNum
nodes.summary: RISC OS-style version number and date definitions for the DrawFile Phoenix module (version 0.01, 03 Aug 2026). Provides preprocessor macros consumed by the CMHG header to populate the module help string.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS AMU-compatible Makefile building the DrawFile Phoenix module from the CMHG header object and the C implementation, using the shared CModule template and the riscos64-amu Docker toolchain.

nodes.name: render_path
nodes.summary: Renders one Draw path object by invoking Draw_Fill for the fill colour and Draw_Stroke for the outline colour as two independent passes, correctly handling the even-odd vs non-zero winding rule from the style word.

nodes.name: fonts_load
nodes.summary: Parses a Draw font-table object, calls Font_FindFont for each entry, and stores the resulting handles in the module-global font table for use by subsequent text-object rendering within the same diagram.

nodes.name: render_text
nodes.summary: Renders one Draw text object by looking up the font handle from the module font table, setting colours via ColourTrans_SetFontColours, and plotting the NUL-terminated string at the baseline position via Font_Paint.

nodes.name: walk
nodes.summary: Recursively walks the Draw object list, dispatching path objects to render_path, font-table objects to fonts_load, text objects to render_text, and group objects to a deeper walk call, with a depth cap of 16 to prevent stack overflow on malformed files.

nodes.name: bbox_walk
nodes.summary: Recursively walks the Draw object list to compute the true bounding box from object geometry, skipping options and font-table objects whose bounding box words carry non-geometric data.

nodes.name: SWI_Render
nodes.summary: DrawFile_Render SWI handler. Validates the diagram pointer and magic number, resets the font table, walks the object list to render all paths and text, then resets fonts again before returning.

nodes.name: SWI_BBox
nodes.summary: DrawFile_BBox SWI handler. Validates the diagram, computes the bounding box from object geometry via bbox_walk, and falls back to the header's declared box if the file contains no renderable geometry.

nodes.name: SWI_DeclareFonts
nodes.summary: DrawFile_DeclareFonts SWI handler stub. Returns success immediately since text rendering does not yet pre-declare font usage to the font manager.

nodes.name: DrawFile_Command
nodes.summary: Star-command handler for *DrawRender. Parses a filename from the command line, loads the file into a heap block via OS_File/OS_Module, invokes SWI_Render, and frees the block.

nodes.name: DrawFile_Init
nodes.summary: Module initialisation entry point. Prints a startup banner to confirm successful loading; no other initialisation is required.

nodes.name: DrawFile_Final
nodes.summary: Module finalisation entry point. No resources to release; returns success unconditionally.

nodes.name: WimpDemo
nodes.summary: RISC OS relocatable module implementing the WimpDemo commands (*WimpDemo, *WimpDemoRun, *WimpTemplate, *WimpDemoQ) to exercise the Phoenix Wimp window manager through SWIs — the first disc-loaded module to drive the Phoenix desktop end-to-end.
nodes.languageNotes: CMunge 64-bit AArch64 module; avoids pointer arrays in .data.rel.ro (the #167 bug) by using 2D char arrays for string tables throughout.

nodes.name: WimpDemo.h
nodes.summary: Header defining Wimp SWI numbers, icon flag constants, 32-bit block helper inlines, and static inline SWI wrappers for Wimp_Initialise, Wimp_CreateWindow, Wimp_OpenWindow, Wimp_CreateIcon, Wimp_Poll, and Wimp_CloseDown, handling AArch64 intptr_t pointer-passing and the RISC OS block-layout contract.
nodes.languageNotes: Block fields are written with wblk_set/wblk_get rather than struct casts to avoid LP64 struct-sizing hazards (OSLib wimp_icon_data is 24 bytes under LP64 where the API demands 12).

nodes.name: WimpDemoHdr
nodes.summary: CMunge 64-bit module header declaring WimpDemo's title, help string, initialisation/finalisation entry points, and four-command keyword table (*WimpDemo, *WimpDemoRun, *WimpTemplate, *WimpDemoQ).
nodes.languageNotes: CMunge passes this file through cpp, so apostrophes and character literals must be avoided in comments and strings.

nodes.name: VersionNum

nodes.name: README-PHOENIX.md
nodes.summary: Development log and architecture notes for WimpDemo: explains why the module proves the Phoenix Wimp architecture is sound, documents the build and run procedure, records boot169/170 test results, and captures the #167 pointer-table relocation bug the test exposed.

nodes.name: HIDDemo
nodes.summary: RISC OS relocatable module implementing *MouseTest, *KeyTest, and *VideoVTest commands that exercise the Phoenix USB HID keyboard/mouse class driver and the VideoV vector chain through OS SWIs, with detailed inline commentary on the boot171 SWI-flood lesson and the boot198 OS_ReadC blocking trap.
nodes.languageNotes: Avoids pointer arrays (the #167 lesson) and deliberately uses OS_Byte 129 INKEY instead of OS_ReadC for non-blocking key polling after #187 made OS_ReadC block.

nodes.name: HIDDemo.h
nodes.summary: Header defining OS input SWI numbers, mouse button bit constants (MB_ADJUST, MB_MENU, MB_SELECT), and static inline wrappers for OS_Mouse and OS_Byte-129 non-blocking key polling used by HIDDemo.
nodes.languageNotes: OS_ReadC is intentionally absent — left undefined rather than unused so no future reader reaches for it after the #192 audit found the same blocking trap in WimpDemo.

nodes.name: HIDDemoHdr
nodes.summary: CMunge 64-bit module header declaring HIDDemo's title, help string, initialisation/finalisation entry points, and three-command keyword table (*MouseTest, *KeyTest, *VideoVTest).

nodes.name: VersionNum

nodes.summary: Constructs an 88-byte Wimp_CreateWindow parameter block by hand in little-endian byte layout, setting visible area, scroll offsets, window flags, title, colour bytes, and work extent.

nodes.name: build_icon
nodes.summary: Constructs a 36-byte Wimp_CreateIcon parameter block by hand, encoding window handle, bounding box, flags, and inline text for a text icon.

nodes.name: do_demo
nodes.summary: Exercises the full Wimp setup sequence: Wimp_Initialise, Wimp_CreateWindow, Wimp_OpenWindow, three Wimp_CreateIcon calls, and one Wimp_Poll — the proof-of-concept that a disc-loaded module can drive the Phoenix Wimp end-to-end.

nodes.summary: Runs a paced Wimp poll loop that decodes and reports Mouse_Click, Open/Close_Window_Request, Redraw_Window_Request, and Key_Pressed events until ESC is pressed or the 30,000-spin limit is reached.

nodes.name: do_template
nodes.summary: Exercises the Wimp template delegation chain by calling Wimp_OpenTemplate, Wimp_LoadTemplate (reporting the loaded window visible area), and Wimp_CloseTemplate — which Phoenix forwards to the resident WimpTemplates module.

nodes.summary: Calls Wimp_CloseDown on the stored task handle to cleanly shut down the WimpDemo Wimp task and zero the module-global state.

nodes.name: do_keytest

nodes.summary: Issues OS_CallAVector with VideoV (0x2C) in R9 and the given reason code in R8, forwarding a graphicscontext_t pointer in R7; returns 1 on success and prints any error.

nodes.name: do_videovtest
nodes.summary: Exercises the VideoV vector chain from C: obtains a GrafCtx (kernel framebuffer primitives), then calls Graf_ChangeBase, Graf_ReadPrimitives, and Graf_Rectangle through OS_CallAVector to verify the full VideoSW round-trip.

nodes.summary: Module initialisation entry point called by *RMLoad; prints the HIDDemo load banner.

nodes.summary: SWI wrapper for OS_Mouse (0x1C) returning current pointer coordinates, button bitmask, and millisecond timestamp.

nodes.name: BoardInfo
nodes.summary: RISC OS provider module (SWI chunk 0x5C000) that decodes the Raspberry Pi board revision code into model, SoC, RAM and prints it as *BoardInfo. Serves as the module's Init/Final/Command entry points and uses VideoCore mailbox data cached by the kernel.

nodes.name: BoardInfo.h
nodes.summary: ABI header defining board_info_buf_t (the shared buffer layout for the BoardInfo_GetInfo SWI at 0x5C000) and the inline boardinfo_getinfo() wrapper that zeroes the buffer and issues the SWI.
nodes.languageNotes: Buffer fields are ordered u64-first then u32s then bytes to remain naturally aligned with no padding in both Norcroft and gcc. The comment explicitly warns against reordering.

nodes.name: Makefile

nodes.name: HALInfo
nodes.summary: RISC OS provider module (SWI chunk 0x5D000) that reports Device Tree-discovered hardware layout — CPU count, RAM, peripheral base, GIC addresses, and the PCIe slot occupant — via *HALInfo. Includes a VID:DID lookup to identify whether the PCIe slot holds a VL805 USB hub or an NVMe drive.

nodes.name: HALInfo.h
nodes.summary: ABI header defining hal_info_buf_t (the shared buffer for the HALInfo_GetInfo SWI at 0x5D000) and the inline halinfo_getinfo() wrapper that zeroes the buffer and issues the SWI.
nodes.languageNotes: Fields ordered u64-first to match the kernel's hal_info_buf_t in devicetree.c byte-for-byte; pcie_id encodes VID in [15:0] and DID in [31:16].

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS AMU Makefile that builds the HALInfo provider as a 64-bit CModule, linking the CMHG-generated header object (HALInfoHdr) with the C implementation.

nodes.name: DiscInfo
nodes.summary: RISC OS provider module (SWI chunk 0x5E000) that queries the kernel's FileCore multi-disc registry and prints a formatted table of disc names, media types, block sizes, and capacities via *Discs.

nodes.name: DiscInfo.h
nodes.summary: ABI header defining disc_info_buf_t and media class constants for the DiscInfo SWIs (0x5E000 count, 0x5E001 get), with inline wrappers discinfo_count() and discinfo_get() that invoke the kernel's FileCore registry.
nodes.languageNotes: Exposes two SWI entry points (DiscInfo_Count / DiscInfo_GetDisc) unlike the single-SWI BoardInfo and HALInfo, reflecting the iterable nature of the disc list.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS AMU Makefile that builds the DiscInfo provider as a 64-bit CModule, linking the CMHG-generated header object (DiscInfoHdr) with the C implementation.

nodes.summary: RISC OS module finalisation entry point; no-op cleanup for this module.

nodes.summary: Fetches the HAL info buffer via halinfo_getinfo() and prints Device Tree validity, Pi model, CPU count, RAM map, peripheral/UART/GIC base addresses, and PCIe slot occupant identification.

nodes.name: HALInfo_Init
nodes.summary: RISC OS module initialisation entry point; prints a version banner on load.

nodes.name: HALInfo_Final
nodes.summary: RISC OS module finalisation entry point; no-op cleanup for this module.

nodes.summary: RISC OS module finalisation entry point; no-op cleanup for this module.

nodes.summary: RISC OS module command dispatch entry point; routes *Discs (cmd_no 0) to do_discs().

nodes.name: WiFiCtl
nodes.summary: Phoenix RISC OS WiFi control-plane module implementing the *WiFiStatus command. Dispatches the WiFiCtl SWI (chunk 0x5B000) via the kernel provider to print association state, SSID, IP, and MAC address.

nodes.name: WiFiCtl.h
nodes.summary: ABI header for the Phoenix WiFiCtl SWI provider (chunk 0x5B000). Defines the wifi_info_t flat struct and the wifictl_getinfo() static inline SWI wrapper that zero-fills before calling to prevent uninitialised-buffer exploits.
nodes.languageNotes: Buffer is zero-filled before the SWI so a missing/failing provider returns zeros rather than stack noise — a defensive pattern repeated across all Phoenix provider headers.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS CModule build configuration for WiFiCtl. Compiles the CMHG header object (WiFiCtlHdr) and WiFiCtl.c into a loadable module using the shared CModule include rule.

nodes.name: XHCIInfo
nodes.summary: Phoenix RISC OS USB host controller info module implementing the *USBInfo command. Queries xHCI controller state, port PORTSC values, and live HID report counters over the XHCI SWI provider (chunk 0x80000) — the report counters enable liveness verification on Pi 5 where serial output drops under load.
nodes.languageNotes: Separate show_controller/do_usbinfo split separates enumeration from presentation, allowing per-controller error propagation without a top-level error check after each print.

nodes.name: XHCIInfo.h
nodes.summary: ABI header for the Phoenix XHCI SWI provider (chunk 0x80000). Defines three naturally-aligned C structs (xhci_ctrl_buf_t, xhci_port_buf_t, xhci_hid_buf_t) plus static inline SWI wrappers that zero buffers before calling to guard against uninitialised-data leaks from a missing provider.
nodes.languageNotes: Struct layouts are deliberately not packed — natural alignment under both gcc (kernel) and Norcroft (module) keeps the byte-identical ABI requirement. Pointers passed as (intptr_t) to avoid 32-bit truncation on AArch64.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS CModule build configuration for XHCIInfo. Compiles the CMHG header object and XHCIInfo.c into a loadable module using the shared CModule include rule.

nodes.name: Ifconfig
nodes.summary: Phoenix RISC OS network interface listing module implementing the *Ifconfig command. Queries all network interfaces (wired GENET + CYW43455 WiFi) over the kernel Ifconfig provider (chunk 0x5F000), printing name, state, IP, MAC, netmask, and gateway.

nodes.name: Ifconfig.h
nodes.summary: ABI header for the Phoenix Ifconfig SWI provider (chunk 0x5F000). Defines the ifcfg_buf_t all-byte struct and static inline SWI wrappers for counting and retrieving interface records from the kernel TCP/IP stack.
nodes.languageNotes: All fields are bytes (no struct padding under any compiler), matching the byte-for-byte layout required with ifcfg_buf_t in net/dhcp.c.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: RISC OS CModule build configuration for Ifconfig. Compiles the CMHG header object and Ifconfig.c into a loadable module using the shared CModule include rule.

nodes.name: BTHW.h
nodes.summary: Hardware interface header for the Phoenix Bluetooth UART driver (CYW43455 BT over PL011). Defines seven SWI constants (chunk 0x5A000) for Tx, receive, timing, HID injection, live-HID handoff, and link-key persistence, plus safe static inline wrappers that handle SWI failure by returning fail-fast values rather than undefined register contents.
nodes.languageNotes: Each SWI wrapper's comment documents the specific failure mode it defends against (e.g., hw_readany returns 0 on error so the H4 parser never reads an uninitialised buffer; hw_time returns 0 so expired timeouts fail immediately). This is the ABI boundary between the kernel BT bring-up and the BTUart host-stack module.

nodes.name: do_status

nodes.name: WIMP_PORT_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Feasibility and phased plan for porting the RISC OS Wimp from ARM assembly to C as a native kernel-linked module, covering dependency gates, architecture decisions, and boot-test milestones.

nodes.name: WIMP_SPEC.md
nodes.summary: Phase 0 specification for the Wimp port extracted from Wimp 5.64 ARM source, classifying all 62 SWIs as keep/stub/drop, defining Phase-1 SWI contracts, CreateWindow block layout, and internal workspace structures to redesign.

nodes.name: BUILDING_A_MODULE.md
nodes.summary: Step-by-step developer guide for building a 64-bit Phoenix module from third-party C source, covering RISC OS directory layout, MakefileBuild64, ResourceFS resource block generation, relocation checking, and module header verification.
nodes.languageNotes: Covers CMunge 0.84 limitations for 64-bit runnable modules and the custom resgen64.py toolchain.

nodes.name: GOTCHAS.md
nodes.summary: Extensive living catalogue of Phoenix/RISC OS development pitfalls with 95 numbered entries spanning diagnostics methodology, LP64 pointer/struct traps, AArch64 ABI differences, hardware/HAL quirks, and build environment issues.
nodes.languageNotes: Covers LP64 struct-aliasing padding bugs (section 7c), 64-bit sentinel value truncation (section 4s), and RISC OS directory-separator dot convention (section 4i).

nodes.name: APP_LAUNCH_CHAIN.md
nodes.summary: Describes the RISC OS !Boot/!Run/!Sprites application launch chain and identifies what Phoenix must still provide (ResourceFS subtree, Choices convention, resolution-variant sprites) before desktop applications can launch correctly.

nodes.name: CMOS_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Documents how Phoenix emulates RISC OS CMOS RAM persistence on Raspberry Pi using a file-backed RamFS image, covering the address-order file layout, measured facts from the CMOS binary, and all implementation steps including the completed write-back (proven on hardware 2026-08-29).

nodes.name: HAL_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Phased plan for a Device-Tree-driven Hardware Abstraction Layer that enables a single Phoenix binary to boot on Pi 4, CM4, Pi 5, and CM5, with a quirk registry for board-specific behaviour and a BCM2711-vs-BCM2712 differences checklist.

nodes.name: INTKEY_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Plan for integrating the RISC OS IntKey keyboard layout module into Phoenix, covering the USB-HID to RISC OS internal-key-number bridge that is currently missing, licence decisions, and acceptance criteria.

nodes.name: RESOURCEFS_PORT_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Detailed 64-bit port specification for ResourceFS covering the registration block format produced by resgen64.py, FSInfoBlock, the five FS entry points, service calls, and the critical finding that Phoenix's path resolution has no filing-system prefix concept.
nodes.languageNotes: Identifies that FileSwitch canonicalises paths before the FS sees them, and documents the three-branch Resources: tree structure ($.Resources, $.Apps, $.Sprites).

nodes.name: RTC_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Real-time clock implementation plan and diary for Phoenix, documenting the discovery that the Pi uses a firmware mailbox tag (not a hardware RTC chip), the time-format conversion derivation, and the completed OS_Word 14 / Service_RTCSynchronised integration proven on hardware (2026-08-30).

nodes.name: SD_BCM2712_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Plan and findings for enabling the SD card slot on BCM2712 (Pi 5 / CM5), including device-tree base addresses, quirks from SDIODriver, and the confirmation that Phoenix's existing SD driver works unmodified on first try (2026-08-29).

nodes.name: MODULAR_ARCHITECTURE.md
nodes.summary: Architecture design document defining Phoenix's lean-core + runtime-loadable module split, the provider/client mechanism, single-binary board selection, kernel-module ABI versioning contract, and failure modes that must be defined before modules ship.

nodes.name: MODULE_ADOPTION_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Prioritised batched plan for adopting RISC OS 64 modules into Phoenix, documenting boot-log findings from the first hardware drop-in tests and categorising modules by infrastructure readiness (Batches A through E).

nodes.name: MULTICORE_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Detailed multi-core (SMP) design for Phoenix choosing asymmetric compute offload (lane A) over true SMP, with staged milestones from single-core groundwork through four-core IPI round-trips, and the one-binary board-difference matrix for Pi 4 and Pi 5.

nodes.name: EXC_IRQ_STACK_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Design plan (task #126) for giving exc_irq_handler a safe dedicated stack in Phoenix, comparing in-handler stack switching (Approach A, recommended) against a full SP_EL0/SP_EL1 split (Approach B, deferred), with staged implementation steps.

nodes.name: VECTOR_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Version 4 software-vector design document for Phoenix covering the RO64 claimant convention (as confirmed by Charles), the dispatch algorithm, the full SWI API to implement (OS_AddToVector, OS_RemoveFromVector, etc.), and the UserV proof-of-concept path.
nodes.languageNotes: Distinguishes SVC-context versus IRQ-context vector dispatch, a key AArch64 concern absent in 32-bit RISC OS.

nodes.name: LICENSE_AUDIT.md

nodes.name: Development Journal

Host-side test harnesses (tools/hosttest/): framebuffer, VDU, FilerUtils, descriptor, haspalette, messagefile, readunsigned, redirect, tile, VDU, fsprefix, fscall. edges.description: Path-based pairing (deterministic)
xHCI driver depends on PCIe RC + VL805 initialization in pci.c
VL805 xHCI development encompassed the multi-boot ERSTBA cache investigation
xHCI driver development culminated in the event ring fix at boot 143
xHCI driver depends on the DMA buffer layout for ring pointers and context memory
xHCI driver implements the USB enumeration stack (Enable Slot, Address Device, GET_DESCRIPTOR)
USB mass storage depends on the enumeration stack to identify and address the NVMe device
USB mass storage (RTL9210 NVMe bridge) is the block device backing FileCore/ADFS disc access
FileCore/ADFS provides disc access for loading RISC OS module binaries (.ffa files)
Module Init() calls RISC OS SWIs — requires SWI dispatch infrastructure to be in place first
AArch64 RISC OS modules use riscos64-clib for their C runtime (_clib_initialisemodule)
CursorModule is a key kernel-linked AArch64 RISC OS module in the module system
The module system registers ARM32 modules as stubs pending AArch32 EL0 mode switching
GENETv5 driver is the hardware layer underlying the Phoenix network stack
The event ring fix at boot 143 was enabled by analysing Circle's xHCI driver object files
SWI dispatch provides OS services that modules call during Init() and operation
The ERSTBA cache problem led to relocating ERST to physical address 0 and changing DMA_OFFSET to 0
Rules 1-50+ document VL805/xHCI-specific hardware behaviour and correct sequences
Rules 47-57 document GENET, RGMII, ARP, and network driver best practices
Rules 118-120 document SDIO SlowArasan controller addressing and bus power requirements
DWC2 EP0 control transfer pattern informed xHCI GET_DESCRIPTOR fix
WIMP task polls GENET RX ring and drives the network receive path every 4ms tick
WIMP desktop uses CursorModule for mouse pointer rendering and input management
Boot 35 (controller running), boot 118 (DWC2 device), boot 143 (event ring) are xHCI milestones
Boot 314 (first frames on wire) and boot 340 (reliable ping) are GENET milestones
usb_bdev_read calls bot_recover on transfer failure then retries
usb_mass_storage_init registers usb_storage_probe as the class driver probe callback
usb_mass_storage.c depends on blockdriver.h for blockdev_t/blockdev_register and xhci functions via extern declarations
usb_mass_storage_init indirectly configures the blockdev ops table containing usb_bdev_read
Paired blockdev read/write ops on the same storage drive
timer_tick and timer_irq_handler are both timer firing paths; timer_irq_handler is the GIC ISR, timer_tick is the software callback walker
